It says a second-instance judgment in a property case cannot be appealed if the benefit from appealing would not exceed 8,000 yuan.","points":[{"text":"The constitutional right to bring a lawsuit means people can sue when their rights are harmed, and courts must judge cases according to law.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Constitution does not say how many court levels a case must pass through. The law may set this reasonably according to the type of case, so not every case needs the same number of levels.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The 8,000 yuan limit is part of a litigation system that applies equally to all parties and helps settle disputes. It is hard to say it interferes with the right to sue.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Whether the rule should be changed later is a question for the legislature to weigh, and it does not make the rule unconstitutional.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The court concluded the rule does not conflict with Articles 1, 16 and 23 of the Constitution.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Parties in property-rights civil cases","Parties appealing second-instance judgments","Legislators"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether supplementary budgets (追加預算) count toward the total budget when applying the Constitution's minimum share for education, science and culture spending in cities and counties. The court decided they do not count. The 35 percent figure is measured against the total budget as drawn up at the start.","held":"The 35 percent minimum in Article 164 of the Constitution refers to the share of total annual expenditure when the budget is drawn up. Supplementary budgets are not included in that total.","points":[{"text":"The question was whether a supplementary budget is part of the total budget for the education, science and culture minimum.","cites":["1"]},{"text":"Article 164 sets the minimum at 35 percent of the total budget in cities and counties, and this refers to the share of total expenditure at the time the budget is compiled.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"A supplementary budget can only be proposed when budget execution runs into a situation listed in Article 53 of the Budget Act, so it arises later and is separate from the original budget.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"For that reason, supplementary budgets are not included in the total budget used for the 35 percent calculation.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["City and county governments","Education, science and culture programs"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是憲法第一百六十四條規定教育、科學、文化經費的比例時，所稱「預算總額」是否包括特別預算。大法官會議認為，預算總額是指政府編製年度總預算時所列的歲出總額，不包括因緊急或重大情事而提出的特別預算。","held":"憲法第一百六十四條所稱「預算總額」，指編製年度總預算時所列之歲出總額，不包括因緊急或重大情事而提出的特別預算。","points":[{"text":"憲法第一百六十四條的「預算總額」，是指各級政府為平常施政而編製年度總預算時所列的歲出總額。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"年度總預算由政府每一會計年度就歲入、歲出全部彙總編成，且每一會計年度只辦理一次。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"特別預算只有具備預算法第七十五條所列各款情事之一，才能在年度總預算之外提出。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"特別預算是因應緊急或重大情事而特別編製，所以不包括在預算總額之內。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["中央、省、市、縣各級政府","教育、科學、文化經費相關機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案兩位聲請人分別因竊盜案件與性騷擾防治法案件，在第二審被改判有罪後，因刑事訴訟法第376條第1款、第2款而不能上訴第三審，因此聲請解釋憲法。憲法法庭認為，第一審已判有罪、第二審維持或改判有罪者不得上訴第三審，屬立法形成範圍，並未違憲。但第二審撤銷無罪判決並自為有罪判決者，被告不得上訴第三審，沒有提供至少一次上訴救濟機會，違反憲法第16條保障訴訟權的意旨。","held":"刑事訴訟法第376條第1款及第2款中，就第二審撤銷無罪判決並自為有罪判決而不得上訴第三審的部分，自解釋公布之日起失效；第一審判有罪後第二審維持或改判有罪而不得上訴的部分，則尚無違憲。","points":[{"text":"憲法第16條保障訴訟權，核心內容包括人民權利受侵害時能請求法院及時有效救濟；初次受有罪判決者，至少應有一次上訴救濟的機會。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"至於審級、程序及要件，則由立法機關衡量案件種類、性質、訴訟政策與司法資源等因素決定是否限制。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"系爭規定旨在減輕法官負擔、讓法官專注處理較重大繁雜的案件；第一審已判有罪者，已有上訴審法院審判的機會，故不許第三審上訴屬立法形成範圍，尚不違憲。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"第二審撤銷無罪判決並改判有罪者，初次受有罪判決即告確定，無法以通常程序上訴尋求救濟。","cites":["10"]},{"text":"再審與非常上訴要件嚴格、門檻高，不足以替代通常的上訴救濟，因此這項上訴機會不是立法機關可裁量限制的審級設計問題，該部分違憲而失效。","cites":["10"]},{"text":"對尚在上訴期間內或已上訴未裁判的案件，解釋文另作處理：被告可依法上訴，原第二審法院應裁定曉示10日內提出第三審上訴，已上訴者法院不得依系爭規定駁回。","cites":["11","3"]}],"who":["第二審撤銷無罪判決並改判有罪的被告","得為被告利益上訴之人","第一審判有罪、第二審維持或改判有罪的被告","本案兩位聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是審查軍事審判法的相關規定，是否讓現役軍人在軍事審判後得不到足夠的救濟，也不合司法獨立的要求。大法官認為，平時經終審軍事審判機關宣告有期徒刑以上的案件，應允許被告直接向普通法院以判決違背法令為理由請求救濟。相關規定與憲法意旨不符，至遲於本解釋公布屆滿二年時失效。","held":"軍事審判法第十一條、第一百三十三條第一項與第三項、第一百五十八條，以及其他不許被告逕向普通法院請求救濟的部分，與憲法意旨不符，自解釋公布之日起至遲二年後失效；有關機關須在期限內修正相關法律並調整審級制度。","points":[{"text":"憲法保障人民身體自由與訴訟權，現役軍人也是人民，同受保障。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"憲法第九條是因現役軍人負有保衛國家的特別義務，才允許對其犯罪設軍事審判，並非讓軍事審判機關專屬審判軍人犯罪、排除普通法院審判。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"軍事審判行使的是國家刑罰權，必須符合正當法律程序的最低要求，包括獨立、公正的審判機關與程序，且不得違背憲法第七十七條、第八十條的司法權建制原理。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"限制軍人權利的軍事審判程序法律，也應遵守憲法第二十三條的比例原則。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"基於保障人身自由、訴訟權與第七十七條意旨，平時經終審軍事審判機關宣告有期徒刑以上的案件，應許被告逕向普通法院請求救濟。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"第十一條使軍事機關完全掌理審判，有違權力分立；第一百三十三條的核可權、覆議權與第一百五十八條須經軍事長官核定審判庭組成，使行政權介入審判。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["現役軍人","被軍事審判判處有期徒刑以上的被告","軍事審判機關與軍法官","負責修法的有關機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案先處理一個程序問題：法官在裁判中引用了行政機關或司法行政機關的命令時，當事人可否聲請大法官解釋。大法官認為可以，因此受理本案。就實體部分，大法官認為前司法行政部要求法院拍賣關稅記帳進口貨物時，須載明未繳關稅並由買受人繳清後才點交的函示，沒有違憲。","held":"法官不受行政命令或司法行政命令中的法律見解拘束，但命令經法官在裁判中引用，當事人即可聲請解釋；前司法行政部有關拍賣關稅記帳進口貨物的兩則函示，未侵害動產抵押權人權益，與憲法保障財產權的本旨並無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"法官依據法律獨立審判，對各機關的釋示命令可以引用，但可表示不同見解，不受拘束。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"司法行政機關的命令不影響審判權的行使，所提示的法律見解只供法官參考，不能命令法官適用。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"命令一經法官在裁判上引用，當事人即可依司法院大法官會議法的規定聲請解釋，所以本件聲請應予受理。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"依關稅法第三十一條第二項、第三項，關稅未繳清的進口貨物，不得轉讓，經強制執行或專案核准者，才可由受讓人繼續分期繳稅或記帳；因此抵押權的擔保利益不能存在於該貨物未繳的關稅上。","cites":["3","5"]},{"text":"因強制執行而受讓貨物者，如未獲准繼續分期繳稅或記帳，須繳清稅款才可取得貨物，這與第五十五條第三項所指的情形不同。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"兩則函示與關稅法上述規定意旨相符，未侵害動產抵押權人的權益，也是確保關稅稽徵所必要，所以不違反憲法保障財產權的本旨。","cites":["3","5"]}],"who":["審判案件的法官","聲請解釋的當事人","動產抵押權人","拍賣關稅記帳進口貨物的買受人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是：以共同犯罪的意思，參與犯罪構成要件以外的行為，或事先同謀而由部分人實行犯罪，是否也算共同正犯。大法官認為這些情形都是共同正犯，並指出先前三號解釋雖用語不同，旨趣一致。","held":"以自己共同犯罪的意思，參與實施犯罪構成要件以外的行為，或以自己共同犯罪的意思事先同謀、由其中一部分人實施犯罪行為者，都是共同正犯。院字第一九０五號、第二０三０號之一、第二二０二號前段解釋，旨趣一致。","points":[{"text":"共同正犯是在共同意思範圍內，各自分擔犯罪行為的一部分，互相利用他人的行為來達成犯罪目的。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"共同正犯的成立，不要求全體都參與實施犯罪構成要件的行為。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"以自己共同犯罪的意思參與構成要件以外的行為，或事前同謀而由部分人實行者，也應認為共同正犯，並對全部行為所生結果負責。","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"院字第一九０五號、第二０三０號之一、第二二０二號前段解釋所述情形，如事前同謀後得贓、同謀並把風、以自己犯罪意思參與實施，都屬共同正犯的範圍。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"這三號解釋因聲請內容不同而用語有異，但旨趣並無二致。","cites":["3","2"]}],"who":["共同犯罪的參與者","事前同謀者","負責把風等參與構成要件以外行為者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Taiwan's Fair Trade Act rules punishing improper multi-level marketing, and a related regulation, violate the Constitution. The court held that the Act's ban and its criminal penalty are constitutional, but that Article 5 of the Multi-level Marketing Management Measures went beyond what the law authorized and must not be applied.","held":"Article 23(1) and Article 35 of the old Fair Trade Act are constitutional: they are clear enough and do not violate the protection of personal freedom and property. Article 5 of the Management Measures exceeded the delegated authority, breached the legal reservation principle, and is not to be applied.","points":[{"text":"Criminal punishment of socially harmful conduct is permitted if clearly defined by law and consistent with Article 23 of the Constitution, and vague-sounding legal terms are acceptable if their meaning can be understood and foreseen and courts can apply them.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Multi-level marketing where participants earn mainly from recruiting others, not from the reasonable market price of goods or services, is improper. It drives ever more recruiting, leaves later joiners with losses, and gives organizers big profits, harming the market and economic stability, so banning it and punishing it with up to three years' imprisonment or fines serves a legitimate purpose and is not excessive.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The terms 'mainly' and 'reasonable market price' are determined by where participants' income comes from and the price of the goods or services, so their scope is determinable. Because the company plans the scheme, its operators can foresee violations, and courts can review them, so the rule is clear enough.","cites":["2","7"]},{"text":"The Fair Trade Commission's interpretation on 'mainly' was consistent with the Act, but its view that a company with a compliant return policy can be treated as having a 'reasonable market price' when no comparable goods exist did not match the Act's intent.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Restrictions on people's rights must be set by law, and any delegation to regulations must be specific in purpose, content and scope. Contract freedom is protected by the Constitution.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Article 5 of the Management Measures gave participants rights to cancel or end contracts at will and required the company to take back goods, refund money and buy back goods, changing Civil Code rules. This concerns rights and duties on leaving a scheme, goes beyond mere administrative management, and exceeds the delegated authority.","cites":["3","9"]}],"who":["Multi-level marketing companies and their operators","Multi-level marketing participants","The Fair Trade Commission"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在釐清先前院字第二０三三號解釋中「多數人」一詞的意思。大法官表示，多數人也包括特定的多數人，至於人數要多少，要看立法意旨和實際情形是否已達到公然的程度。","held":"院字第二０三三號解釋所稱多數人，包括特定之多數人在內；其人數應視立法意旨及實際情形已否達於公然之程度而定，並對該解釋予以補充釋明。","points":[{"text":"先前解釋認為「公然」只要有不特定人或多數人得以共見共聞的狀況即可，不必實際上真的被共見共聞，但事實上必須有得以共見共聞的狀況。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"從先前解釋及當時聲請解釋的原呈來看，多數人明確包括特定的多數人。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"各罪成立的要件不同、罪質也不同，所以特定多數人的計算，要看立法意旨及實際情形是否已達公然的程度。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["適用刑法分則「公然」規定的人","涉及公然要件的案件當事人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Thirty-eight legislators challenged Taiwan's 2017 civil servant pension reform law, which cut retirees' pension income, raised contribution rates and stopped pensions for some retirees who take private school jobs. The court upheld nearly all of the cuts and the higher contributions, but struck down the rule suspending pensions for retirees re-employed at private schools. It also told the authorities to make later adjustments and to revise the rule on inflation adjustment.","held":"Most challenged provisions (higher contributions, minimum guarantee, pension cuts, preferential-deposit interest cuts) are not unconstitutional. Article 77(1)(3) violates equal protection and loses effect on the day of the ruling. The request for a provisional order is rejected.","points":[{"text":"The higher contribution rate applies only going forward, so it is not retroactive. It reasonably serves the important goal of extending the life of the pension fund, which has been under-funded and is running at a deficit.","cites":["80","83","84","85"]},{"text":"The minimum guarantee protects retirees' basic living, and retirees whose original pay was already below it are not cut. Not topping up their pay does not violate the right to survival.","cites":["88","89","90"]},{"text":"The cuts apply the new law to pension relationships that are still continuing, so they are not retroactive.","cites":["94","95"]},{"text":"The cuts do not reach the retirees' own contributions and touch only the government-funded part, so the court reviewed them leniently. The important public goals outweigh retirees' reliance, and the phase-in periods, floors and exemptions soften the impact.","cites":["97","98","110","122","124"]},{"text":"Authorities must adjust the cuts at the first periodic review if the reform goal is reached early, and must amend the rule so pensions are adjusted when consumer prices rise by a set percentage.","cites":["125","130","132"]},{"text":"Suspending pensions of those re-employed at private schools fails the strict equal-protection test. It covers too broadly, since not all private schools get government subsidies. It also covers too narrowly, since it ignores other subsidized private bodies and lump-sum pensions.","cites":["135","138","139","140","141"]}],"who":["Retired civil servants receiving pensions","Serving civil servants paying into the pension fund","Retirees re-employed at private schools","Survivors receiving survivor pensions"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Taiwan's irrigation association organization rules, which say who pays water-handling fees and small channel upkeep costs, are unconstitutional. The court held they are not, because the rules only confirm a long-standing custom. It said the fees among small irrigation group members are private-law matters, so disputes go to civil court.","held":"The relevant provisions of the irrigation association rules do not conflict with the constitutional protection of property. Fees and upkeep costs among small group members follow private-law principles, and disputes over them go through civil litigation.","points":[{"text":"Irrigation associations are public-law legal persons whose members are by law the landholders and beneficiaries in their area. They are comparable to local self-governing bodies and have self-rule within what the law authorizes.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The rules on members' rights and duties and on the association's organization and staffing serve the public interest and fit the law's authorization, so they do not conflict with constitutional property protection or the limits on restricting rights.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"By long custom, small irrigation groups manage water distribution and channel upkeep themselves, by labor or money, and the members decide the amounts. So the fees among group members follow private-law principles, and disputes go to civil court.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"This differs from the fees, construction costs and usage charges the association collects from members, which are public-law burdens. That the association may collect the fees on behalf of groups, or subsidize them, does not change their nature.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The rule provisions making members bear the fees and upkeep costs only confirm that custom and do not alter its nature, so they do not conflict with property protection.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The court noted that, since the association is a public-law body and administrative litigation has been reformed, it should be reviewed whether to keep the private-law custom or make these fees public-law burdens set by statute. It also said a regional group-meeting guideline is not a law or order and cannot be reviewed.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Irrigation association members","Small irrigation group members","Irrigation associations"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Seven people were convicted of selling drugs under the Narcotics Hazard Prevention Act after courts relied on two old Supreme Court precedents. Those precedents said that buying drugs for profit was enough to complete the crime of selling. The Constitutional Court held that selling is complete only when the drugs have actually been sold, so the precedents are unconstitutional to that extent.","held":"The parts of the two precedents (25年非字第123號 and 67年台上字第2500號) that treat buying drugs for profit as a completed sale offense conflict with the constitutional principle that crimes and punishments must be set by law. They therefore violate Articles 8 and 15 of the Constitution; the offense under Article 4, paragraphs 1 to 4, requires that the act of selling be completed.","points":[{"text":"Criminal law touching life, liberty and property must follow the principle that crimes and punishments are fixed by law. Courts may not expand the elements of an offense or widen the range of punishable acts.","cites":["12"]},{"text":"By ordinary dictionary meaning, 'selling' (販賣) centers on selling out goods. It is not merely buying them.","cites":["14"]},{"text":"Article 4 puts selling in the same paragraphs, with the same penalties, as manufacturing and transporting drugs. Selling should therefore be read as selling out, which causes harm comparable to those acts.","cites":["15"]},{"text":"The same word in other articles, such as possession with intent to sell, would produce an unreasonable result if it meant only buying.","cites":["16"]},{"text":"The Act separates four offenses: completed selling, attempted selling, possession with intent to sell, and possession. Completed selling therefore means the sale has been carried out and does not cover mere purchase.","cites":["17"]},{"text":"The legislative history shows the lawmakers have distinguished these four offenses since 1955. They never intended mere buying to count as completed selling.","cites":["18","19"]},{"text":"The two precedents held that buying for profit is enough. To that extent they expand the offense and violate the principle of legality and Articles 8 and 15.","cites":["20","21"]}],"who":["People convicted of selling drugs on the basis of the two precedents","The seven petitioners","Courts applying the drug selling offense"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是寺廟登記規則中，募建寺廟逾期延不登記時可撤換住持或管理人的規定，是否違憲。大法官認為，就募建的寺廟而言，這項規定與監督寺廟條例第十一條的立法意旨相符，是保護寺廟財產、增進公共利益所必要，並未牴觸憲法保障人民財產權的本旨。","held":"寺廟登記規則第十一條撤換寺廟管理人的規定，就募建寺廟而言，與監督寺廟條例第十一條立法意旨相符，與憲法保障財產權之本旨並無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"監督寺廟條例規定寺廟財產及法物應呈請登記，並由住持管理；違反者，主管官署得革除其住持之職。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"管理者即使不是僧道、也未用住持名稱，只要實際對寺廟有管理權，依該條例立法意旨，仍適用革除規定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"內政部依法定職權訂定寺廟登記規則，其中規定逾期延不登記或新寺廟不聲請登記者，如無特殊理由，得撤換住持或管理人。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"就募建寺廟而言，此規定與條例立法意旨相符，是保護寺廟財產、增進公共利益所必要，因此不違反憲法保障財產權的本旨。","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"本解釋僅就募建寺廟而為，其他寺廟不在解釋範圍。","cites":["5"]}],"who":["募建寺廟的住持或管理人","募建寺廟","主管寺廟登記的官署"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A Taipei court judge asked the Constitutional Court whether two immigration-law provisions are constitutional. One bans charging or agreeing on a fee for matchmaking cross-border marriages, and the other fines people who do so. The court decided both provisions do not violate the Constitution.","held":"The ban on requiring or agreeing on payment for cross-border marriage matchmaking does not violate the constitutional protections of the right to work, freedom of contract, or equality. The fine of NT$200,000 to NT$1,000,000 for doing so does not violate the constitutional protection of property rights.","points":[{"text":"The ban limits the right to work of professional matchmakers and the freedom of contract of occasional matchmakers, but the state may limit these for legitimate public interests if the means reasonably relate to the goal.","cites":["6","7"]},{"text":"The purpose is legitimate: to protect the people marrying, prevent human trafficking, and avoid commodifying marriage and objectifying women, given differences between the parties and information gaps.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The means are reasonably related: the ban does not prohibit matchmaking itself or set qualifications, still allows non-profit matchmaking, and does not bar gifts freely given after success, while helping de-commercialize matchmaking and reduce abuses.","cites":["9","10"]},{"text":"On equality, the court used a lenient standard because the classification is not suspect and involves only commercial matters, not vital personal rights.","cites":["12","13"]},{"text":"Treating cross-border matchmaking worse than domestic matchmaking has a legitimate aim and a reasonable link, since the risks of information gaps, trafficking and pressure on the spouse who relocates are more pronounced.","cites":["14"]},{"text":"The fine range lets the authority weigh how serious the violation is, and general rules on reducing penalties can avoid overly harsh results even at the minimum, so property rights are not violated.","cites":["16","17"]}],"who":["Cross-border marriage matchmakers (businesses and individuals)","People seeking cross-border marriage matchmaking","Non-profit legal entities doing matchmaking","Occasional matchmakers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a 1996 Administrative Court resolution was constitutional. It said an expropriation stays valid even if the compensation was not paid within the legal time limit. The court decided that this view conflicts with the constitutional protection of property, so it must not be applied.","held":"Compensation for expropriated property must be reasonable and paid promptly. If the compensation is not paid within 15 days, or within a reasonable period in special cases, the expropriation approval loses effect. The Administrative Court's contrary resolution is not to be applied.","points":[{"text":"Article 15 of the Constitution protects property rights, so the state may expropriate property for public use or other public interest only with reasonable compensation.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Compensation is a special sacrifice made for the public interest, so it must cover the owner's loss. It must be adequate and also paid as quickly as possible.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Article 233 of the Land Act requires compensation within 15 days after the public notice ends. Even when an objection delays this, the amount must be passed on within the same 15-day limit once it is assessed.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The strict procedure aims to protect people's property while the state serves the public interest. If the owner refuses payment and the money is deposited, extra compensation ordered later that goes unpaid means the expropriation cannot be treated as unaffected.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Expropriation and compensation are inseparable. Article 235 of the Land Act ends the owner's rights only when compensation has been fully paid.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"If the extra amount is very large or there are special circumstances, payment must still be made promptly within a reasonable period after the assessment is final. Otherwise the expropriation approval loses effect.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Owners of expropriated property","Land-needing agencies","Land administration authorities","Administrative courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是立法委員聲請解釋，疑問包括副總統可否兼任行政院院長、新任總統就職時行政院院長辭職如何處理，以及立法院要求總統重新提名院長的決議有無拘束力。大法官認為副總統兼任院長並非顯然違憲，但與憲法使兩職位由不同人擔任的本旨未盡相符；院長的禮貌性辭職由總統裁量；立法院的決議對總統無拘束力。","held":"副總統兼任行政院院長憲法無明文規定，職務性質非顯不相容，但影響繼任或代行職權的設計，與憲法本旨未盡相符，應適當處理；院長禮貌性辭職如何處理屬總統裁量的統治行為，不作合憲性審查；立法院八十五年六月十一日的決議逾越職權，僅屬建議，對總統無拘束力。","points":[{"text":"副總統兼任院長的問題是兩個憲法職位能否兼任的法律問題，不是單純政治人事安排，所以大法官可以作實體解釋。","cites":["22"]},{"text":"憲法沒有明文禁止兼任，兼任也不明顯違反權力分立；副總統平時沒有具體職權，與院長之間沒有分工、制衡或利益衝突，職務性質並非顯不相容。","cites":["24","25","26"]},{"text":"過去的兼任先例有爭議，也曾有相反的例子，不能算已形成有規範效力的憲政慣例。","cites":["23"]},{"text":"兼任的瑕疵未達重大而明顯的程度，所以不能認定明顯違憲；但兼任遇到總統缺位或不能視事時，會出現三個職位集於一人，影響憲法的繼任與代行職權設計，與三個職位分由不同人擔任的本旨未盡相符。","cites":["28","30","31"]},{"text":"院長在新任總統就職時辭職是禮貌性辭職，不是憲法義務；核准、退回或慰留是總統的裁量，屬統治行為，不由大法官審查。","cites":["32"]},{"text":"向立法院負責的是行政院，立法院除憲法規定的事項外，不能決議要求總統做或不做某事；要求總統重新提名的決議等於創設憲法不採的不信任投票，逾越職權，僅屬建議。","cites":["33"]}],"who":["副總統與行政院院長","總統","立法院與立法委員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議是財政部函釋規定，非經都市計畫劃為道路預定地、而由私人設置的道路土地，不得用來抵繳遺產稅，是否違憲。大法官認為，遺產稅本應繳現金，只有現金繳納確有困難時才可用實物抵繳，且實物須易於變價。該函釋符合法律意旨，與憲法沒有牴觸。","held":"財政部七十一年十月四日函釋認為私人設置、未經都市計畫劃為道路預定地的既成道路土地不得抵繳遺產稅，是因其變價不易，符合法律意旨，與憲法尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"遺產稅本應以現金繳納，必須現金繳納確有困難，才可用實物抵繳。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"申請實物抵繳是否符合要件、實物是否適於抵繳，應由稅捐稽徵機關調查核定，納稅義務人不能任意指定實物。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"實物抵繳的目的是期待其變為現金，所以施行細則規定抵繳實物須易於變價或保管，且未設定他項權利。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"「易於變價」不能與「保管」擇一即可；若無法變價卻許抵繳，國家反增無意義的保管負擔，違反母法意旨。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"私人設置、非都市計畫道路預定地的道路土地，主管機關無徵收義務，屬不易出售變價之物，故不許抵繳。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"相關規定與函釋為貫徹稅法執行及培養誠實納稅風氣所必要；若全部實物都不易變價，能否抵繳須於調查核定時另行考量。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["遺產稅納稅義務人","稅捐稽徵機關","私設道路土地所有人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an Interior Ministry order was unconstitutional because it said that when a share of co-owned property is itself jointly owned by several people, the Land Act's majority-consent rule for disposing of co-owned property does not apply. The court held that transferring such a share can follow that rule, and that the ministry's point in its order added a limit the Land Act does not contain, so it must not be applied to that extent.","held":"A share in real estate that is jointly owned (公同共有) may be transferred under the Land Act Article 34-1, paragraph 5, applying paragraph 1. Point 12 of the Interior Ministry's 1988 enforcement guidelines adds a limit the Land Act lacks and so is not to be applied to that extent.","points":[{"text":"Co-ownership limits how each owner can use the property, which can hinder its use, disposal and free circulation and cause economic harm.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 34-1 of the Land Act aims to balance co-owners' interests while easing property transactions, resolving co-ownership disputes and promoting effective use for the public interest.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"A share is the co-owner's proportion of ownership and is no different in nature from ownership, so disposing of co-owned property by transfer means transferring ownership.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Allowing jointly owned shares to be transferred under paragraph 1 eases transactions, may reduce the number of owners or end the co-ownership, and so serves the law's purpose.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Transferring a jointly owned share ends the joint ownership of that share, which is different from converting joint ownership into separate co-ownership among the owners.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The Interior Ministry may issue orders only on minor, technical details of carrying out the law and cannot contradict it or add limits; Point 12 added such a limit on jointly owned property.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Joint owners of real estate","Co-owners of land or buildings","Interior Ministry and land administration officials"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a rule is constitutional that makes courts refuse to approve an adoption of a mainland Chinese person when the Taiwan adopter already has a child or adopted child. The court held that, as applied to someone adopting their spouse's mainland-resident child, the rule goes too far and is unconstitutional. That part stops having effect from the day the ruling was announced.","held":"The part of Article 65, item 1, of the Taiwan-Mainland relations statute that makes courts refuse to approve a Taiwan resident's adoption of their spouse's mainland child is inconsistent with the constitution's protection of the freedom to adopt (Article 22) and the proportionality principle (Article 23). It loses effect from the day of the ruling.","points":[{"text":"The freedom to adopt is protected by Article 22 because adoption is part of the family system and matters for the personal development of both adopter and adopted child.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The rule limits the freedom of Taiwan residents to adopt mainland residents, and the constitution allows special legislation on relations between the two sides.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Courts should respect the legislature on cross-strait matters unless there is an obvious serious flaw, but any limit on this freedom must still meet the proportionality principle.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The rule's aim of protecting Taiwan's security and social stability by avoiding population imbalance is legitimate, and the rule helps achieve it.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Adopting a spouse's mainland child supports marital happiness, family harmony and the child's development, yet the rule makes no exception for it.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"So the harm to this freedom is out of balance with the public interest protected, making the limit excessive.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["Taiwan residents who want to adopt a spouse's mainland child","Mainland-resident children of spouses of Taiwan residents","Taiwan residents who already have children or adopted children","Courts reviewing adoption applications"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是：不是為了修改憲法而召集的國民大會臨時會，能不能修改憲法。大法官認為，憲法修改影響重大，應讓國民預先知道修憲目的並有表達意見的機會，因此不是以修憲為目的召集的臨時會，不能行使修憲職權，並補充釋字第二十九號解釋。","held":"非以修改憲法為目的而召集的國民大會臨時會，不得行使修改憲法的職權；釋字第二十九號解釋因此予以補充。","points":[{"text":"憲法是國家根本大法，修改關係憲政秩序安定與國民福祉，應讓國民預知修改目的並有表達意見的機會。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"國民大會臨時會依不同情形及程序召集，釋字第二十九號解釋只針對依憲法第二十九條定期集會的職權，並非說臨時會不論原因與程序都能行使全部職權。","cites":["3","4"]},{"text":"讓國民知道修憲目的，也能使國民大會代表瞭解民意，使其行使職權符合國民的合理期待與信賴。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"過去的臨時條款與憲法增修條文，都是特別規定為修憲而召集臨時會，與上述意旨相符。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"修憲雖無集會前半年公告的規定，但若召集目的不是修憲，就不能在因其他事項召集的臨時會中規避召集程序限制而直接修憲。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"因此依憲法增修條文第十一條第一項、第二項及第十五條所召集的臨時會，不得行使修憲職權。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["國民大會及其代表","總統","全國國民"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案處理兩個問題:憲法上所說的「法官」是否包括檢察官,以及實任檢察官的身分保障是否與實任推事相同。大法官會議解釋,憲法第八十一條所稱的法官不包括檢察官;但實任檢察官的保障,除轉調外,與實任推事相同。","held":"憲法第八十一條所稱法官,是指同法第八十條的法官,不含檢察官。實任檢察官的保障依憲法第八十二條及法院組織法第四十條第二項,除轉調外,與實任推事相同。","points":[{"text":"憲法第八十一條所稱的法官,指的是憲法第八十條所規定的法官,因此不包含檢察官。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"實任檢察官的保障,依憲法第八十二條及法院組織法第四十條第二項的規定,與實任推事相同。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"但在轉調方面,實任檢察官的保障與實任推事不同,屬於例外。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["檢察官","實任檢察官","實任推事","法官"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case was about land expropriation compensation: whether a land authority could throw out its own announced land value and send it to a review committee when no one had objected, and how deadlines for paying compensation work. The court said the authority cannot do that when neither the land user nor the owner objected, and it set rules on the payment deadline, including after a committee re-evaluation.","held":"If neither the party needing the land nor the owner objects to the compensation amount, the land authority may not cancel the announced value and send it to the Standard Land Price Review Committee. The 15-day payment deadline still applies, with exceptions for a pending review or owner-approved extension, and after a committee decision payment must be made within a time limit of no more than 15 days.","points":[{"text":"Under the cited Land Act articles, the authority estimates compensation where no legal land value exists, and review by the committee happens only when someone objects. So with no objection, the authority has no power to cancel the announced value and send it for re-evaluation.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Under the earlier interpretation cited, approval of an expropriation lapses if payment is not made within 15 days of announcement. But if there was an objection and the matter was properly sent to the committee, or the owner agreed to a delay on record, the owner's interests are not harmed, so approval does not lapse.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The Land Act's payment deadline aims to prevent expropriation approvals from hanging unresolved and to reduce harm to owners and protect their private rights.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The law sets no deadline for paying a value re-evaluated by the committee, but for the same reasons the authority must promptly notify the land user and set a deadline for payment, which may not exceed 15 days.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["Land owners whose land is expropriated","Parties needing land for expropriation","Local land administration authorities","Standard land price review committees"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked when the time limit for asking to reopen a civil case starts if the court's final decision relied on a legal view that the Judicial Yuan later interpreted as contrary to the true meaning of the law. The court decided the time limit runs from the day that interpretation is announced. But if the civil judgment became final more than five years ago, a reopening based on an obvious error in applying the law is still not allowed.","held":"The deadline to file for a retrial based on such an interpretation counts from the day the interpretation is announced, following the proviso of Article 500, paragraph 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. However, civil judgments final for over five years still cannot be reopened for an obvious error in applying the law, under Article 500, paragraph 3, and Interpretation No. 188 is supplemented.","points":[{"text":"The Judicial Yuan has the power to interpret the constitution and unify the interpretation of laws and orders under Article 78 of the Constitution.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"If a final judgment's legal view is interpreted as contrary to the true meaning of the law, that interpretation can be used as a ground for retrial or extraordinary appeal, though not where the court's view was not an obvious error in applying the law.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Counting the filing deadline from the day the interpretation is announced is needed to protect people's rights.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"An error in applying the law is a flaw of the original final judgment, so civil judgments final for over five years cannot be reopened on that ground, which keeps the legal order stable.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Parties to civil cases with final judgments","Courts handling retrial requests"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是多位法官認為「公職人員年資併社團專職人員年資計發退離給與處理條例」的部分規定可能違憲，因而聲請釋憲。憲法法庭認為，該條例受審查的第2條第2款、第4條第1項、第5條第1項第1款與第2款及第7條規定，均尚無違背憲法，其餘聲請不受理。","held":"憲法法庭宣告系爭條例第2條第2款（平等原則）、第4條第1項與第5條第1項第1款、第2款（財產權、不溯及既往、信賴保護）及第7條（法安定性）均尚無違憲；其餘聲請不受理。","points":[{"text":"條例點名特定社團屬特殊類型法律，但目的是落實轉型正義、匡正黨國體制下的違法年資併計，分類與目的有實質關聯；救國團曾隸屬國防部也不影響違法併計的問題，故不違反平等原則。","cites":["66","67","68","70","71"]},{"text":"扣除社團年資並要求退職政務人員返還溢領給與，雖是真正溯及，但為特別重要的公共利益，不為憲法所當然不許；當年考試院函令欠缺法律依據、重大違法，受領人也無值得保護的信賴。","cites":["78","79","80","81"]},{"text":"受影響的退離給與屬恩給制，與公職人員在職時的給付無關，立法者有較大調整空間；手段與回復退休法制的目的有合理關聯，並設有每月至少2萬5千元的下限及分期繳納，故不違反財產權保障。","cites":["83","84","85","86","87"]},{"text":"社團本應以雇主身分負擔專職人員的退休金，卻藉違法函令轉嫁給國家，並取得人才等無形利益，因此要求社團返還與目的有合理關聯，無不當聯結。","cites":["92","94","95","96"]},{"text":"社團返還義務雖屬真正溯及，但為轉型正義的重大公益；社團也是違法制度的協力者，無值得保護的信賴，且不須加計利息，未逾越必要範圍。","cites":["97","98","99"]},{"text":"第7條排除權利行使期間的規定，是因我國漸進式民主轉型，不排除期間限制就難以實現轉型正義，有其必要，故不違反法安定性。","cites":["102","103","104"]}],"who":["退休（職、伍）公職人員","退職政務人員","條例所列特定社團（如國民黨、救國團）","曾任社團專職人員後轉任公職者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是行政機關科處罰鍰的公文書，能否作為強制執行的依據。大法官解釋指出，對人民財產強制執行，必須有強制執行法第四條所列的執行名義。罰鍰公文書只有在法律規定送由法院強制執行或得移送法院辦理時，才可視為執行名義。","held":"行政機關依法科處罰鍰的公文書，如法律定有送由法院強制執行或得移送法院辦理，可認為強制執行法第四條第六款的執行名義；否則不能直接據以強制執行。","points":[{"text":"對人民財產強制執行，必須有強制執行法第四條所列的執行名義才可進行。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"罰鍰公文書若法律定有送由法院強制執行或得移送法院辦理，就可認為是同法第四條第六款的執行名義。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"若法律沒有這類規定，罰鍰公文書不能直接作為強制執行的依據。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["受行政機關罰鍰處分的人民","科處罰鍰的行政機關","辦理強制執行的法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及土地經地籍重測後，發現與鄰地界址重疊而面積減少，之前依較大面積多繳的地價稅可否退稅。財政部早年函釋認為不適用稅捐稽徵法第二十八條退稅。大法官認為這種多繳屬於「因計算錯誤溢繳之稅款」，該部分函釋與解釋意旨不符，不再援用。","held":"財政部兩則函釋中，認為重測後因界址重疊面積減少者不適用稅捐稽徵法第二十八條退稅的部分，自解釋公布之日起不再援用；退稅至多追溯至最近五年已繳之地價稅。","points":[{"text":"地價稅以土地所有權人在同一直轄市或縣（市）的地價總額為基礎，並採累進稅率，面積愈多、地價愈高，稅負愈重。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"課徵地價稅應以正確的土地面積為課稅基礎，才符合實質課稅的公平原則。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"地籍重測結果與原登記面積有出入時，除非否定重測結果或確認作業有瑕疵，應以重測後變更登記的面積為準。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"重測發現界址重疊而面積減少，表示原據以核列的地價總額不正確；使人多負稅負者，屬於稅捐稽徵法第二十八條所稱「因計算錯誤溢繳之稅款」。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"財政部函釋認為面積增減不適用退稅，與上述意旨不符，故不再援用；退稅最多追溯最近五年，且本解釋只適用於地價稅的稽徵。","cites":["3","6"]}],"who":["繳納地價稅的土地所有權人","地籍重測後面積減少的土地所有權人","地價稅稽徵機關","地政機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑都市更新條例中，主管機關核准都市更新事業概要與核定事業計畫的程序是否保障人民的財產權與居住自由。憲法法庭認為，概要核准的程序、申請概要的同意比率（僅超過十分之一），以及事業計畫核定前的送達與聽證規定，都不符正當行政程序而違憲，相關機關須於一年內修正。但事業計畫的同意比率規定，以及災區部分建築物重建的特別規定，則未違憲。","held":"都市更新條例第十條第一項、第二項及舊第十九條第三項前段不符正當行政程序，有違憲法保障財產權與居住自由，須於公布日起一年內檢討修正，逾期該部分失效；第二十二條第一項的同意比率及第二十二條之一在限定範圍內，未違反比例原則。","points":[{"text":"都市更新核准概要與核定計畫，都是限制人民財產權與居住自由的行政處分，可能使人喪失權利、被迫遷離。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"因影響重大，法律應設置公平、專業、多元的審議組織，確保利害關係人知悉資訊並能陳述意見；核定事業計畫時還應公開舉辦聽證。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"概要核准的規定未要求設置適當審議組織，也未確保利害關係人知悉資訊，僅有公聽會不足以保障其陳述意見。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"申請概要只需超過十分之一同意，比率太低，少數人即可啟動程序，使多數人被迫參與，不符正當行政程序。","cites":["10"]},{"text":"事業計畫核定前未向其他所有權人分別送達資訊，也未辦理聽證、說明採納與否的理由，故違憲。","cites":["11"]},{"text":"事業計畫核定的同意比率均已過半，立法目的正當，未違反比例原則，但仍應隨時檢討；災區部分建築物重建的規定限於迅行劃定地區且不變更其他棟權利，亦合比例原則。","cites":["13","14"]}],"who":["更新單元內土地及合法建築物所有權人","申請都市更新的人與實施者","其他利害關係人與權利人","主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether people other than the original applicant, who each asked the court to review the same law before its ruling was published but whose requests were not handled together, are also covered by the ruling. The court decided they can be, as long as the court's justices decided that their requests met the legal requirements.","held":"If someone other than the original applicant asked for an interpretation of the same law before the ruling was published, and the justices decided the request met the legal requirements, that person's underlying case can also benefit from the earlier rule that an interpretation has effect on the applicant's own case. Interpretation No. 193 is supplemented accordingly.","points":[{"text":"Earlier Interpretation No. 177 says a ruling also has effect on the applicant's own case, so that applicants who benefit can seek relief through legal procedures.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Interpretation No. 193 already covered one applicant with several cases on the same law, even if the court did not handle them together.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Interpretation No. 193 did not clearly say what happens when different applicants raise the same question without their requests being combined, so a supplementary interpretation was needed.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To carry out the purpose of Nos. 177 and 193 and respect equal treatment, applicants who all applied before the ruling and met the legal requirements should not be treated differently.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The court noted that Administrative Litigation Act Article 273, paragraph 2 implements Nos. 177 and 185, so cases of different applicants that qualify can also seek a retrial under this ruling.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Original applicants whose requests were decided","Other applicants who asked about the same law before the ruling","People seeking a retrial in affected cases"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A person who retired in 1974 sued over his retirement pay, which was calculated without a \"professional allowance.\" He lost in the Supreme Court, which applied an administrative rule, and he asked whether that rule violated the Constitution and the civil servant retirement law. The court held that the rule had already been repealed before the events at issue, so no constitutional question arises.","held":"If a challenged order was already repealed when the matter in dispute arose, it no longer has effect. Even if a court relied on it, that only raises whether relief can be sought through court procedures, not a constitutional conflict.","points":[{"text":"The applicant challenged a Executive Yuan rule on pay adjustment for military, public and teaching staff, which the Supreme Court applied when ruling against him. He said it conflicted with the civil servant retirement law and Article 172 of the Constitution.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 172, which makes orders that conflict with the Constitution or laws void, covers only orders that are still in effect but whose content conflicts with them.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The Executive Yuan repealed the rule from July 1, 1973, and the Taiwan Provincial Government passed this on to its agencies, so it was repealed before the applicant retired.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"His retirement pay was also not calculated under that rule, as a forestry bureau reply confirms.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Because the rule had lost effect when the matter arose, a court's reliance on it only raises whether relief is available through court procedures, not a constitutional conflict.","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["Retired public employees","Courts that apply government orders","Government agencies issuing orders"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於行政院函釋對於有公用地役關係的既成道路，是否可以不予徵收補償。大法官認為，土地因公益而被特別犧牲，國家應依法徵收並給予補償；若經費困難，應訂定期限逐年辦理或以其他方法補償。行政院兩則函釋與此意旨不符的部分，不再援用。","held":"既成道路符合要件而成立公用地役關係者，國家應依法律徵收並補償，經費困難時應訂期限逐年辦理或以他法補償；行政院六十七年及六十九年兩函與此不符的部分，不再援用。","points":[{"text":"憲法保障人民財產權，國家因公益雖可徵收土地，但必須給予相當補償。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"個人因社會責任等限制而受特別犧牲、社會公眾因而受益時，應享有相當補償的權利。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"既成道路成立公用地役關係須具備三要件：為不特定公眾通行所必要、所有人起初未阻止、年代久遠而未中斷。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"所有權人對這類土地已無法自由使用收益，形成特別犧牲，國家應依法徵收補償；經費困難時，應訂定確實可行的期限逐年辦理，或以債券、抵稅、公有土地抵償等方式彌補。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"同一道路範圍內其他私有土地都徵收補償，卻只因有公用地役關係就以命令繼續使用而不補償，違反平等原則。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"道路因地理環境或人文狀況改變而喪失原有功能時，應隨時檢討並廢止；行政院兩函與上述意旨不符部分不再援用。","cites":["2","5"]}],"who":["既成道路土地的所有權人","各級政府及有關機關","通行道路的公眾"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及內政部發布的都市計畫樁測定及管理辦法，其中規定經上級政府再行複測決定後，不得再提異議。大法官認為這項規定會限制人民提起訴願及行政訴訟的權利，與憲法第十六條意旨不符，因此就此部分不予適用。","held":"都市計畫樁測定及管理辦法第八條後段「經上級政府再行複測決定者，不得再提異議」的規定，限制人民依訴願法及行政訴訟法請求行政救濟的權利，與憲法第十六條意旨不符，應不予適用。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十六條保障人民權益受侵害時有訴願及訴訟的權利，受理機關或法院也有依法決定或裁判的義務，且此權利不得以行政命令限制。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"依辦法第六條及第八條，土地權利關係人認為樁位測定錯誤時，可申請複測及再複測，但第八條後段規定經上級政府再行複測決定者不得再提異議。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"行政法院裁定依文義解釋，認為不得再提異議含有不得訴願及提起行政訴訟之意，因此足使人民的行政救濟權利受限制。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"雖然辦法已有複測及再複測的救濟途徑，但限制人民訴願及行政訴訟權的部分，與憲法保障人民權利的意旨不符，應不予適用。","cites":["5"]}],"who":["土地權利關係人","受樁位測定影響的人民","受理訴願的機關與行政法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於動員戡亂時期國家安全法規定，戒嚴時期經軍事審判且已確定的非現役軍人刑事案件，解嚴後不得向普通法院上訴或抗告，是否違憲。大法官認為，這是因為此次戒嚴長達三十餘年的特殊情況，為使裁判安定、維持社會秩序所必要，且仍可依法聲請再審或非常上訴，因此與憲法尚無牴觸。","held":"該國家安全法規定，已確定的案件解嚴後不得上訴或抗告，但仍許聲請再審或非常上訴，與憲法尚無牴觸。戒嚴不屬此次特殊情況者，不適用本解釋。","points":[{"text":"憲法規定人民除現役軍人外不受軍事審判，但戒嚴法規定非現役軍人可由軍事機關審判，是憲法承認戒嚴制度而生的例外。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"戒嚴法規定解嚴後可依法上訴，以補軍事審判對人權保障不周之慮，符合憲法意旨。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"此次戒嚴自三十八年起至七十六年解嚴，長達三十餘年，情況特殊，時過境遷，事證調查困難。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"已確定案件不得上訴或抗告，是為謀裁判安定，也是維持社會秩序所必要。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"有再審或非常上訴原因者仍可依法聲請，已能兼顧人民權利，與憲法尚無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"戒嚴若不屬於此次特殊情況，則不適用本解釋。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["戒嚴時期受軍事審判的非現役軍人","現役軍人","普通法院與軍事審判機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Taiwan's juvenile case law says a court that receives a juvenile case by transfer may never transfer it again. A Hualien court asked whether this is constitutional, because the juveniles in its cases did not live in Hualien. The Constitutional Court held the ban unconstitutional where the receiving court is not actually the better place to protect the juvenile.","held":"The ban on re-transfer is invalid, from the date of the judgment, to the extent it applies where the receiving court cannot better protect the juvenile. The relevant authorities have 2 years to amend the law. Until then, the receiving court may re-transfer after investigating, and the juvenile or their representatives may appeal.","points":[{"text":"The juvenile law is the state's way of meeting its constitutional duty to protect juveniles' health and healthy growth, so it must serve the juvenile's best interests.","cites":["11","12","13"]},{"text":"Transfers between juvenile courts must rest on real investigation showing the new court better protects the juvenile, and the juvenile must be able to state their views on where the case is heard.","cites":["16","17","18","19","20"]},{"text":"The ban aims to stop courts passing cases back and forth and causing delay, so it is acceptable where the receiving court truly gives better protection.","cites":["21","22","23"]},{"text":"Investigations can be incomplete or wrong, and a juvenile's living situation can change, so the receiving court may no longer be the best place to protect the juvenile.","cites":["25","26"]},{"text":"A blanket ban leaves the court helpless in such cases, and the juvenile has no appeal or other remedy against the transfer order, which violates the constitutional duty of special protection.","cites":["27","28"]},{"text":"In those cases the ban does not help its own purpose and is not an appropriate means, so it fails proportionality; the court also urged review of the lack of remedies against transfer orders.","cites":["30","31"]}],"who":["Juveniles in protection cases","Juveniles' legal representatives and current guardians","Juvenile courts receiving transferred cases","Lawmakers and authorities who must amend the law"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether teachers at public schools, including those who also hold administrative posts, are covered by the Civil Servants Service Act. The court decided that teachers hired under a teaching contract are not covered as civil servants under Article 24 of that Act. A teacher who also takes on a school administrative post is covered for that administrative work.","held":"Public school teachers hired by contract are not 'civil servants' under Article 24 of the Civil Servants Service Act, but a teacher who also holds an administrative post is covered for that post. Full-time teachers still may not take outside jobs unless other rules allow it, under Article 34 of the Educational Personnel Employment Act.","points":[{"text":"Contract-hired teachers do teaching and research work based on a contract, which differs from civil servants who carry out duties set by law under a superior's supervision.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So contract-hired teachers are not civil servants under Article 24 of the Civil Servants Service Act.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"If such a teacher also takes a school administrative post, the Act still applies to that administrative work.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The court's earlier Interpretation Yuan-Jie No. 2986 said contract-hired staff were not covered. The court supplements it as to contract-hired teachers.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"Teachers' conduct is still bound by other laws and their contracts, and they should have ethical rules.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Under Article 34 of the Educational Personnel Employment Act, full-time teachers may not teach or work elsewhere unless other laws provide otherwise.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Contract-hired public school teachers","Teachers who also hold school administrative posts","Full-time teachers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Eight people had been convicted of criminal defamation for things they posted, sent or wrote about others. They asked Taiwan's Constitutional Court to review the defamation rules in the Criminal Code and, in two cases, the court judgments. The court held the rules are constitutional as long as they are applied with a reasonable-fact-checking safeguard, and it rejected all eight petitions.","held":"The defamation provisions (Criminal Code Articles 310 and 311) do not violate the Constitution, provided that a speaker on a public-interest matter who reasonably checked the facts beforehand, and who did not knowingly or recklessly rely on false evidence, is not punished. All eight petitions were dismissed as without merit.","points":[{"text":"Free speech and reputation are both constitutionally protected. When they conflict, the court must balance them, giving weight to how much the speech contributes to public debate.","cites":["53","54","55","56"]},{"text":"Criminal punishment of defamation aims to protect the constitutional right to reputation. It is suitable for that goal, and no equally effective, less harmful alternative exists. The exceptions in Articles 310(3) and 311 further narrow the punishable range.","cites":["62","63","64"]},{"text":"The exception for purely private-life matters unrelated to public interest is acceptable. Proving such matters true would intrude on the privacy of the person described, so speech there yields to reputation and privacy.","cites":["69","70","71"]},{"text":"For public-interest matters, 'truth' does not require absolute objective truth. Requiring that would stifle news reporting, and speakers also owe a duty to verify facts.","cites":["74","75","76"]},{"text":"A speaker who reasonably checked the facts beforehand and relied on false evidence without knowledge or serious recklessness is not punished. Prosecutors or private accusers must prove such bad intent. Without reasonable checking, or with bad intent, reputation takes priority.","cites":["77","78","79"]},{"text":"How careful the checking must be depends on the case. Speech on media or social platforms needs more rigorous checking, while speech with high public-debate value gets more room for error if there is no bad intent.","cites":["80"]}],"who":["People convicted of or facing defamation charges","People who post or publish factual claims about others, including on social media","News media and other publishers","People whose reputation is harmed by statements"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案聲請人是服義務役的軍人，與非軍人被控共同搶奪，軍事法院判他有罪，普通法院卻判非軍人無罪確定。憲法法庭認為，軍事審判法只許以判決違背法令為由上訴普通法院，尚不違憲；但軍人若遇此種有罪、無罪歧異的情形，卻無法聲請再審，則侵害訴訟權，因此准許聲請人在期限內聲請再審。","held":"軍事審判法第181條第5項只許以判決違背法令為由上訴高等法院，尚難謂違反憲法第16條；聲請人自判決送達日起30日內，得就軍事法院該有罪判決向臺灣高等法院高雄分院聲請再審，其餘聲請不受理。","points":[{"text":"審級救濟中事實審與法律審的劃分，原則上屬立法形成範圍；系爭規定的立法意旨僅在落實釋字第436號解釋，使被告能以違背法令為由向普通法院求助，且仍有非常上訴可救濟，故不能因未許以事實認定錯誤上訴就認定違憲。","cites":["20","25"]},{"text":"同一事實不可能既成立又不成立犯罪；若主要證據相同，共同正犯卻分別被判無罪與有罪確定，軍事法院有罪判決的事實認定正確性會引起合理懷疑。","cites":["28"]},{"text":"依無罪推定、罪證有疑利歸被告等原則，應讓受有罪確定判決的軍人以此為由聲請再審，並可直接開啟再審，不受刑事訴訟法第420條第1項第6款須有新事實或新證據的限制。","cites":["28","29"]},{"text":"相關法律未賦予軍人此種再審事由，侵害憲法第16條保障的訴訟權，不符合依正當法律程序公平審判的要求，故聲請人得聲請再審，並應向對應的普通法院（臺灣高等法院高雄分院）提出。","cites":["29","30","33"]},{"text":"軍事審判法第1條的爭議因已修正而不復存在，且釋字第436號解釋後已完成修法，故這些部分不受理或無須補充解釋。","cites":["15","29"]}],"who":["受軍事法院有罪判決的軍人","與軍人被訴共同犯罪的非軍人","本案聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及總統依憲法第五十二條享有的刑事豁免權範圍，以及總統是否享有國家機密特權。大法官解釋認為，總統的豁免權只是任職期間暫時不能被訴究的程序障礙，並非免除罪責，且不及於證據調查與保全、證人義務；總統就國家機密事項則享有決定不公開的權力，並有拒絕證言與拒絕提交證物之權。","held":"總統刑事豁免權是暫時性的程序障礙，不及於他人案件的證據調查保全與證人義務；總統就國家機密事項享有拒絕證言及拒絕提交證物之權，相關程序在立法前由特別合議庭審查。暫時處分聲請無須審酌，部分聲請不受理。","points":[{"text":"憲法第五十二條是基於總統國家元首的特殊身分所作的尊崇與保障，屬法律之前人人平等的例外，釋字第三八八號解釋無須變更。","cites":["16","17","18"]},{"text":"總統不受訴究只是暫時性程序障礙，而非實體免責，所以任職期間不得以總統為嫌疑人或被告進行偵查、起訴與審判，卸任後仍可追訴。","cites":["17","19"]},{"text":"豁免權僅及於總統個人犯罪的暫緩訴究，不及於他人案件的證據調查保全；為避免證據湮滅可保全證據，但不得限制人身自由或妨礙職權，搜索扣押須經特別合議庭准許。","cites":["20"]},{"text":"作證義務不是「刑事上之訴究」，但應準用民事訴訟法第三百零四條就其所在詢問，以示尊崇。","cites":["21"]},{"text":"豁免權針對職位而設，原則上不得事前概括拋棄，但個別證據調查經總統自願配合可視為拋棄個案豁免；第三人如共犯不受保障。","cites":["22"]},{"text":"依權力分立與制衡，總統為最高行政首長，負維護國家安全之責，享有國家機密特權，但並非絕對權力；其拒絕證言與提交證物的程序由總統釋明，並可由特別合議庭審理異議。","cites":["24","25","26"]}],"who":["總統","檢察官與法院","立法機關","涉及總統犯罪的第三人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"台中縣政府辦理區段徵收時，依內政部施行細則的規定，要求台灣自來水公司負擔一半新設自來水管線工程費用，自來水公司認為這違反法律保留原則而聲請釋憲。憲法法庭認為，這項規定沒有法律明確授權，卻規範了涉及地方自治團體財政自主權及公營自來水事業財產權的事項，違反法律保留原則，最遲兩年後不再適用。","held":"土地徵收條例施行細則第52條第1項第8款（新設自來水管線工程費用由需用土地人與管線事業各負擔二分之一）無法律明確授權，違反法律保留原則，自解釋公布日起最遲屆滿2年不再適用；修正後的現行規定在需用土地人為地方自治團體的範圍內亦同。","points":[{"text":"具私法人地位的公營自來水公司享有憲法財產權保障，其權利受侵害時可聲請釋憲，因此本案予以受理。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"限制人民權利原則上須由法律規定，或由法律明確授權的命令規範；對公營事業財產權及地方自治團體財政自主權的限制也一樣。","cites":["5","6"]},{"text":"工程費用如何分擔，涉及開發效益、財務規劃與負擔能力，不是細節性或技術性事項，影響也不輕微，應有法律或法律明確授權為依據。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"土地徵收條例第62條只概括規定施行細則由中央主管機關訂定，並未明確授權就自來水管線費用的分擔主體與比例以命令補充，也無法由整體條文推知。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"系爭規定與自來水法第65條在分擔主體、比例、地區與目的上都不同，不能視為內容相同的規定而免於違反法律保留。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"綜合以上，系爭規定違反法律保留原則；現行規定在涉及地方自治團體財政自主權的範圍內也無明確授權。","cites":["10"]}],"who":["需用土地人（含地方自治團體）","公營自來水事業（如台灣自來水公司）","辦理區段徵收的機關","其他管線事業機關（構）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是多位土地所有人主張，土地稅減免規則第9條但書規定，無償供公眾通行的道路土地若屬建造房屋應保留的法定空地，就不能免徵地價稅，違反平等原則等。憲法法庭認為這項差別待遇目的正當、分類與目的有合理關聯，與平等原則無違；聲請人四的裁判憲法審查被駁回，其餘聲請不受理。","held":"土地稅減免規則第9條但書（法定空地部分不免徵地價稅）與憲法第7條平等原則尚無違背；聲請人四聲請裁判憲法審查部分駁回，其餘聲請不受理。","points":[{"text":"平等原則的審查上，租稅減免涉及整體財稅政策，只要目的正當且分類與目的有合理關聯，即符合平等權保障。","cites":["19"]},{"text":"但書的目的是顧及租稅公平負擔、避免免稅條件過度寬鬆，目的正當。","cites":["22"]},{"text":"99年修正所稱「應保留之法定空地」與舊規定的「應保留之空地」只是用語變更，意涵相同，內涵依建築法等規定。","cites":["24"]},{"text":"法定空地屬建築基地一部分，具通風採光、防火等功能，所有人仍享有建築上的利益；單純無償供公眾使用的道路土地則無此利益，故區別課稅有合理關聯，也未逾授權範圍。","cites":["26"]},{"text":"聲請人四關於認事用法的爭執與違憲無涉，而內政部函釋以建築管制觀點認定法定空地，尚難謂違憲，故裁判憲法審查聲請無理由。","cites":["29","30","31"]},{"text":"其餘主張未具體指摘牴觸憲法之處，或以行政處分、裁判為聲請客體，不合法而不受理。","cites":["33","34"]}],"who":["無償供公眾通行土地的所有人","建築基地法定空地的所有人","稅捐稽徵機關","本案四組聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是臺灣高等法院審理案件時，認為國家安全法規定人民入出境都要經過許可、未經許可者要受刑罰，可能違憲，因而聲請解釋。憲法法庭認為，該法未區分國民是否在臺灣地區設有住所而有戶籍，一律要求入境須經許可並以刑罰制裁，違反比例原則，侵害國民隨時返回本國的自由。因此與解釋意旨不符的部分，自入出境相關法律規定施行時起不再適用。","held":"1992年修正後的國家安全法第三條第一項，對在臺灣地區設有住所而有戶籍的國民也一律要求入境須經許可，並對未經許可入境者處罰，違反憲法第二十三條比例原則；與解釋意旨不符的部分，自專就入出境所制定的相關法律規定施行時起，不予適用。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十條保障居住、遷徙自由，包括入出國境的權利，國家不得將國民排斥於國家疆域之外；在臺灣地區設有住所而有戶籍的國民得隨時返回本國，無待許可。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"為維護國家安全及社會秩序，入出境的權利可以限制，但須符合比例原則並以法律規定。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"舊的動員戡亂時期國家安全法規定是為因應當時情勢，適用於該時期與憲法尚無牴觸，但解嚴及終止動員戡亂時期後，法制應逐步回歸正常。","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"修正後的國家安全法第三條第一項仍泛指人民入出境均須許可，未區分有無住所與戶籍，並依第六條對未經許可入境者處刑罰，違反比例原則，侵害國民返回本國的自由。","cites":["3","4","6"]},{"text":"立法機關已制定入出國及移民法並另定施行日期，所以不符部分自相關規定施行時起不予適用。","cites":["3","6"]}],"who":["在臺灣地區設有住所而有戶籍的國民","僑居國外但在臺灣地區未設有戶籍的國民","大陸地區人民"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及民用航空運輸業管理規則中，因違反不得搭載無入境簽證或入境證旅客的規定，而依民用航空法處以罰鍰的部分，其法律授權依據是否明確。大法官認為，對違反行政法上義務者科處罰鍰會限制人民權利，處罰要件與數額應由法律定之；此處法律授權依據不明確，與憲法第二十三條意旨不符。該部分規定應自解釋公布日起，至遲一年後失效。","held":"民用航空運輸業管理規則第二十九條第一項，經同規則第四十六條適用民用航空法第八十七條第七款處罰的部分，法律授權依據有欠明確，與憲法第二十三條意旨不符，自本解釋公布日起至遲屆滿一年時失效。","points":[{"text":"科處罰鍰涉及人民權利的限制，處罰的構成要件及數額應由法律規定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"法律若授權以命令補充構成要件，授權的內容及範圍必須具體明確，才符合憲法第二十三條以法律限制人民權利的意旨。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"該管理規則第二十九條第一項是交通部於七十七年九月十五日修正時，為因應解除戒嚴後的需要而增訂，因違反此項規定而處罰的部分，法律授權依據有欠明確。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"民用航空法第八十七條第七款對「其他違反本法或依本法所發布命令者」一律科處罰鍰，是對應受處罰的行為作空泛而無確定範圍的授權，也應一併檢討。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["民用航空運輸業者","受罰鍰處罰的人民","負責制定相關命令的行政機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是有人聲請大法官解釋，憲法第四條所說的「固有之疆域」究竟指哪些範圍。大法官認為，領土範圍如何界定是重大的政治問題，不應由行使司法權的釋憲機關來解釋，因此決定不予解釋。","held":"憲法第四條「固有疆域」的範圍如何界定，屬重大政治問題，不應由釋憲機關解釋，本件聲請不予解釋。","points":[{"text":"憲法第四條對領土不逐一列舉，而是概括規定「依其固有之疆域」，並設變更程序加以限制，有其政治上及歷史上的理由。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"國家領土範圍如何界定純屬政治問題，這種界定行為在學理上稱為統治行為，依權力分立的憲政原則，不受司法審查。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"若要解釋「固有之疆域」指什麼，必然涉及領土範圍的界定，而這是重大的政治問題，所以本件聲請不予解釋。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["聲請解釋的人","釋憲機關（大法官）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Five people convicted in criminal cases challenged a Criminal Procedure Code rule. Under it, a police-interview statement from a witness who has died, or who cannot be found or brought to court, may be used as evidence. The Constitutional Court held the rule is not unconstitutional, provided courts apply it strictly and protect the defendant's right to defend himself or herself, and provided such a statement is never the only or main basis for a guilty verdict.","held":"The challenges by all five petitioners to Article 159-3, items 1 and 3, were rejected, because the rule is constitutional within the limits the court set. Petitioners 1 and 3's remaining requests were not accepted, and petitioners 4 and 5's requests for a temporary order were rejected.","points":[{"text":"Defendants have a constitutional right to a fair trial and full defense, including questioning witnesses in court. A witness's out-of-court statement, if the witness was never questioned in court, generally cannot be used to convict.","cites":["31"]},{"text":"The legislature may make exceptions in the public interest of finding the truth, if the defendant gets fair compensation for the lost defense rights and the statement is not the only or main proof of guilt.","cites":["32","33"]},{"text":"The rule's statutory conditions are strict: the witness must be dead or unfindable and cannot be brought to court. The statement must also be shown to have been made in specially trustworthy circumstances and be necessary to prove the facts. The prosecutor bears the burden of proof, and the defendant may contest these conditions.","cites":["37"]},{"text":"Because the defendant cannot question such a witness, the court must make up for that loss. It can let the defendant question the interviewer and others when deciding whether the statement is admissible, and strengthen the defendant's questioning of witnesses who do appear.","cites":["36","38"]},{"text":"The court may not use such a statement as the only or main evidence of guilt. Other solid supporting evidence is needed. Within these limits, the rule does not violate Articles 8 and 16 of the Constitution.","cites":["38","39"]},{"text":"Some requests were not accepted because the other rules and the resolution challenged were not applied in the final judgments. The temporary-order requests were rejected because the main requests had been decided.","cites":["26","41"]}],"who":["Criminal defendants","Witnesses who did not appear in court","Courts and judges","Prosecutors"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Article 25 of the Physicians Act, as amended in 1986, is unconstitutional. It let authorities suspend a doctor for one month to one year, or revoke the license, for illegal or improper conduct in practice. The court held that the rule is not unconstitutional because it is clear enough and is a necessary measure.","held":"The 1986 Article 25 of the Physicians Act does not violate the principle of legal clarity, does not conflict with the constitutional protection of people's rights, and is consistent with Article 23 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Professional discipline rules may use open-ended terms, because life is complex. They are acceptable if their meaning is understandable, people can foresee what breaches duty and what punishment follows, and courts can review them.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"'Illegal conduct in practice' means conduct in medical work that, by professional knowledge, is objectively understood as not permitted by law. It is limited to medical-practice acts and does not cover every illegal act by a doctor, so its scope can be determined.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"'Improper conduct in practice' means medical conduct that falls short of illegality but goes against medical theory and medical ethics and lacks legitimacy. Such conduct cannot be listed in full detail, so open-ended concepts are used.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"In individual cases, a properly composed body can decide the meaning using professional knowledge and common social understanding, and courts can review it. So the rule meets the clarity principle.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Illegal or improper conduct by doctors endangers medical safety and public health, and improper fee claims can erode the finances of national health insurance.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Letting the authority choose a penalty by the degree of harm is necessary to uphold medical ethics, keep social order and promote the public interest, so it does not conflict with Article 23.","cites":["2","5"]}],"who":["Physicians","Patients and insured persons","Competent health authorities","Medical professional associations"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A man whose law was struck down as unconstitutional by the court (Interpretation No. 716) kept being turned away when he tried to reopen his old case, partly because the 5-year limit for reopening had passed while his request was pending at the court. The court decided that the time his request was pending at the court should not count toward that 5-year limit. It also let him file again to reopen his case within 30 days.","held":"For people whose requests led the court to strike down a law, the time their request was pending at the court does not count toward the maximum period for reopening their case; the same applies to the civil procedure 5-year limit, and Interpretation No. 209 is supplemented to that extent. The applicant may file to reopen the Taipei High Administrative Court judgment within 30 days of this ruling, free of the 5-year limit.","points":[{"text":"Interpretations bind everyone and apply to the person who requested them, who may rely on them to seek a reopened case, in order to protect the right to bring lawsuits.","cites":["12"]},{"text":"The 5-year maximum for reopening serves the public interest and legal stability and is a reasonable limit in ordinary cases.","cites":["13"]},{"text":"But if the time a request is pending at the court counted, a person who wins a favorable interpretation could still be too late and get no effective remedy, so that time must be deducted; any remaining time, or the 30 days from publication if the remainder is longer, applies.","cites":["14"]},{"text":"Interpretation No. 209's 5-year limit under the civil procedure rule is similar, so on the same reasoning the pending time is deducted there too and No. 209 is supplemented; its 30-day part needs no change.","cites":["15"]},{"text":"The court may set a specific remedy for the underlying case, not bound by the 5-year limit, to give the applicant a real chance of relief.","cites":["17"]},{"text":"Even after deducting the pending periods, this applicant would still be past 5 years, after three earlier attempts were rejected, so the court allowed a new filing within 30 days and ordered the case retried in line with Interpretation No. 716.","cites":["18","19"]}],"who":["Applicants whose requests led the court to strike down a law","Courts hearing reopening cases","The applicant in this case (莊水池)"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問，最高法院二十九年度上字第一００五號判例把「發現未經斟酌之證物」限於事實審言詞辯論終結前已存在的證物，是否違憲。大法官認為，這個判例是為了促使當事人及早提出證物、防止濫行提起再審之訴，並維持確定裁判的安定性，與憲法並無牴觸。","held":"該判例認為只有事實審言詞辯論終結前已存在的證物才可作為再審理由，與憲法並無牴觸。至於辯論終結後才存在的證物，雖不能作為再審理由，但其所證明的事實是否受確定判決既判力拘束，須依個案情形決定。","points":[{"text":"法律允許當事人在事實審言詞辯論終結前隨時提出攻擊或防禦方法，第三審則以第二審確定的事實為基礎，不得再提出新攻擊或防禦方法，所以這裡的言詞辯論終結前指事實審言詞辯論終結前。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此當事人應將已存在、已知悉而得提出的證物，在事實審言詞辯論終結前全部提出；確定終局判決既判力的基準時也是事實審言詞辯論終結時。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"若當事人故意不提出已存在並已知悉的證物，留待判決確定後再提起再審之訴，就是濫用再審制度，既違反訴訟經濟，也影響確定終局判決的安定性。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"該判例的目的在促使當事人及早提出證物，防止判決有既判力後任意提起再審之訴，維持確定裁判的安定性，因此與憲法無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"事實審言詞辯論終結後才存在的證物雖不得作為再審理由，但其所證明的事實是否受既判力拘束，應依個案情形決定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"若證物是依據辯論終結前已存在的證物而製作，該製作的證物能否算是發見未經斟酌的證物，屬於事實認定及適用法律的見解問題。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["民事訴訟當事人","提起再審之訴的人","事實審與再審法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Article 31 of the National Health Insurance Act and the medical rules issued under it are unconstitutional. The court found that Article 31 is too broad and unclear, and that the 1995 medical measures and related internal guidelines went beyond what the law allowed. It ordered the problem parts of the law and the related orders to be reviewed and corrected within two years.","held":"Article 31 of the Act violates the principle of legal clarity, and the 1995 medical measures exceeded the law's authorization. The problem parts of the law and related orders must be reviewed and corrected within two years of the ruling's announcement.","points":[{"text":"National health insurance is compulsory social insurance affecting everyone, so rights and duties under it need clear rules and must rest on law. Any authorization to fill in details by order must be specific, clear and foreseeable to the insured.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"When the law lets the agency issue regulations through a set procedure, it must use them and cannot replace them with internal administrative rules. Without authority to sub-delegate, it cannot hand rule-making to its subordinate bodies.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Article 39 is meant to define clearly what is not covered. For the catch-all item 12, the agency must announce non-covered services and drugs in advance and cannot issue other exclusions instead; if that is not enough, the law can be amended.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"Article 31 is too broad and unclear. The medical measures under it should concern outpatient or inpatient care only.","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"The 1995 measures unilaterally changed the insured's basic rights and duties, and Article 31(2) passed the setting of high-tech items and review procedures to the insurer without authority, exceeding the law.","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"Article 41(3) on prior review sets no items or standards for refusing payment and requires prior review regardless of urgent need, which conflicts with protecting the insured. The payment-standard and drug-price provisions cannot be used to define what is excluded from coverage.","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"Excluding coverage through broadly delegated regulations is already inadequate, and replacing them with internal administrative guidelines not clearly authorized by law violates the legal reservation principle.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["Insured persons","Health insurance agencies","Contracted medical institutions","Health authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a court precedent was unconstitutional for barring any appeal when a personnel authority found a civil servant's proposed appointment unqualified or lowered its rank. The court held that such people may seek relief through administrative appeal or administrative litigation after going through the statutory review process. The part of the precedent that conflicts with this can no longer be used.","held":"Civil servants whose proposed appointment is found unqualified or given a lower rank, and who still disagree after the legal review process, may file an administrative appeal or lawsuit. The conflicting part of Administrative Court precedent No. 400 (1970) is no longer to be applied.","points":[{"text":"Whether a civil servant can challenge a measure in an administrative proceeding depends on what the measure does; earlier interpretations already allowed court challenges for measures that change civil servant status or seriously affect the person.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"A finding of unqualified or a lowered rank in appointment review seriously affects the constitutionally protected right to hold public office.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"So after applying for review under the legal procedure and still disagreeing with the decision, the person may file an administrative appeal or lawsuit to seek relief.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The precedent said such decisions are not administrative actions toward citizens and allowed only a request for review within the agency, with no appeal; the part conflicting with this reasoning is no longer applied.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The petition on one provision of the implementing rules for reservists' transfer to public office was not accepted because no final court judgment existed.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Civil servants whose proposed appointment is rejected or lowered in rank","Personnel authorities","Administrative courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"38位立法委員認為公務人員退休資遣撫卹法調降退休所得、提高基金撥繳費用等規定違憲，聲請解釋。憲法法庭認為多數規定尚無違憲，但要求相關機關後續調整；唯獨再任私立學校職務即停領月退休金的規定違反平等權，自解釋公布日起失效。","held":"提高撥繳費用基準、最低保障金額、調降退休所得與優存利息等規定尚無違憲，並要求至遲於第1次定期檢討時調整、儘速修正物價指數調整規定；第77條第1項第3款違反平等權，自公布日起失效；暫時處分之聲請駁回。","points":[{"text":"調降退撫給與是把新法適用於跨越新舊法、仍在繼續的月退休金等法律關係，且未追繳已領給付，因此不涉及法律不溯及既往原則。","cites":["93","94","95"]},{"text":"提高撥繳費用基準只對未來生效，且基金長期不足額提撥、入不敷出，逐步調高與延長基金用盡年限的目的有合理關聯，故未違反比例原則。","cites":["80","82","83","84"]},{"text":"最低保障金額保障調降後的基本生活；原本低於該金額者並非因新法而被調降，不補足也不違反生存權。","cites":["88","89"]},{"text":"調降並未及於個人在職時提撥的費用本息，只涉及政府預算支應的部分，故採寬鬆標準審查；目的是追求重要公共利益，且設有過渡期間、底限與不予調降等減緩措施，與信賴保護、比例原則尚無違背。","cites":["97","98","110","122","124"]},{"text":"附表三的調降期程與幅度可能使現階段改革效益提前達成，因此相關機關至遲應於第1次定期檢討時，在不改變替代率架構下適當調整。","cites":["129","130"]},{"text":"第67條第1項前段未要求依物價指數調整，與改革初衷不盡一致，應儘速修正；第77條第1項第3款的分類涵蓋過廣又過窄，與目的欠缺實質關聯，違反平等權。","cites":["132","138","139","140","141"]}],"who":["退休公務人員及其遺族","現職公務人員","再任私立學校職務的退休公務人員","提出聲請的立法委員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a court-practice rule is unconstitutional. The rule says that when property under provisional seizure or a provisional injunction is compulsorily purchased or expropriated by the government, the enforcement court must deposit the price or compensation with the court. The Constitutional Court held that the rule is not unconstitutional.","held":"The rule (point 70 of the enforcement notes) requiring the court to deposit the purchase price or compensation does not conflict with Article 5 of the Central Regulations Standards Act, and it does not violate the constitutional protection of property rights.","points":[{"text":"Provisional measures that stop a debtor from transferring property are a preliminary enforcement step. They secure the creditor's eventual claim and are needed to maintain social order and advance the public interest.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Seized property cannot block a government purchase or expropriation, but the price or compensation stands in for the property. The ban on transfer therefore continues to cover that money, and a provisional injunction turns into a provisional seizure.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The deposit rule only declares that the original seizure's effect continues over the substitute. This preserves the creditor's future claim.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Depositing the money does not extinguish the debt, and it adds no restriction on the debtor's rights and leaves the debtor no worse off.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The rule is consistent with the cited Compulsory Enforcement Act provisions, so it does not conflict with Article 5 of the Central Regulations Standards Act or with the constitutional protection of property.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"If the substitute can no longer achieve the purpose of securing the claim, whether the debtor may object under the Enforcement Act is a separate question.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Debtors whose property is under provisional seizure or a provisional injunction","Creditors seeking to secure future claims","Enforcement courts","Government bodies that purchase or expropriate property"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在審查檢肅流氓條例第十一條第一項，法院可以把被移送裁定的人「留置」，也就是限制其身體自由於一定處所。大法官認為，該條例沒有明確規定法院可以裁定留置的要件，除了依第六條、第七條逕行拘提的情形外，是否留置都交給法院自行裁量，已逾越必要程度，與憲法第八條、第二十三條不符。這部分規定應於解釋公布之日起一年內失效。","held":"檢肅流氓條例第十一條第一項關於法院留置的規定，就留置要件未明確規定、全由法院裁量的部分，違反憲法，應於本解釋公布之日起一年內失效；在相關法律修正前，法院裁定留置時應依本解釋意旨妥為審酌。","points":[{"text":"限制人身自由的處置，不論是否為刑事被告，所依據的程序須依法律規定，內容須實質正當，並符合憲法第二十三條的條件，才符合憲法第八條。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"留置與刑事訴訟法的羈押目的相類，但條例有意另稱「留置」，要件也不盡相同，立法設計有異，不能以羈押相比。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"法院雖被授予較大的裁量權以維護社會秩序，但限制人民權利的部分仍須符合明確性原則，並受基本權保障與比例原則限制。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"留置是在感訓處分確定前拘束身體自由於一定處所的強制處分，雖有其必要，卻是對人身自由的嚴重限制。","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"條例未明確規定留置要件；除依第六條、第七條逕行拘提而可推論有留置正當理由者外，是否有繼續嚴重破壞社會秩序或妨礙後續審理之虞，都由法院自行裁量，已逾越必要程度。","cites":["3","6"]}],"who":["被移送裁定的人","受理流氓案件的法院","檢舉人、被害人或證人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked what kind of penalty the fines under the Stamp Tax Act are, and whether a person must have acted intentionally to be fined. The court decided the fines are purely administrative penalties, and that a violation does not require intent. It also changed an earlier interpretation (院字第一四六四號).","held":"Fines under the Stamp Tax Act are purely administrative penalties. A taxpayer who has committed a violation is to be fined according to how serious it is, and intent is not required. Earlier interpretation 院字第一四六四號 is changed.","points":[{"text":"The fines set by the Stamp Tax Act are purely administrative penalties.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"Where a taxpayer has violated the law, a fine must be imposed under the law, with the amount depending on how serious the circumstances are.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"A violation does not depend on intent, so intent is not an element of the offense.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"The earlier interpretation 院字第一四六四號 addressed a specific situation at that time, so it is changed.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Taxpayers under the Stamp Tax Act","Authorities imposing Stamp Tax Act fines"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Article 330 of the Civil Code and Article 7 of the Enforcement Rules of the Deposit Act are unconstitutional. Article 330 ends a creditor's rights in deposited property after ten years of not exercising them, and the property then goes to the national treasury. The rules start the ten years the day after the deposit. The court held they are not unconstitutional, but said creditors must be properly notified, and it called for the rules to be reviewed and revised.","held":"The ten-year period and its start date do not conflict with the Constitution. Because forfeiture affects property rights, the depositor or the deposit office must notify the creditor by notice, service or public announcement, and if that was not done, make up the service or announcement within a reasonable time before the period ends. The enforcement rules must be thoroughly reviewed and revised.","points":[{"text":"After a deposit, the creditor can collect at any time. If the creditor does not, the deposit office must keep the property indefinitely and rights stay uncertain, which harms the economy and society.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The rules aim to settle rights in the deposited property early, which is needed to keep social order stable, so they do not conflict with the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The law already requires the depositor to notify the creditor, and requires the deposit office to serve or announce the deposit notice.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Because the property goes to the national treasury and affects the creditor's property rights, the deposit must be notified, and if that was not done, service or announcement must be made up before the period ends.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"If the property went to the treasury without such make-up notice, the creditor may still seek state compensation where the State Compensation Act's conditions are met.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The enforcement rules should be thoroughly reviewed and revised in line with this reasoning to protect people's property rights.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Creditors of deposited property","Depositors","Deposit offices","The national treasury"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked what the last part of an earlier ruling (No. 363) meant. That earlier ruling had said that anyone applying to build public facilities while the Investment Encouragement Statute was in force must meet its Article 3. The court explained that this refers to businesses that develop public facilities, and that landowners who are individuals and have not formed a company may invest first but are not automatically entitled to the statute's benefits.","held":"The court held that the 'Article 3' requirement in Ruling 363 refers to the item in Article 3, paragraph 1, covering public-facility development businesses. A landowner who is an individual and has not formed a company may invest first under Article 58-1, paragraph 1, but whether they get the various incentives is decided under the statute's own rules. Ruling 363 is supplemented accordingly.","points":[{"text":"Ruling 363 had already said that the Taipei market rule requiring applicants to hold all private land in the market site added a restriction the law does not contain, so it was not to be applied.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Where public-facility developers acquire land through purchase talks, mediation or price-based buying, this can harm landowners' protected interests. That is why the amended statute let landowners invest first.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The statute let developers negotiate directly only if the government notified the owner in writing and the owner did not reply within two months or gave up. Compared with the original draft, which had investors negotiate purchases directly, the legislative intent to put landowners ahead of developers is clear.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So the statement in Ruling 363 about meeting Article 3 means that developer businesses applying to build public facilities must meet the requirements in Article 3, paragraph 1, item 11.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"A landowner who is an individual and has not formed a company may invest first under Article 58-1, paragraph 1, but whether they get the incentives is handled under the statute's rules.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Landowners who are individuals without a company","Public-facility development businesses","Applicants to invest in building public facilities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a constitutional interpretation body can review how the Legislative Yuan passed the laws setting up the National Security Council, National Security Bureau and Personnel Administration Bureau. The court said that how the legislature follows its own procedures is generally its internal matter, and the court reviews it only for obvious, serious constitutional defects. Because it is disputed whether these three laws were actually voted on and that cannot be shown without investigation, the Legislative Yuan must decide that itself.","held":"Procedures inside the legislature are generally for the legislature to decide, and a law it has sent to the President and that was promulgated takes effect. The court can strike down a law only for an obvious, serious defect in how it was made. For the three organizational laws, the Legislative Yuan must settle within a reasonable time whether they were passed and, if its result differs, send the law to the President again.","points":[{"text":"Under the separation of powers, a legislature's way of following its own rules is an internal matter that other state organs should respect, known as parliamentary self-discipline.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Legislative Yuan has the same self-discipline power as other democratic parliaments. Its rules come from its organic act, rules of procedure and practice, and foreign court examples show respect for this.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"A law promulgated by the President after the Legislative Yuan sent it over exists formally and takes effect even if it departed from the legislature's procedures.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"A law can be struck down for procedural defects only if they are obvious and serious without needing fact investigation, such as skipping the required vote.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Where it is disputed whether a defect is serious and facts need investigating, the court is limited. Oral argument covers only legal questions, and summoning legislators would move a political dispute to the judiciary.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"The minutes of these three laws were unconfirmed, but that did not touch the basic rules for making a law. Whether they were actually voted on is disputed and unclear, so the Legislative Yuan must resolve it in a reasonable time.","cites":["2","5"]}],"who":["Legislative Yuan","President","National Security Council, National Security Bureau and Personnel Administration Bureau","Courts and constitutional interpretation bodies"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether it is unconstitutional that people who were given several short prison terms, each of which could be paid off with a fine, lose that option when the combined sentence goes over six months. The court found this puts an unnecessary limit on people's freedoms and does not fully fit Article 23 of the Constitution. It said the criminal law rules involved should be reviewed and revised.","held":"Where each separate sentence is six months or less and could be converted to a fine, but the combined sentence set under the joint-punishment rule exceeds six months so conversion is barred, this does not fully fit Article 23 and the rules should be revised. The part of Article 41 limiting fine conversion to sentences of six months or less, for these cases, stops being effective one year after the ruling is announced at the latest.","points":[{"text":"The joint-punishment rules for several crimes decided before a final judgment were not meant to leave the convicted person worse off.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Where each crime carries a heavy maximum of three years or less and each sentence is six months or less, a person facing hardship over body, education, job or family could normally pay a fine instead of serving time under Article 41.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"When the combined sentence exceeds six months, the fine option is lost and the person must serve time, even though it was available for each sentence on its own.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"This is an unnecessary restriction on people's freedoms and rights and does not fully match Article 23 of the Constitution.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"The rules should be revised together with related issues, such as how to credit a part of the sentences already served.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["People convicted of several crimes before a final judgment","People whose separate sentences are each six months or less","People whose combined sentence exceeds six months"],"covered":true}
