Judges who sat in earlier stages need not recuse.","cites":["90"]},{"text":"The Supreme Court's rules assigning a case back to the same judge are constitutional. They were set in advance and apply generally, and the judge reviews a lower-court ruling, not their own.","cites":["111","115"]},{"text":"A judge who took part in a ruling that was sent back may sit again at the same level, because the defendant still gets a full new hearing. Prior involvement alone does not prove bias, speeds up trials, and avoids running out of eligible judges.","cites":["123","125","127","128","129"]}],"who":["Criminal defendants seeking retrial or extraordinary appeal","Criminal court judges","Defendants in cases sent back for retrial","Legislators and judicial authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A parent whose minor daughter was harmed by three juveniles asked the court to review a rule on juvenile hearings that gave victims no chance to speak in court. The Constitutional Court found that the juvenile case law, taken as a whole, does not expressly let victims (or their legal representatives) appear and give their views, and this falls short of constitutional due process. The government must fix the law within 2 years, and until then juvenile courts must generally summon victims to speak.","held":"Article 36 and the related provisions of the Juvenile Case Act, read together, are unconstitutional to the extent they do not expressly let victims (and their legal representatives) appear in court and state their views in juvenile protection cases. The responsible authorities must amend the law within 2 years, and until then juvenile courts must summon victims and give them a chance to speak, unless there is a proper reason it is unsuitable.","points":[{"text":"The constitutional right to sue and the due process principle give crime victims, including victims in juvenile cases, a basic right to take part in court proceedings, including appearing to state their views.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The state must specially protect the healthy growth of children and youth, and the Juvenile Case Act aims at the juvenile's healthy self-development, so juvenile protection proceedings differ from criminal trials, but victims keep a right to speak where this does not conflict with that aim.","cites":["4","5"]},{"text":"Victim statements help the court find the facts and choose suitable protective measures, and the Act has long given victims their own procedural standing, such as receiving rulings, appealing and consenting to apology or restoration steps.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"So lawmakers must balance protecting juveniles with victims' participation, at minimum giving victims a chance to state views in court, and may not exclude them across the board without proper reason and proportionality.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Article 36 only gives the juvenile's legal representative, guardian and assistant a chance to speak, and other provisions only occasionally let victims speak when consent is sought, so victims have no regular right to be heard.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"As a result victims may be unable to give their account or views to the court, so the rules fail due process; the court ordered a 2-year fix and interim summoning of victims, with the court choosing a manner of speaking that respects the juvenile's healthy growth.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["Victims of juvenile misconduct and their legal representatives","Juveniles in protection proceedings","Juvenile courts","Legislators and authorities amending the law"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a particular kind of light rail track (輕便軌道) counts as immovable property (real estate). The court decided that such tracks are real estate, unless they were laid only temporarily. A track that stays attached to the land and serves a set economic purpose counts as real estate.","held":"Light rail tracks are to be treated as real estate, except those laid only temporarily. Tracks that stay attached to land and serve a set economic purpose count as real estate.","points":[{"text":"The court relied on Article 66, paragraph 1 of the Civil Code, which refers to things fixed to land: not part of the land itself, continuously attached to it, serving a set economic purpose, and not easily moved.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"A track laid on a continuing basis, as opposed to a temporary one, fits that description.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Even if such a track is rebuilt or altered, like a house it does not lose its character as a thing fixed to land, so it is treated as real estate.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Owners of light rail tracks","Operators of light rail tracks"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於民國85年修正的公務人員任用法施行細則第15條第2項，對「薦任第七職等以下職務」的解釋是否違憲。大法官認為這是主管機關對母法所作的補充性解釋，仍在母法合理解釋範圍內，並未違反憲法第18條保障服公職權利，也未違反第23條法律保留原則。","held":"該施行細則第15條第2項規定指「職務之列等最高為薦任第七職等者」，屬補充性解釋，尚在母法合理解釋範圍內，與憲法第18條及第23條法律保留原則均無違背。","points":[{"text":"憲法第18條保障服公職權利，包括任職後依法令晉敘陞遷之權；晉敘陞遷的重要內容應以法律定之。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"主管機關依法律授權訂定施行細則時，若為適用規定而作補充性解釋，且不違反一般法律解釋方法，並符合憲法原則及法律意旨，就不違反法律保留原則。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"立法者為避免衝擊文官制度、顧及考試陞遷管道及公務人員素質，限制考績升任薦任官等者只能擔任薦任第七職等以下職務，屬立法形成自由。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"任用法第17條第4項所稱「以擔任薦任第七職等以下職務為限」，立法理由不明確、文義不清晰，有待解釋。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"施行細則的解釋可避免考績升等者占用列等超過第七職等的職務，使跨列設計失去意義，故在母法合理解釋範圍內，並不牴觸母法及憲法第18條、第23條。","cites":["3","6"]}],"who":["考績升任薦任官等的公務人員","委任第五職等公務人員","公務人員任用及晉敘主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a law reserving the massage trade for visually impaired people is constitutional. The court ruled that the rule violates the constitutional guarantees of equality, the right to work, and the proportionality principle. The rule will stop having effect no later than three years after the ruling is announced.","held":"The rule that only visually impaired people may work in massage (Article 37(1) of the old law, now Article 46(1)) is inconsistent with Constitution Articles 7, 15 and 23. It loses effect no later than three years after the ruling is announced.","points":[{"text":"The rule gives visually impaired people a job-reservation benefit while barring everyone else from massage work, so it had to satisfy equality, the right to work and proportionality.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Protecting the work of visually impaired people is an important public interest, backed by the Constitution's commitment to helping disadvantaged groups.","cites":["4","7"]},{"text":"Equality: as society developed, the massage market grew and the ban became an excessive restriction on sighted people. Other people with disabilities were also excluded, and the rule has not much improved the economic and social position of visually impaired people. Goal and means therefore lack a substantial connection.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Right to work: the ban is an objective restriction on career choice, which is allowed only to protect especially important public interests and only by proportionate means.","cites":["6","7"]},{"text":"The scope of the ban is unclear, so enforcement is inconsistent and sighted people risk breaking the law in similar work. Trained and certified people could work in massage, but the ban forces them to change careers or lose their jobs. The cost to them is out of proportion to the employment benefit for visually impaired people.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The authorities should use other measures, such as training and reserved job opportunities, and manage the massage trade carefully. The three-year period allows time for careful planning and implementation.","cites":["8"]}],"who":["Visually impaired people","People without visual impairment who want to work in massage","Other people with disabilities","Competent authorities and massage consumers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance directive was unconstitutional. The directive let tax offices hold back deed tax bills when several people applied to pay deed tax on the same building or land. The court held that the directive went beyond the statute, blocked people from completing the tax steps needed to register ownership, and conflicted with the constitutional protection of property, so it should no longer be applied.","held":"The Ministry of Finance's 1981 directive allowing tax offices to delay issuing deed tax notices until the parties agree or a court rules is inconsistent with Article 15 of the Constitution (protection of property) and may no longer be applied.","points":[{"text":"Under the Deed Tax Act, paying deed tax is tied to exercising and acquiring property rights, because land offices register a change of ownership only on a deed tax payment receipt.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"When several people apply in turn for the same building or land, the tax office must promptly issue a tax notice to each applicant so they can pay and then register the change.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Civil disputes should be resolved by the parties through legal procedures, and administrative agencies should not step in and require them to negotiate an agreement.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Where one item is sold to several buyers, each contract is valid. Under the principle of equal claims, no buyer's claim excludes the others, and each may request registration of the ownership transfer.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The directive went beyond the statute by letting offices delay the notices. People could not finish the tax steps needed to register ownership, which harmed their exercise of property rights and conflicts with Article 15.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["People applying to pay deed tax on property","Buyers of the same property","Tax collection offices","Ministry of Finance"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a blank tax-paid certificate stamped for audit-based tax collection, if lost by a motorcycle manufacturer, can be treated like a lost inspection certificate so the tax authority collects back taxes. The court said no: the tax authority may not do so under the principle that taxes must be based on law. Cases where tax was actually evaded are still to be handled according to law.","held":"For motorcycle makers taxed by audit, a lost blank tax-paid certificate stamped as a stand-in for the factory-release certificate cannot be treated like a lost inspection certificate under Article 128 of the Commodity Tax Collection Rules, so the tax authority may not collect back taxes on that basis. If tax was actually evaded, it must still be dealt with according to law.","points":[{"text":"Article 128 of the Commodity Tax Collection Rules requires back taxes to be calculated when ordinary audit-taxed manufacturers lose inspection certificates.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The stamped blank tax-paid certificate is only a temporary substitute for the factory-release certificate, and the Rules have no express provision for back taxes when it is lost.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 125 of the same Rules separately provides another way to handle such losses.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Because of the principle that taxes must rest on law, the authority cannot apply Article 128 by analogy, though real tax evasion is still handled according to law.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Motorcycle manufacturers taxed by audit","Tax authorities","Manufacturers who lose stamped blank tax-paid certificates"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是：裁判確定前犯數罪，各罪宣告的有期徒刑都未逾六個月、原本各得易科罰金，但依刑法併合處罰所定的應執行刑逾六個月，因而不能易科罰金，這樣是否違憲。大法官認為這會對人民自由權利造成不必要的限制，與憲法第二十三條規定未盡相符，相關刑法規定應檢討修正。","held":"此種因併合處罰致執行刑逾六個月而不得易科罰金的情形，與憲法第二十三條未盡相符，刑法相關規定應檢討修正；刑法第四十一條以六個月以下為限的規定，就此情形部分，自解釋公布之日起，至遲一年後失效。","points":[{"text":"刑法設併合處罰規定，並明定各刑為有期徒刑時，在最長刑期以上、合併刑期以下定執行刑，可見原無讓受刑人處於更不利地位的意思。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"數罪的宣告刑均未逾六個月，且因身體、教育、職業或家庭關係執行顯有困難者，依第四十一條本來都得易科罰金，有以罰金代替自由刑的機會。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"但併合處罰所定執行刑逾六個月就不得易科，使原有的易科機會得而復失，非受自由刑執行不可，屬對人民自由權利的不必要限制，與憲法第二十三條意旨未盡相符。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"相關規定應連同相關問題，例如數宣告刑中一部已執行完畢如何抵算，一併檢討修正。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["裁判確定前犯數罪的受刑人","被宣告六個月以下有期徒刑的人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案的爭點是：告訴人誣告時，檢察官是否一定要對被誣告人另外做不起訴處分。大法官表示，檢察官發現原告訴人是誣告時，可以直接就誣告起訴，不必另對被誣告人做不起訴處分。不過，如果原告訴人對原來告訴的事件有聲請，檢察官仍須補做不起訴處分書。","held":"檢察官發現原告訴人誣告時，可直接就誣告起訴，不必另對被誣告人為不起訴處分；但原告訴人對原告訴事件如有聲請，檢察官仍應補為不起訴處分書。","points":[{"text":"爭點在於告訴人誣告時，檢察官是否應對被誣告人為不起訴處分。","cites":["1"]},{"text":"檢察官發現原告訴人誣告時，可直接就誣告起訴，不必另對被誣告人為不起訴處分。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"但原告訴人對原告訴事件如有聲請，檢察官仍應補為不起訴處分書。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["檢察官","原告訴人","被誣告人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A person who passed the 1974 special civil service exam for Taiwan Province grassroots staff was refused a pass certificate because he had not done the required internship. He argued the internship rule violated his constitutional right to take exams and hold public office. The court held that the internship rule and the approved internship measures are constitutional.","held":"The Examination Yuan, as the highest examination body, may set exam rules and methods. The internship provision in the 1974 exam rules and the approval of the internship measures stay within its powers, do not harm people's right to take exams, and do not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Examination Yuan is the highest examination body, and the Constitution (Article 83) gives it power over examinations, so it may make exam rules and choose suitable exam methods.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The internship means learning on the job. It is a suitable way to test candidates' ability and help them understand the work, so passing it before a certificate is issued is part of the exam process, not a probationary trial period.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The internship stays within the Examination Yuan's powers and applies equally to everyone admitted in that exam, so it does not go against the spirit of the exam system in Article 85.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The rules left the internship details to the Taiwan Provincial Government to draft and approve. This delegation does not harm the right to take exams, so it does not conflict with Article 18.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The applicant's claims that the rule conflicts with the exam law, or that it was made through an improper procedure, are not constitutional questions, so the court declined to interpret them.","cites":["3","4"]}],"who":["People admitted through the 1974 Taiwan grassroots civil service exam","Exam candidates generally","Examination Yuan","Taiwan Provincial Government"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a public servant may also work as the publisher or editor of newspapers, magazines and similar publications. The court decided that, unless other laws provide otherwise, public servants may not hold those roles. The ruling gives no further reasoning in the paragraphs provided.","held":"Unless a law or regulation provides otherwise, a public servant may not serve as the publisher or editor of a newspaper-type publication or magazine, under Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Civil Servants Service Act.","points":[{"text":"The question was whether public servants may concurrently serve as publishers or editors of newspapers and similar publications.","cites":["1"]},{"text":"Under Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Civil Servants Service Act, public servants cannot hold these posts, except where other laws or regulations say differently.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Public servants","Newspaper and magazine publishers","Newspaper and magazine editors"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案的爭點是：行政院依懲治走私條例第二條第二項專案公告管制物品及其數額，若之後公告內容有變更，是否適用刑法第二條。大法官認為不適用，因為變更的只是公告內容，並不是處罰的法律規定有變更。","held":"行政院依懲治走私條例第二條第二項所作管制物品及其數額的公告，內容變更後，對於變更前走私行為的處罰，不能認為有刑法第二條的適用。","points":[{"text":"刑法第二條所說的「法律有變更」，指的是處罰的法律規定有變更。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"行政院公告內容的變更，並不是懲治走私條例處罰規定的變更。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此公告變更與刑法第二條所稱法律有變更不符，該條自然不適用。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["變更前有走私行為的人","辦理走私案件的機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是財政部發布的營利事業所得稅查核準則，對在台以新台幣支付國外佣金如何認定，是否違憲。憲法法庭認為該規定只是佣金認定與舉證方式的技術性、細節性規定，未逾越所得稅法等相關規定，也未加重人民稅負，與憲法第十五條、第十九條、第二十三條及第七條平等原則均無牴觸。","held":"該準則第九十二條第五款第五目規定，在台以新台幣支付國外佣金，應在不超過出口貨物價款百分之三範圍內，憑國外代理商或代銷商名義出具之收據認定，並不違憲；其與其他國外佣金規定的差別也不違反平等原則。","points":[{"text":"人民有依法律納稅之義務，租稅法律應本於租稅法律主義，並衡酌經濟意義及實質課稅之公平原則解釋。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"該準則第九十二條有關國外佣金的各款規定，都屬於舉證方法與認定要件，且該準則規範的是結算申報的調查、審核事項。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"在台以新台幣支付國外佣金是否真有支付事實，查證困難，因此參考過去外匯管制時可逕行辦理押匯的限額，以出口貨物價款百分之三為認定標準，超出與否所需的證據與舉證程度不同。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"超過百分之三的部分，營利事業仍可提出其他證明文件，經稽徵機關查核相符即可認定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"此規定屬技術性、細節性事項，為簡化稽徵作業、避免國外佣金浮濫列報所必要，未逾越所得稅法等規定，也未加重人民稅負，故不牴觸憲法第十五條、第十九條、第二十三條。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"與其他國外佣金規定的不同，只是斟酌事實情況差異而定不同認定標準，故不違反憲法第七條平等原則。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["支付國外佣金的營利事業","稽徵機關","國外代理商或代銷商"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Taipei City rule limiting who may apply to invest in building retail markets was unconstitutional. The rule required applicants to hold the use rights to all private land within the market site. The court held that this added a restriction the urban planning law does not contain, so the rule should not be applied.","held":"The Taipei City requirement that applicants hold use rights to all private land in the market site adds a limit not found in Article 53 of the Urban Planning Law, goes against the constitution's protection of people's rights, and is not to be applied. During the period the Statute for Encouragement of Investment was in force, applications to build public facilities must meet its Article 3.","points":[{"text":"Local administrative bodies may issue orders to fill in details needed to carry out a law, but those orders must not conflict with the law.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Article 53 of the Urban Planning Law lets approved private investors rent public land or ask the government to buy private land for them, and does not require applicants to hold use rights to all the private land.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Statute for Encouragement of Investment, Article 58-1, rests on the same purpose by letting investors buy land through the government when negotiations fail.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Taipei's rule added a restriction the law lacks and conflicts with the law's aim of having governments help private investment in public facilities and improve urban development, so it goes against the constitution's protection of people's rights.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"While the investment statute was in force, applicants to build markets had to meet its Article 3, which limits eligible businesses to joint-stock companies engaged in production.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Private persons or groups wanting to invest in building retail markets","Taipei City government","Owners of private land within market sites"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是民事確定判決若消極地不適用應適用的法規，而且影響裁判結果，當事人能否提起再審。大法官認為這種情形屬於民事訴訟法第四百九十六條第一項第一款所說的「適用法規顯有錯誤」，應允許再審；但若對裁判顯無影響，則不能作為再審理由。","held":"確定判決消極的不適用法規而顯然影響裁判者，屬適用法規顯有錯誤，應許當事人提起再審之訴；與此見解不合的最高法院判例部分不予援用。若對裁判顯無影響，則不得據以再審。大法官依人民聲請所作解釋，對該聲請人據以聲請的案件也有效力。","points":[{"text":"最高法院判例認為「適用法規顯有錯誤」不包括消極不適用法規，依此當事人就這類確定裁判無從以再審尋求救濟。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"適用法規顯有錯誤，指應適用的法規未適用，或不應適用的法規誤予適用；該款原是參照民事第三審上訴理由及刑事非常上訴的規定增設，以貫徹憲法保障人民權益的本旨。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"第三審上訴及非常上訴所稱違背法令，兼指不適用法規與適用不當，所以該款除適用不當外，也應包含消極不適用法規。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"消極不適用法規須對裁判結果顯有影響，當事人才可請求救濟；若顯無影響，就無保護必要，不得作為再審理由。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"人民聲請解釋而結果對聲請人有利時，為符合許可人民聲請解釋的規定，解釋效力應及於其據以聲請的案件，聲請人可依法定程序請求救濟。","cites":["8"]}],"who":["提起再審之訴的民事當事人","聲請解釋的人民","民事確定判決的當事人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Supreme Court precedent is unconstitutional because it says how a party must state, in a third-instance appeal, that the lower court's judgment violated the law. The precedent requires a specific showing, such as naming the legal provision, principle, interpretation or precedent relied on, or the facts fitting the listed grounds. The court held that the precedent does not conflict with the Constitution.","held":"The Supreme Court precedent (71 Tai-Shang No. 314) only explains how the civil procedure provisions apply and how to specify a legal violation. It adds no restrictions the law does not set, does not impair people's proper exercise of the right to sue, and does not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution's right to sue means people can bring suit when their rights are infringed and courts must judge according to law, but the Constitution does not say how the right is exercised, so the legislature may make reasonable rules based on the nature of the case.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Code of Civil Procedure makes the third instance a review on points of law, so an appeal from a second-instance judgment must rest on a violation of law, and the appeal must state its grounds.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The law requires appeal grounds to be filed, and an appeal that does not file them is dismissed without a request to fix it. This lets the third-instance court review the case and prevents abusive appeals.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Code does not say how appeal grounds must be written, and the precedent fills that gap by explaining the text of the law and how to specify a legal violation.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Because the precedent adds no restrictions the law does not provide and does not impair the proper exercise of the right to sue, it does not conflict with the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Parties filing third-instance civil appeals","Courts hearing civil appeals","Litigants claiming a lower-court judgment violated the law"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問臺灣省工廠工人退休規則中，關於工人自願退休的規定，是否違反憲法。大法官認為，這項規定與憲法尚無牴觸。理由是它有助於維持工人退休後的生活，也有利於勞資協調合作與生產發展。","held":"臺灣省工廠工人退休規則關於工人自願退休的規定，與憲法尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"憲法要求國家制定保護勞工的法律、實施保護勞工的政策，也要求勞資雙方本於協調合作原則發展生產事業。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"省政府為保護勞工、促進勞資協調合作，在執行中央法令而法令未臻周全時，於不牴觸的範圍內，可以訂定單行法規。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"內政部依工廠法訂定的施行細則，已規定工廠訂定工廠規則時，應載明退休、撫卹、資遺、福利事項。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"自願退休的規定旨在維持工人退休後的生活，與憲法保護勞工的政策無違。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"這項規定也能促進工人新陳代謝、提高生產效率、鼓勵工人專業服務，有利工廠經營，符合勞資協調合作發展生產事業的精神，所以與憲法尚無牴觸。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["工廠工人","工廠","臺灣省政府"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Criminal Code rule is constitutional that bars converting a prison term into a fine when several offenses, each one eligible for conversion, are combined into a total sentence of more than six months. The court decided that this part of the rule violates the Constitution and no longer has effect. It also dismissed two related requests: the interim-measure requests and one petitioner's challenge to Article 53.","held":"The part of the current Article 41, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Code that excludes conversion to a fine when each sentence is convertible but the combined sentence exceeds six months violates Article 23 of the Constitution and is inconsistent with Interpretation No. 366. It loses effect on the day the interpretation is announced.","points":[{"text":"Under the Constitution, bodily freedom is protected. Prison should be used only when a lighter penalty cannot do the job, and converting a short prison term to a fine eases the harshness of imprisonment.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Combining sentences for several offenses is meant to give them a fair overall assessment, not to put the person in a worse position. Losing the chance to pay a fine because the combined term exceeds six months amounts to a harsher judgment of conduct already judged, going beyond the purpose of the combined-sentence system, as Interpretation No. 366 explained.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The legislature's stated aim of avoiding encouragement of crime is legitimate. But judges can already impose prison terms over six months that cannot be converted, and prosecutors can refuse conversion under the proviso of Article 41, paragraph 1 when it would not correct the offender or maintain legal order.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Allowing conversion of a combined sentence over six months does not necessarily encourage crime, so refusing it in every case is an excessive restriction on bodily freedom.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The legislature has wide freedom to make law but may not go beyond the Constitution or the court's constitutional interpretations. The 2005 amendment went back on the earlier rule that already matched Interpretation No. 366.","cites":["4","5"]},{"text":"One petitioner's challenge to Article 53 only disputed how the courts applied the law. The challenge to Article 54 concerned a provision the final ruling had not applied, so both were not accepted. The related interim-measure requests were dismissed.","cites":["8","9","3"]}],"who":["People sentenced for several offenses that could each be converted to a fine","Courts and prosecutors deciding on conversion to fines","The legislature"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Five city and county councils passed local food-safety rules that banned any detectable ractopamine (a feed additive, 'lai-ji') in imported meat, and the central government declared the rules void or refused to approve them. The Constitutional Court held that setting safe residue limits for imported meat is a matter for central legislation, so the central government's actions were constitutional. It declined to hear the remaining requests.","held":"The court held that safe-residue standards for beta-agonists in imported meat and meat products are for the central government to legislate. It also held that the Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Executive Yuan did not exceed their constitutional power to supervise local government when they voided or refused to approve the local rules, and it dismissed the remaining requests.","points":[{"text":"The constitution sets up a unitary state, not a federal one. Local self-government lawmaking remains bound by the constitution and central law, and local rules that conflict with central law are invalid.","cites":["65","66"]},{"text":"Local lawmaking is limited to people and things inside the locality's own area. A local rule that has a direct and close real effect outside the area is a cross-regional or national matter and cannot be left to each locality.","cites":["69","70"]},{"text":"Residue standards for meat sold nationwide must be uniform, because different local limits would directly affect buyers, sellers and transport outside each area. Under the constitution's provisions on commerce and public health this is central legislative business, and the Food Safety Act authorizes only the central authority to set the standard.","cites":["73","74"]},{"text":"The five local ordinances, though worded as applying to local residents, affect people and things outside their areas. They therefore went beyond local lawmaking power and conflicted with the Food Safety Act and the constitution.","cites":["76"]},{"text":"The earlier Interpretation No. 738 does not help the petitioners. There, central law gave local authorities power and the rules affected only locals; here the local standards lack authorization, contradict central rules, and affect people outside the area.","cites":["78"]},{"text":"The zero-detection rules also conflict with the constitution's guarantee of free circulation of goods within the country. Lawfully imported ractopamine meat was effectively made illegal locally, even meat merely passing through, which obstructs the domestic market.","cites":["85","86","87","88"]},{"text":"Because the local standards lacked authorization and conflicted with central law, the supervising authorities could declare the ordinances void or refuse approval. Whether the central standard protects health well enough is a risk-assessment question outside this case.","cites":["81","82","92"]}],"who":["Local councils and governments of cities and counties","Central health and executive authorities","Importers and sellers of meat","Consumers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a patent law rule requiring a patent holder to attach an infringement appraisal report before filing a criminal complaint is constitutional. The court decided the rule places an unnecessary limit on people's right to bring legal action and breaks the proportionality principle. The requirement and its consequence are no longer to be applied from the date of the ruling.","held":"The patent law provisions requiring an infringement appraisal report to be attached to a complaint (Article 131, paragraph 2), and making a complaint without it invalid (paragraph 3), are not to be applied from the date the interpretation is published.","points":[{"text":"The constitutional right to bring legal action covers seeking redress from judicial bodies, including criminal justice, and the state must provide institutional protection for it. Laws may reasonably limit how it is used, but only within the proportionality principle of Article 23.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Under criminal procedure, expert appraisal is a kind of evidence that applies only after proceedings begin, and the prosecutor or court chooses the appraiser.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Even if the victim submits an appraisal report, prosecutors or courts must still investigate the evidence themselves and cannot decide a crime occurred on the report alone.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Making the report a condition for filing a complaint is therefore an unnecessary limit on the right to sue and violates the proportionality principle.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Appraisal bodies might refuse requests, delay, or be unable to handle fast-changing patent content, so patent holders could miss the legal deadline to file a complaint.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"A patent holder who files a written complaint that specifically points to evidence of infringement has made a valid complaint.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Patent holders","Alleged patent infringers","Prosecutors and courts","Appraisal bodies"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭執的是：政府採購得標廠商若國內員工逾一百人，就必須僱用一定比例的原住民，沒達到就要繳代金，這樣的規定是否違憲。憲法法庭認為這些規定沒有違反平等原則和比例原則，也不違反憲法對財產權與營業自由的保障。不過法庭也提醒相關機關應檢討改進。","held":"原住民族工作權保障法第十二條第一項、第三項及政府採購法第九十八條，要求國內員工逾一百人的得標廠商至少僱用百分之一原住民，未達標準須繳代金，並不違憲。","points":[{"text":"規定限制了廠商的營業自由與財產權，繳代金也是對財產權的限制，因此須受平等原則與比例原則檢驗。","cites":["3","4"]},{"text":"規定是為落實憲法對原住民族的保障，促進其就業、改善經濟與社會狀況，目的正當。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"進用比例僅百分之一，負擔不重；也可改繳代金，且代金用於促進原住民就業，與公共利益並非顯失均衡，故符合比例原則。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"以員工逾百人分類，是因大型廠商僱用較有彈性、分擔能力較高，且原住民在就業市場處於相對弱勢，分類與目的有合理關聯，不違反平等原則。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"法庭提醒：此措施多提供短期或非技術性工作，國家仍應有積極作為並定期檢討；代金若超過採購金額，宜有減輕機制。","cites":["8"]}],"who":["政府採購得標廠商","原住民","員工逾一百人的廠商"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Article 31-1 of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Act is unconstitutional. That article confiscates imported or transshipped cargo when it does not match the manifest, cargo list, transshipment list or shipping contract documents. The court held that it does not conflict with Article 23 of the Constitution.","held":"Article 31-1 of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Act, which confiscates goods that do not match the shipping documents unless they were proven to be loaded by mistake, is not in conflict with Article 23 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Customs is responsible for catching smuggling, defined as moving goods across the border without declaring them in order to evade inspection, duties or controls.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"How customs should inspect and what measures it uses to stop smuggling is for the legislature to decide, based on trade practice, customs work and enforcement methods.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Under Interpretation No. 275, a person who breaks a legal duty need not have acted intentionally but must be at fault. Where the act only breaks a prohibition or duty, fault is presumed unless the person proves otherwise.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"In normal international trade, exporters must give correct documents to carriers, and importers should require that the contracted goods be shipped, to avoid mismatches that break import law.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So the article requires importers and exporters to follow standard trade and shipping procedures and record and declare goods honestly in the documents.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Those who can prove a mistaken loading avoid confiscation, the rule does not displace Interpretation No. 275, and it is necessary for the public interest.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Importers","Exporters","Customs authorities","Carriers and shippers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A shareholder who held 700,000 shares in a company had them converted to cash in a merger against its wishes, and asked the court to return the shares. It lost in the ordinary courts and then asked for a constitutional ruling. The court held that the rules allowing cash-out mergers and exempting certain shareholders and directors from conflict-of-interest recusal, as they stood before the July 2015 amendment, violated the constitutional protection of property because they lacked adequate information and a fair-price remedy.","held":"The two provisions, to the extent that the law before the 8 July 2015 amendment gave cashed-out shareholders no timely information and no effective remedy to ensure a fair price, conflict with the constitutional protection of property. The petitioner may apply to a court within 2 months of receiving the ruling to set a fair price.","points":[{"text":"Shares are property protected by the Constitution, since they carry value, dividend rights, voting rights and rights to remaining assets.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Lawmakers have wide discretion over mergers, but when a merger greatly affects dissenting shareholders, such as by forcing them out, they must at least ensure timely information about conflicts of interest and an effective remedy for a fair price.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Cash-out mergers take away dissenting shareholders' shares, and exempting interested shareholders and directors from recusal lets a large holder push the decision through. This greatly affects the shareholders' rights.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Letting interested shareholders and directors vote is not entirely without justification. The key issue is whether dissenting shareholders are adequately protected.","cites":["9"]},{"text":"The old law gave dissenting shareholders no timely access to key information on the merger's effects, the interested parties' stakes, and their reasons.","cites":["10"]},{"text":"The court-set price mechanism applied only when shareholders themselves asked to be bought out, not to those forced out against their will, so there was no effective fair-price remedy.","cites":["11","14"]}],"who":["Shareholders cashed out in mergers against their will","Shareholders and directors with interests in merging companies","The petitioner in this case","Companies carrying out cash-out mergers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A person who hired a lawyer to file a retrial lawsuit at the Supreme Court did not pay the court fee. The court dismissed the case without ordering the fee to be paid, relying on Article 9 of the Enforcement Act of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Constitutional Court held that this rule does not violate the Constitution.","held":"The rule letting a court, without setting a deadline, order a fee correction when the appellant has a lawyer representing them and has not paid the court fee does not hinder the right to sue or equality before the law. Whether it also applies to retrial suits against final third- or second-instance judgments is a question of applying the law in court, and is not unconstitutional.","points":[{"text":"The right to sue must be exercised in the legal form. Correction rules exist to protect people who may lack legal knowledge, but a party with a lawyer is expected to know that a court fee is required.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"To avoid delaying cases, Article 9 lets the court decide whether to order correction, and this does not hinder the right to sue.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The equality clause does not forbid reasonable differences in law based on things like occupation, economic situation or special relationships, so Article 9 does not infringe equality.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Whether Article 9's appeal rule applies to retrial suits is a matter of applying the law in court. Courts should use discretion carefully because the rule affects people's rights, but it is not unconstitutional.","cites":["6"]}],"who":["Appellants represented by lawyers","Parties filing retrial suits","Courts handling appeals and retrials"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是臺灣省非都市土地容許使用執行要點中，限制水質、水量保護區內畜牧設施使用的規定，是否違憲。大法官認為該規定是為執行自來水法及水污染防治法，並未對人民權利增加法律所無的限制，與憲法保障財產權及法律保留原則尚無牴觸。","held":"八十四年六月七日修正發布的執行要點第二十五點，規定在水質、水量保護區範圍內不得新設立畜牧場者，不得同意畜牧設施使用，與憲法第十五條財產權保障意旨及第二十三條法律保留原則尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"區域計畫法旨在促進土地及天然資源的保育利用、改善生活環境、增進公共福利；其第二條後段規定本法未規定者適用其他法律，符合立法目的的其他法律，如自來水法、水污染防治法，均在適用之列。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"內政部依此訂定非都市土地使用管制規則，第六條第一項規定土地應依容許使用項目使用，但其他法律有禁止或限制規定者，依其規定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"執行要點第二十五點是為執行自來水法及水污染防治法，依上述但書意旨，對土地使用應否禁止或限制作出具體明確的例示規定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"此規定也是實現區域計畫法立法目的所必要，並未對人民權利增加法律所無的限制，因此與財產權保障及法律保留原則尚無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"具體個案中的土地是否屬於水質、水量保護區範圍，屬法院認事用法的問題。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["保護區內的土地所有人","畜牧業者","土地使用管制主管機關","法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是行政法院的兩則判例說「行政罰不以故意或過失為責任條件」，是否違憲。大法官認為，人民違反法律義務而受行政罰，法律無特別規定時，雖不須出於故意，仍須有過失。判例中與此意旨不符的部分，與憲法保障人民權利的本旨牴觸，不再援用。","held":"受行政罰的行為，法律無特別規定時，不以故意為必要，但仍須以過失為責任條件；僅違反禁止規定或作為義務、不以發生損害或危險為要件者，推定有過失，行為人不能證明自己無過失時即應受罰。兩則判例與此不符的部分不再援用。","points":[{"text":"行政罰是對人民的制裁，原則上行為人應有可歸責的原因，所以法律無特別規定時，雖不須故意，仍須有過失。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"為了維護行政目的的實現，同時兼顧人民權利的保障，僅違反禁止規定或作為義務、且不以發生損害或危險為要件的行為，推定為有過失。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"行為人若不能舉證證明自己無過失，就應受處罰。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"兩則判例所說「行政罰不以故意或過失為責任條件」等語失之寬泛，與上述意旨不符的部分違反憲法保障人民權利的本旨，不再援用。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["受行政罰的人民","行為人","行政法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案起因於聲請人慈祐宮所有的土地上，有他人所有的建物被登錄為歷史建築，聲請人認為這限制其土地權利卻未獲相當補償。憲法法庭認為，登錄時不必取得土地所有人同意，尚不違憲；但若土地所有人的權利受限已構成特別犧牲，現行規定卻未給予相當補償，在此範圍內違憲，有關機關須在2年內修法。","held":"文資法關於歷史建築登錄未以土地所有人同意為要件，尚難認違憲；但同法第99條第2項及第100條第1項未對構成特別犧牲的土地所有人給予相當補償，在此範圍內不符憲法第15條，有關機關應自解釋公布日起2年內修正文資法。","points":[{"text":"憲法保障財產權，即使國家未剝奪所有權，若對使用、收益或處分的限制逾越社會責任所應忍受範圍而形成特別犧牲，國家也應給予相當補償。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"歷史建築登錄是為保存文化資產、充實國民精神生活與發揚多元文化，目的屬正當公益。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"歷史建築不能離開所定著的土地而存在，對土地所有人的限制就登錄目的而言屬必要，不因所有人是否同意而不同，所以不以同意為要件尚難認違憲。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"第三人土地上的建物被登錄後，若土地所有人使用、管理、處分土地的權能受限已逾社會責任範圍，形成特別犧牲，就應享有受相當補償的權利。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"補償可用金錢或其他適當方式，立法者有形成自由。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"地價稅減徵與免徵遺產稅的規定，或屬量能課稅原則的呈現，或縱屬稅捐優惠，都難謂是相當的補償。","cites":["9"]}],"who":["歷史建築所定著土地的第三人所有人","歷史建築的所有人","負責修法的有關機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a person who deposited money or goods with a court to pay off a debt, and later takes it back, is covered by an earlier ruling (No. 39) on deposits. The court said that earlier ruling does not cover this kind of deposit made for a creditor under Article 326 of the Civil Code. But if the depositor is legally allowed to take the deposit back, Article 125 of the Civil Code still applies.","held":"The deposits meant in Interpretation No. 39 do not include a debtor's payment deposit made for a creditor under Civil Code Article 326. Where such a depositor may legally take back the deposit, Civil Code Article 125 still applies.","points":[{"text":"Interpretation No. 39 was meant to clarify an earlier interpretation (院解字第3239號), and its wording on returning case funds and taking back deposits refers only to custody deposits, not payment deposits for a creditor under Article 326.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The earlier interpretation's wording about returning bail money and civil court funds held by the court makes this reading even clearer.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Where a payment depositor can take back the deposit under Articles 11 or 13 of the Deposit Act, that Act sets no special time limit for the claim, so Civil Code Article 125 applies.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The agency's question about notice after a payment deposit and the ten-year period under Article 330 was not treated as a real doubt about Interpretation No. 39, since it does not differ from a Supreme Court precedent, so no interpretation was given on it.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Debtors who make payment deposits","Creditors named in payment deposits","Persons entitled to take back deposits"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論公務員曾因貪污被判刑確定、並獲緩刑宣告時，在緩刑期間能否應考試或擔任公職。大法官表示，這類人即使獲緩刑，仍要等到緩刑期滿且緩刑宣告未被撤銷後，才可應任何考試或任為公務人員。","held":"曾服公務而有貪污行為經判決確定者，即使受緩刑宣告，也須待緩刑期滿且緩刑宣告未被撤銷，才可應任何考試或任公務人員。","points":[{"text":"考試法第八條第一項第二款及公務人員任用法第十七條第二款所列情事，屬於釋字第五十六號解釋所稱的「他項消極資格」。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"曾服公務而有貪污行為經判決確定者，即使受緩刑宣告，仍適用上述消極資格的限制。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"因此須等緩刑期滿而緩刑宣告未被撤銷，才能應考試或任公務人員。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["曾服公務而有貪污行為經判決確定者","受緩刑宣告的前公務員","想應考試的人","想任公務人員的人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a rule in the Land Act limiting the right of former owners to buy back expropriated land is unconstitutional when the land went unused because of someone other than the government. The court held that the rule is not unconstitutional as long as it is applied in line with the ruling's reading. Under that reading, former owners can still reclaim land where the delay was not their fault and the authorities and the user of the land did not act.","held":"Article 219, paragraph 3 of the Land Act does not conflict with the Constitution when applied within the ruling's meaning. If the delay in using the land is not attributable to the former owner and the authorities and the land-using body failed to act within the period, the former owner's reclaim right is not blocked.","points":[{"text":"Land ownership is protected and limited by law, and expropriation must meet the necessity principle in Article 23 of the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The reclaim right exists to prevent unnecessary expropriation, poorly prepared plans, or delay by the body that needs the land, so it is kept for the former owner.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"If the delay in using the land is the fault of the former owner or of users occupying the land for the owner, the delay cannot be blamed on the expropriating side.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"If the delay is due to other users and not the owner, and the local land authorities did not remove or move the improvements within one year and the land-needing body also did not bring necessary lawsuits, the owner should not be blocked from reclaiming.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Denying reclaim in that situation would put the disadvantage on the former owner even though the authorities and the land-needing body failed to act.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"If the land was already put to use as public property before this ruling and reclaiming would seriously harm the public interest, the owner cannot reclaim it but may seek compensation based on the expropriation price at the time of use.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Former owners of expropriated land","Users occupying expropriated land","Bodies needing land for public projects","Local land authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether, after the 1997 constitutional amendments took effect, Taiwan's provinces are still legal public bodies (public juridical persons). The court decided that provinces remain a level of local government but are no longer local self-governing bodies. They can still be public juridical persons in a limited way, for matters that laws assign to the province and that are not assigned to the nation or to counties and cities.","held":"Under Article 9 of the amended Constitution, a province remains a level of local government but has no self-governing matters set by the Constitution and no power to organize itself, so it is not a self-governing public body. A province may still have public-body status to the extent that laws passed consistently with the amendments leave matters within its authority and let it hold rights and duties.","points":[{"text":"The court said it was interpreting how the Constitution applies, not reviewing whether a law is unconstitutional.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To be a self-governing public body, a regional body must have power to make and carry out rules on its own self-governing matters and must have the power to organize itself.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Under Article 9 of the amendments, the province stays a level of local government. But since 21 December 1998 it has had no constitutionally set self-governing matters and no power to organize itself, so it is not a self-governing public body.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Other public bodies can exist besides the nation and self-governing bodies, such as bodies with compulsory membership that exercise public power and can hold rights and duties. Existing law already recognizes such bodies.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Article 9 authorizes the legislature to set by law the province's organization, powers and relations. So a law consistent with the amendments can leave matters to the province, and to that extent the province can be another kind of public body.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The authority in Article 9, paragraph 3 to adjust the Taiwan Provincial Government's functions by special law does not let the legislature ignore the limits the amendments set on how the provincial government is organized.","cites":["6"]}],"who":["Provincial government of Taiwan","Counties and cities","The legislature that makes laws on provinces"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在審查行政院訂定的「限制欠稅人或欠稅營利事業負責人出境實施辦法」，限制欠稅人出境的規定是否違憲。大法官認為該辦法是依稅捐稽徵法與關稅法的授權所訂定，沒有超出授權目的及範圍，也已顧及納稅義務人的權益。因此認定該辦法為確保稅收、增進公共利益所必要，與憲法並無牴觸。","held":"行政院七十三年七月十日修正發布的限制出境實施辦法，其第二條第一項規定未逾越法律授權的目的及範圍，且為確保稅收、增進公共利益所必要，與憲法尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"該辦法是依稅捐稽徵法第二十四條第三項及關稅法第二十五條之一第三項明文授權所訂定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"辦法第二條第一項規定的限制出境，並未逾越法律授權的目的及範圍。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"辦法第五條規定，有該條所定六款情形之一時，應立即解除出境限制，已兼顧納稅義務人的權益。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"限制出境的規定是為確保稅收、增進公共利益所必要，與憲法第十條、第二十三條均無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["欠繳稅捐的納稅義務人","欠稅營利事業及其負責人","稅捐稽徵機關與海關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Article 6 of the Detention Act and Article 14, paragraph 1 of its Enforcement Rules were unconstitutional. These rules let detained defendants only file internal complaints about how a detention center treats them, and did not let them sue in court. The court held that the parts barring court action violate the constitutional right to bring a lawsuit, and ordered the authorities to fix the rules within two years.","held":"The parts of the two provisions that do not let detained defendants go to court for relief conflict with Article 16 of the Constitution. The relevant authorities must, within two years of the ruling's announcement, review and amend the Detention Act and related rules to set up a suitable court process for timely and effective relief.","points":[{"text":"The right to sue means people whose rights are harmed must have a chance to go to court for timely, effective relief, and this cannot be taken away because of a person's status.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Detention is the most severe interference with personal liberty, and apart from limits needed for the purpose of detention and order in the facility, detained defendants' constitutional rights are in principle the same as other people's, given the presumption of innocence. So if they say the detention authority's decision unlawfully went beyond what was necessary, they must be allowed to sue.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The complaint system gives the detention authority a chance to review itself and offers prompt relief, and it is up to the legislature to design it, but it cannot remove the right to go to court.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The rules date from a time when detainees were seen as in a special power relationship allowing only complaints. A complaint is an internal self-review and is not equivalent to a court trial, so it cannot fully replace court relief.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Whether the court route should be criminal, administrative or a special procedure involves many factors needing planning time, so the authorities are given up to two years to set suitable rules.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The complaint system's nature, organization, procedures and links are unclear, so the authorities should also review it and its relationship to lawsuits when they revise the rules.","cites":["8"]}],"who":["Detained criminal defendants","Detention centers and their supervising authorities","Legislators and agencies revising the rules","Courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論受刑人不服行政機關不予假釋的決定時，應向哪一種法院尋求救濟。因最高行政法院與最高法院的見解不同，大法官作出解釋。大法官認為這類救濟究竟如何設計，應由立法通盤考量，在相關法律修正前，由行政法院審理。","held":"受刑人不服行政機關不予假釋的決定，其救濟方式有待立法通盤考量決定；在相關法律修正前，由行政法院審理。","points":[{"text":"現行監獄行刑法只規定受刑人可提出申訴，沒有明文規定其他救濟途徑。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"最高行政法院與最高法院對於受刑人應向哪個法院訴請救濟，見解發生歧異。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"假釋與否關係徒刑是否停止執行，涉及人身自由；申訴屬行政機關自我審查，不能完全取代向法院請求救濟，所以應由法院審理。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"由何種法院審理、循何種程序，需考量案件性質、即時有效的權利保護、法院組織及人員配置等，應由立法通盤決定。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"在法律修正前，因不予假釋的決定具有行政行為性質，依行政訴訟法相關規定，由行政法院審理。","cites":["5"]}],"who":["受刑人","法務部等行政機關","行政法院","普通法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及教育部發布的遊藝場業輔導管理規則，其中規定電動玩具業不得讓未滿十八歲的兒童及少年進入營業場所，違反者可撤銷營業許可。大法官認為這些規定限制人民的工作權及財產權，卻沒有法律或法律明確授權作依據，違反憲法第二十三條的法律保留原則，因此不予援用。","held":"該規則第十三條第十二款（電動玩具業不得容許未滿十八歲者進入）及第十七條第三項（違反者撤銷許可），違反憲法第二十三條的法律保留原則，應不予援用。","points":[{"text":"人民營業自由受憲法工作權及財產權保障，營業許可條件、應遵守的義務及違反的制裁，都應以法律定之，且須符合憲法第二十三條的要件。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"若由法律授權以命令補充規定，授權的目的、內容及範圍必須具體明確，才能據以發布命令。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"禁止未滿十八歲者進入是營業應遵守的義務，限制營業對象自由；撤銷營業許可是違反義務的制裁，兩者都涉及工作權及財產權，需有法律或法律授權為依據。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"主管機關雖是為維護社會安寧、善良風俗及兒童少年身心健康，在法制未完備時基於職權發布命令，有實際需要，但仍須符合憲法意旨。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"少年福利法、兒童福利法已就相關事項制定法律規範，主管機關尤不得沿用未獲法律授權的命令，這是依法行政的基本要求。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"人民行為依當時法律屬違法者，不因相關職權命令後來被宣告不予適用，就得主張救濟。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["遊藝場業、電動玩具業者","未滿十八歲的兒童及少年","主管機關（教育部）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案的問題是監察院對於自己所掌管的事項，能不能向立法院提出法律案。憲法只明文規定考試院可以提案，對監察院沒有規定。大法官會議認為監察院可以提出，這與憲法精神相符。","held":"監察院關於所掌事項，得向立法院提出法律案，這樣的理解符合憲法的精神。","points":[{"text":"憲法沒有明文規定監察院能否提案，但「省略即排除」的拉丁法諺並非任何情形都能適用；法條有闕漏或尚有解釋空間時就不適用，憲法也有其他闕文的例子，如監察委員的選舉未規定以法律定之，不能認為是有意排除。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"從憲法第七十一條與第八十七條的制定經過來看，關係院院長包括立法院以外的各院院長，各院都可提案是制憲代表所不爭的，也沒有人反對或主張只有考試院才能提案。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"五院依憲法建置，各在所掌範圍內獨立行使職權、相互平等；監察、司法兩院和考試院一樣有提案的職務需要，憲法沒有理由有意排除它們。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"法律案的議決雖專屬立法院，但其他各院對自己所掌事項較為熟悉，向立法院提案作為立法意見的提供，於理於法都無不合。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"考試院依憲法第八十七條既可提案，再基於五權分治、平等相維的體制，並參酌第八十七條及第七十一條的制訂經過，監察院得提案與憲法精神相符。","cites":["5"]}],"who":["監察院","立法院","考試院","司法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked what happens to an original share certificate after a court judgment that had declared it void (an 除權判決) is later revoked. The court decided the original certificate becomes valid again, unless the company has already issued a new certificate and a good-faith transferee has lawfully acquired shareholder rights. In that exception, the original certificate's validity can hardly be restored.","held":"After a judgment declaring a share certificate void is revoked, the original certificate regains its validity. The exception is where the company has already issued a new certificate and a good-faith transferee has lawfully acquired shareholder rights; then the original's validity is hard to restore, and those who lose rights may claim damages or return of unjust enrichment as the law provides.","points":[{"text":"Once a judgment declares a certificate void, the applicant may assert the rights on the certificate against the obligor, and the person holding the certificate can no longer exercise rights under it.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"When that judgment is revoked, its effect disappears retroactively, so the original certificate should be valid again.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"A share certificate is a kind of security, so the same rule applies to shares: the original share regains validity.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"If the company has already issued a new share certificate and a good-faith transferee has lawfully acquired shareholder rights, the original certificate's validity is hard to restore, to protect the safety of securities transactions, in line with the intent of Article 565, paragraph 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"People who suffer loss of rights in these situations may claim damages or the return of unjust enrichment as the law provides, and this supplements Court Interpretation Yuan-Zi No. 2811.","cites":["3","2"]}],"who":["Holders of the original share certificates","Companies that issued the shares","Good-faith transferees of replacement shares","People who lost rights and suffered loss"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問內政部的函釋是否合憲。該函釋認為，即使主要計畫已公布超過二年，只要主要計畫書規定須先擬定細部計畫才能申請建築，就可以不准人民申請建築執照。大法官認為這項函釋超出都市計畫法的規定，另外加上法律所沒有的限制，不符憲法保障人民財產權的意旨，不適用。","held":"內政部七十三年二月二十日函釋，以主要計畫書規定須先擬定細部計畫為由，不准已逾二年的土地申請建築執照，逾越都市計畫法規定，違反憲法保障財產權的意旨，不得適用。","points":[{"text":"都市計畫法第十五條第一項第十款的「其他應加表明之事項」，只限於與第一款至第九款性質相類的事項；法律已另有明文規定的事項，不得再作限制或相反的規定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"未發布細部計畫地區限制建築使用，是為增進公共利益所必要，但人民的財產權不能因主管機關遲延發布細部計畫而繼續無法自由使用土地。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"第十七條第二項但書規定，主要計畫公布逾二年且能確定建築線或公共設施已興建完成者，可依建築法令指定建築線、核發建築執照，以解除限建、保障人民自由使用財產的權利。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"主要計畫書不得在第十款中規定須待細部計畫完成法定程序才發建築執照，以排除但書的適用。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"內政部函釋及苗栗縣政府公告中關於核發建築執照的規定，逾越第十款範圍並另加但書所無的限制，與憲法保障財產權的意旨不符，應不適用。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["申請建築執照的土地所有人","內政部及都市計畫主管機關","主管建築機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the Administrative Execution Act's rules on bringing people in by force (拘提) and detaining them (管收) to make them pay public-law money debts are constitutional. The court held that detention and compelled appearance are allowed in principle, but several of the listed grounds go further than necessary, and the court procedure for detention falls short of due process. The use of administrative enforcement officers to carry out these measures was upheld.","held":"Detention is not forbidden in principle, but grounds 4, 5 and 6 for detention and grounds 1, 3, 4 and 5 for compelled appearance exceed what is necessary and violate Article 23. Allowing detention without a court hearing, and the 5-day ruling period, also fall short of due process, and the unconstitutional provisions lose effect at the latest six months after the ruling is announced.","points":[{"text":"Detention to force payment of public-law money debts is not forbidden when the debtor can pay but does not, since such payment serves major public interests.","cites":["2","7"]},{"text":"Detention grounds 4, 5 and 6 (refusing to state, failing to report assets or reporting falsely, not appearing) do not require proof that the person can pay or that milder measures were tried, so they go beyond what is necessary.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Compelled appearance is shorter than detention but still must meet proportionality; only the grounds of likely flight and not appearing after proper notice were found necessary, and the other four go too far.","cites":["9"]},{"text":"Before detention, a neutral court must hear the person, who must be able to attend and defend themselves, though the process need not match criminal pretrial detention.","cites":["10"]},{"text":"The 5-day period for ruling lets courts skip an immediate hearing, which protects rights poorly and should be reviewed and amended.","cites":["11"]},{"text":"When detention is ordered together with compelled appearance, or for not appearing, the person has not appeared, so no hearing is possible, which violates due process.","cites":["12"]},{"text":"The 'police authority' in Article 8 is meant functionally, so having administrative enforcement officers carry out court-ordered compelled appearance and detention does not violate the Constitution.","cites":["14"]}],"who":["People owing public-law money debts","Administrative enforcement offices and officers","Courts handling detention requests","Legislators who must amend the law"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是立法委員聲請解釋，質疑戶籍法規定人民請領國民身分證時必須按捺指紋並錄存，否則不發給身分證，是否違憲。大法官認為這項規定侵害人民受憲法保障的資訊隱私權，且不符比例原則，與憲法第二十二條、第二十三條意旨不符。該規定自解釋公布之日起不再適用。","held":"戶籍法第八條第二項、第三項強制人民按捺指紋並錄存，否則不發給國民身分證的規定，與憲法第二十二條、第二十三條意旨不符，自解釋公布之日起不再適用；依其他相關規定換發身分證的作業仍可繼續進行。","points":[{"text":"本件由三分之一以上立法委員在修法未果後聲請，符合受理要件，應予受理。","cites":["10","11"]},{"text":"隱私權受憲法第二十二條保障，其中資訊隱私權保障人民對個人資料的決定權、知悉與控制權及更正權，但並非絕對，國家得依符合第二十三條的法律明確加以限制。","cites":["12","13"]},{"text":"國民身分證的發給直接影響人民行使基本權利，不按捺指紋就拒發身分證，形同強制按捺並錄存指紋。","cites":["14"]},{"text":"指紋是具高度辨識功能、可開啟完整個人檔案的敏感資訊，國家若大規模強制蒐集，須是與重大公益密切關聯的侵害較小手段，並以法律明確規定。","cites":["15"]},{"text":"戶籍法未明文規定蒐集指紋的目的，已不符憲法保障資訊隱私權的本旨；防範犯罪也不是戶籍法的立法目的。","cites":["16"]},{"text":"即使以防偽、防冒領冒用、辨識路倒病人失智者及無名屍體等為目的，強制全民錄存指紋仍損益失衡、手段過當，不符比例原則。","cites":["16","17"]},{"text":"若國家基於重大公益要大規模蒐集指紋並建立資料庫，須以法律明定目的、確保必要性與關聯性、禁止目的外使用，並採取防護措施；各國立法例與民調只能作參考，不能據以論斷憲法意旨。","cites":["18","19"]}],"who":["請領國民身分證的人民","立法委員","戶政等主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a business that sells goods at a partner store and collects the payment itself can be treated as the taxpayer for business tax, and whether a fixed 5% fine for missing receipts is constitutional. The court said the tax treatment is consistent with the constitution, but the 5% fine rule is unconstitutional where it has no reasonable cap and produces overly harsh penalties in individual cases, so it must not be applied in those cases.","held":"The Ministry of Finance letter and the court's 1998 meeting resolution (on others' tax payments not affecting the seller's duty to pay) do not violate the principle that taxes must be set by law. The 1990 version of the Tax Collection Act article 44, which imposes a 5% fine with no reasonable maximum, violates proportionality and property rights where it causes obviously excessive penalties, and must not be applied.","points":[{"text":"Under the constitution, tax elements must be set by law, but authorities may explain the law if they follow constitutional principles, the law's purpose and ordinary methods of interpretation.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"A third party cannot change the legally defined taxpayer by contract or by paying in its own name. Such payment only raises a refund question and does not discharge the real taxpayer's duty.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The business tax law makes the seller of goods the taxpayer and requires that seller to issue the invoice.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The Finance Ministry letter holds that a business that sells goods and collects payment itself is the seller and must issue the invoice. The partner store is not the seller, unlike a department store counter where the store collects payment. This adds no new tax duty, does not breach equality and does not limit freedom of business.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Because every sales stage's business is a taxpayer under the value-added system, whether a non-party reported tax on invoices it issued does not remove the real taxpayer's duty to pay the missing tax.","cites":["9"]},{"text":"The 5% fine serves a legitimate purpose of ensuring accurate receipts, but with no cap it can produce obviously harsh penalties and seriously harm property rights, so it breaches proportionality.","cites":["12","13"]}],"who":["Businesses that sell goods at partner stores and collect payment themselves","Business-tax taxpayers who must pay missing tax","Businesses fined for not issuing or obtaining receipts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是行政法院就國民住宅條例第二十一條第一項所定「收回國宅並移送法院裁定後強制執行」事件，究竟該由行政法院或普通法院審理，向大法官聲請解釋。大法官認為，政府與承購人、承租人或貸款人所訂的買賣、租賃或借貸契約屬私法關係，收回國宅的強制執行事件是民事事件，該條所稱法院指普通法院。普通法院民事庭不能以行政法院可受理為由駁回聲請。","held":"國民住宅主管機關依條例第二十一條第一項收回國宅並聲請強制執行的事件為民事事件，由普通法院審理，普通法院民事庭不得以另有行政法院可受理為由裁定駁回；行政法院認無審判權時，應駁回並依職權移送有審判權的普通法院。","points":[{"text":"國家可選擇以公法或私法行為達成行政任務，爭執依性質分歸行政法院或普通法院；立法機關也可另行設計審判權歸屬，一經立法即拘束各機關及人民。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"政府主管機關直接興建分配的國宅，經審核後與申請人訂立買賣、租賃或借貸契約，是推行社會福利的私經濟措施，並無權力服從關係，不能逕認為行使公權力。","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"第二十一條第一項是針對特定違約行為賦予執行力的特別規定，涉及私權關係，屬民事事件，所稱法院指普通法院。","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"行政訴訟法新制實施，不能成為普通法院民事庭駁回強制執行聲請的理由。","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"大法官對個案審判權歸屬的認定視為既判事項，各法院均須遵守；先前普通法院以無審判權駁回的裁定有瑕疵，不生拘束力。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"行政法院應駁回並依職權移送普通法院，受移送法院應回復繫屬並依法審判，以保障人民訴訟權。","cites":["4","8"]}],"who":["國民住宅承購人、承租人或貸款人","國民住宅主管機關","普通法院與行政法院","申請收回國宅強制執行的當事人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Taiwan's conflict-of-interest law is unconstitutional when it bars public officials and their related persons from trading with the agency the official serves or supervises, and fines violators one to three times the deal amount. The court held that the ban itself is constitutional, but that the fine rule is too harsh in some cases because it has no adjustment mechanism. The fine rule will lose effect within one year.","held":"The ban on trading (Article 9) does not violate the Constitution, though the authorities should promptly review its application to officials' related persons. The fine of one to three times the transaction amount (Article 15) violates the proportionality principle and the protection of property, and will lose effect no later than one year after the ruling is announced.","points":[{"text":"The ban and the fine limit work, property, business freedom and freedom of contract, which the Constitution protects, so any limit must meet the proportionality principle.","cites":["4","5"]},{"text":"The purpose is legitimate: to stop unfair competition, improper transfer of benefits and conflicts of interest, and the ban and fine help achieve it.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The ban is necessary because without it officials could use their power to channel benefits, and no less harmful means would work as well.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The ban is not excessive, because it covers only the official's own agency or supervised agencies, so those affected can still trade with others.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Where banning related persons would leave only a few bidders and create a monopoly, harming the public interest, the authorities should review whether the ban is still needed when open and fair procedures exist; officials are held to a higher standard than related persons.","cites":["2","9"]},{"text":"The fine is too harsh in some cases: the deal amount is often far higher than the profit, and even the minimum of one times the amount may be unaffordable, yet the law has no adjustment mechanism.","cites":["3","4","10"]}],"who":["Public officials","Relatives and other related persons of public officials","Government agencies that make purchases, leases or contracts","Businesses fined under the law"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Taiwan's Domestic Violence Prevention Act is unconstitutional because it says little about how police carry out protection orders that do not involve money. The court found the general authorization in Article 52 not unconstitutional in itself. But it said the law lacks procedures and methods for police enforcement, and that the relevant authorities should amend the law quickly.","held":"Article 52's general authorization does not itself violate the Constitution, but the law set no procedures or methods for police enforcement of non-monetary protection orders and gave no specific authorization, so the authorities must amend the law promptly. Until then, police may borrow the procedures of the Administrative Execution Act and use suitable enforcement methods.","points":[{"text":"Restrictions on personal liberty must be set by law, and property restrictions by law or a clearly authorized order. Where the law itself provides for handling of persons, it may specifically and clearly authorize the competent agency to carry it out. Minor, technical details may be set by orders issued under a general authorization.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Under those principles, Article 52 of the Act, which has the central authority set the rules for police enforcement, does not conflict with the Constitution. The Ministry of the Interior's 1999 measures, including the rules on handing over minor children, fit the legislature's intent and only cover details.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The Act's Article 20(1) only names the enforcing body and the procedure for money-payment orders. It sets no procedures or methods for police enforcing other orders, and Article 52 gives no specific, clear authorization for what the measures must contain.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Protection orders can involve measures on persons or compulsory enforcement against property, so these matters should be set by law or by an order with specific, clear authorization. The authorities should amend the law quickly, for example by stating that the Administrative Execution Act or the Compulsory Enforcement Act applies, or by authorizing detailed rules on how those laws apply.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Under the Administrative Execution Act, enforcement other than money payments is handled by the original agency or the competent agency. Court judgments may be enforced by administrative agencies where the law so provides. The Act makes police responsible for enforcing non-monetary protection orders.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"Until the law is amended, police may apply the Administrative Execution Act's procedures to protection orders and use suitable enforcement methods.","cites":["3","6"]}],"who":["Police agencies enforcing protection orders","Domestic violence victims and their minor children","People subject to protection orders","Legislature and competent authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是有人聲請釋憲，質疑所得稅法施行細則第二十五條第二項及財政部兩則函釋，規定納稅義務人選定標準扣除額、經稽徵機關核定應納稅額後，就不能再改為列舉扣除額。憲法法庭認為這些規定沒有超出所得稅法的規範目的，也沒有增加法律所無的限制，因此不違反憲法第十九條的租稅法律原則。另外，聲請人要求宣告法院裁判違憲並撤銷的部分，不予受理。","held":"施行細則第二十五條第二項及兩則財政部函釋均不違反憲法第十九條租稅法律原則；納稅義務人選定標準扣除額且經核定後，不得要求改用列舉扣除額。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十九條的租稅法律原則，是指課稅或給予減免稅優惠時，租稅主體、客體、稅基、稅率等構成要件應以法律明定。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"標準扣除額與列舉扣除額可擇一申報，是立法者為租稅正確與稽徵便宜而設；為避免選擇造成租稅法律關係不確定，有合理限制的必要。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"施行細則以稽徵機關是否完成核定作為選擇期限，是維護租稅安定的合理手段，調和了稽徵正確、程序經濟效能與租稅安定，沒有逾越所得稅法的規範目的。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"主管機關在法定職權內釋示，只要不違反一般法律解釋方法並符合立法意旨，就不違反租稅法律原則。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"兩則財政部函釋只是闡釋上述規定的適用原則，即核定後不得變更已選定的申報方式，沒有增加法規所無的限制。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"法院裁判本身依現行法制不能作為違憲審查的對象，本院也不能撤銷，所以這部分聲請不予受理。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["綜合所得稅納稅義務人","稽徵機關","財政部","聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a person who was pardoned, and who might be able to return to a public office lost through a criminal conviction, can ask to have that office restored. The court said a pardon that declares a conviction and sentence void does not undo sentences already carried out, but it does restore lost civil rights from the day the pardon takes effect. For public offices lost through the conviction, the person may apply to the responsible authority, which handles the request under the relevant laws, if the office can be restored going forward.","held":"A presidential pardon that voids a conviction and sentence has no retroactive effect on sentences already served. Any deprivation of public rights ends from the day the pardon takes effect, and a person who lost a public office may apply to the responsible authority if it can be restored going forward.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution (Article 40) gives the President the power to grant amnesty, pardon, sentence reduction and restoration of rights, and the Pardon Act (Article 3) allows a pardon to declare a conviction and sentence void in special circumstances.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To keep the legal order stable and respect effects that already arose from lawful enforcement, such a pardon does not reach back to sentences already carried out.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"Because the conviction and sentence become void from the day the pardon takes effect, a deprivation of public rights ends from that same day and those rights are restored.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"A public office lost through a final guilty judgment, if it can be restored going forward, may be dealt with by the responsible authority on the person's application, under this interpretation and relevant laws.","cites":["3","2"]}],"who":["People who received a pardon voiding their conviction","People deprived of public rights by a conviction","People who lost public office through a final conviction","Authorities responsible for public offices"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an accountant who objects to a final decision of the Ministry of Finance's accountant disciplinary review committee can take it to administrative court. The court decided that this review decision is in effect the final appeal decision, so no further appeal steps are needed. An accountant who believes the decision is unlawful and harms their rights may go directly to administrative court.","held":"The review committee's decision on disciplining an accountant is substantively equal to a final appeal decision, so no further petition or second petition is allowed or needed. The disciplined person may sue directly in administrative court if they think the decision is unlawful and harms their rights.","points":[{"text":"The constitutional right to petition against administrative actions exists so the agency or its superior can correct unlawful or improper actions; if another legal remedy already achieves this, it is substantively equal to an appeal and no further appeal step is needed.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The appeals law's proviso (\"unless the law provides otherwise\") covers this situation, and it does not mean a person who has used up an equivalent remedy is barred from going on to administrative court.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The disciplinary committee's decision to discipline an accountant is an administrative action, and asking for a review of it is substantively like an appeal.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So the review committee's decision equals a final appeal decision, with no need for another petition or second petition; the disciplined person may go directly to administrative court, in line with Article 16 of the Constitution protecting the right to sue.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Accountants facing discipline","Ministry of Finance accountant disciplinary committees","Administrative courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於政務官退職酬勞金所用的「月俸額」，是否包括月俸以外的其他現金給與。大法官認為，計算政務官退職酬勞金的基準「月俸額」，除月俸外，也應包括「其他現金給與」。不過實際應發給的數額，要依退職時法律所訂的計算標準辦理。","held":"計算政務官退職酬勞金基準的「月俸額」，除月俸外亦應包括「其他現金給與」部分；其他現金給與的應發數額，依退職時法律所訂計算標準為之。","points":[{"text":"政務官退職酬勞金以月俸額為計算基準，而政務官每月支領的俸額依規定包括月俸及公費。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"現行法對退職金的月俸額是否以月俸及公費為標準沒有明確規定，應參酌條例修正時公務人員退休、撫卹相關法令的立法目的，作整體解釋。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"一般公務人員退休金以最後在職月俸額為基數，政務官撫卹也準用公務人員撫卹法，所以政務官退職酬勞金的計算標準應與舊制公務人員的標準相稱。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"依修正前公務人員退休法的規定，月俸額與本俸有別，除本俸或月俸外還包括其他現金給與，因此政務官的月俸額也應包括其他現金給與。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"政務官的界定是否牴觸憲法雖有爭議，但不在本解釋範圍，在法律修正前仍依現行法律解釋。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["政務官","退職的政務官","公務人員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether special municipalities (directly governed cities) must set aside the same share of their budgets for education, science and culture as provinces do. The court decided that they must, because a special municipality has a constitutional status comparable to a province. Its share is therefore set by the rule for provinces, not the rule for ordinary cities and counties.","held":"Article 164's minimum shares set the portion of total annual expenditure that each level of government must devote to education, science and culture. A special municipality's share is to follow the rule for provinces.","points":[{"text":"Article 164 sets minimum shares of the budget for education, science and culture: 15% for the central government, 25% for provinces, and 35% for cities and counties. The 'budget total' means the total expenditure in the annual general budget for ordinary governance, as earlier interpretations Nos. 77 and 231 explained.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The word 'city' in the Constitution sometimes means only provincial cities and sometimes also includes special municipalities, so the word alone does not settle the question.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Because Article 118 places self-governance of special municipalities within the chapter section on provinces, a special municipality that practices self-governance is a local self-governing body at the same level as a province, with comparable status, powers, responsibilities, finances and burdens.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Special municipalities are densely populated and unusual in political, economic and cultural terms, and their infrastructure needs cost more than those of counties and provincial cities. Their finances must be allocated carefully so that city development stays balanced.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"So a special municipality's share of the budget for education, science and culture should follow the provincial rule.","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["Special municipalities (directly governed cities)","Provinces","Provincial cities and counties","Residents who rely on education, science and culture spending"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether earlier court precedents barring civil servants from challenging the pay grade (級俸) set for them were unconstitutional. The court decided that civil servants who dispute their approved pay grade may file an administrative appeal and an administrative lawsuit. The two precedents that said otherwise may no longer be used.","held":"A civil servant who disputes the pay grade assigned to them may bring an administrative appeal and an administrative lawsuit, following the same reasoning as Interpretation No. 323. The two Administrative Court precedents (Nos. 414 of year 57 and 400 of year 59) are no longer to be applied, and Interpretation No. 323 is supplemented.","points":[{"text":"Whether a civil servant can appeal or sue over an administrative action affecting their status depends on what the action contains, as earlier interpretations explained.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Under Interpretation No. 323, when an agency finds a person unqualified or lowers the rank first intended for them, this greatly affects the constitutionally protected right to hold public office, so they may appeal and sue.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Because the same reasoning applies, a dispute over the approved pay grade also allows an administrative appeal and lawsuit.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"As a result, the two earlier Administrative Court precedents should no longer be applied, and Interpretation No. 323 is supplemented.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Civil servants disputing pay grade","Public employees whose qualifications are reviewed","Agencies that review and set pay grades","Administrative Court"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Government bodies, central or local, sometimes disagree about how to apply the same law or order, and ask the court for a unified interpretation. The court ruled that such an interpretation takes effect on the day it is announced, unless it says otherwise, and that it also applies to the case that caused the disagreement and to similar cases. If the original case already has a final judgment that the interpretation finds contrary to the true meaning of the law, the interpretation can be used as grounds for a retrial or an extraordinary appeal.","held":"A unified interpretation takes effect on its announcement date unless it states otherwise, and applies to the disputed case and similar cases handled by agencies. If a final judgment in the disputed case is found to contradict the law's true meaning, the interpretation may serve as grounds for a retrial or extraordinary appeal.","points":[{"text":"The rule allowing agencies to request a unified interpretation rests on the Constitution's grant of power to the Judicial Yuan to unify interpretation of laws and orders, so the court sets out the correct meaning for agencies to follow.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Because of this, an interpretation given on request takes effect on the day it is announced, unless the interpretation itself says otherwise.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Since the interpretation is the standard agencies must follow, it should also apply when they handle the disputed case and similar cases.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"If a final judgment in the disputed case used a view the court finds contrary to the law's meaning, that counts as a clear error in applying the law or a violation of law.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"To protect people's rights, the parties may then rely on the interpretation as grounds for a retrial or extraordinary appeal through the legal procedures.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Central and local government agencies","Parties in the disputed case","Parties in similar cases"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a law letting authorities announce which acts count as polluting the environment was valid, and whether Tainan City's announcement banning unapproved advertisements in certain places went too far. The court held the law itself is acceptable, but Tainan's announcement went beyond what the law allowed because it treated every unapproved advertisement as pollution. The announcement loses effect within three months of the ruling.","held":"The provision of the Waste Disposal Act allowing authorities to announce other polluting acts does not violate the constitutional requirement that a law's delegation be clear. Tainan's announcements exceeded that delegation and lose effect no later than three months after the ruling is published.","points":[{"text":"Limits on people's basic rights should generally be set by law; authorities may fill in details only if the law clearly states the purpose, content and scope of the delegation, and the rules they issue must stay within it.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Read as a whole, the Waste Disposal Act's purposes (clearing waste, improving environmental sanitation, protecting public health) and its listed acts show the delegation is clear enough, so announced acts must be comparable in polluting effect to the ten listed ones.","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"Other listed provisions show that polluting the environment is not limited to dumping waste; other acts harming sanitation and public health can count too.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Tainan's announcement banned and punished unapproved advertisements in listed places and ways, without asking whether they harm sanitation or health or reach a comparable level of pollution, so it went beyond the law's authorization.","cites":["3","5"]},{"text":"The authority must promptly revise its rules so that only unapproved advertising reaching the required level of pollution is a violation; the announcement loses effect within three months.","cites":["5","3"]},{"text":"Because advertising is a form of expression protected by free speech, the authority must consider the necessity and appropriateness of any resulting limits on speech or other rights when revising.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Parts of the petition were not accepted: complaints about how a court applied the law, and about a separate announcement not applied in the final judgment.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["People who put up advertisements in Tainan City","Local environmental authorities","Residents of Tainan City"],"covered":true}
