Under Article 87, objections go to the traffic division of an ordinary court rather than through the usual administrative appeal and administrative litigation route.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The legislature designed this based on the nature of the affected interests, how often such cases occur, the urgency of final decisions, and the workload of the bodies hearing them.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The procedure gives parties the chance to defend themselves and submit evidence, and a judge under Article 80 of the Constitution weighs the evidence and decides fairly, so it meets due process and does not conflict with Article 16.","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["People penalized for traffic violations","Local courts hearing traffic objections","Traffic enforcement authorities","The legislature"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"After the 1999 Taiwan earthquake, the Ministry of the Interior issued letters saying consolation payments for people whose homes were fully or half destroyed would go to those registered and actually living in the damaged home, and had to be claimed within a set period. The court decided these rules were not unconstitutional.","held":"The Ministry's letters tying payments to household registration and actual residence in the damaged home, with an application deadline, stay within the emergency order's purpose and do not violate Article 7 (equality) or Article 23 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The state owes disaster victims appropriate aid, and this is emergency assistance. In deciding who gets it, on what terms and how much, state bodies have wide room, provided they respect equality and use reasonable means given finances and resources.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The President issued the emergency order after the earthquake. Its procedure did not fit Interpretation No. 543 but that was found not to make it unconstitutional, though its content must still meet general constitutional principles.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The emergency order and its enforcement rules aim to give emergency consolation to affected households, consistent with Article 155. Central agencies such as the Ministry of the Interior may carry it out directly.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"People actually living in destroyed homes urgently needed help, while those not living there still had a place to live. This justified a reasonable difference in treatment based on registration, actual residence and a time limit, which is a necessary supplement within the order's scope and consistent with Article 7.","cites":["5","2"]},{"text":"The payment is emergency consolation, not compensation for property loss, so denying it to those who do not qualify does not restrict property rights and raises no Article 23 problem.","cites":["5","2"]}],"who":["People whose homes were fully or half destroyed in the 1999 earthquake","Residents living in the damaged homes","People registered at, but not living in, the damaged homes","Ministry of the Interior"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the first-term members of the Legislative Yuan and Control Yuan may keep exercising their powers when the nation faces a major crisis. The court said yes: if a major upheaval makes it practically impossible to hold the next elections under the law, the first-term members continue in their roles until the second-term members are elected and convene.","held":"Where a major national upheaval makes it practically impossible to lawfully hold the next election, the first-term legislators and control members continue to exercise their powers until the second-term members are lawfully elected and assembled or convened.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution sets terms of three years for legislators (Article 65) and six years for control members (Article 93), and a term would normally run from taking office until the constitutional period ends.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"A major national upheaval can make it practically impossible to hold the next election according to law.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"Letting the two Yuans' powers stall would clearly conflict with the Constitution's basic purpose of establishing a five-Yuan system.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"So until the second-term members are lawfully elected and convened, the first-term members should keep exercising their powers.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["First-term legislators","First-term control members","Second-term members not yet elected"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是有人質疑立法委員選舉採「單一選區兩票並立制」、設有政黨比例代表席次，以及政黨得票須達百分之五才能分配席次的規定是否違憲。憲法法庭認為，憲法增修條文的這些規定並未違反自由民主憲政秩序，公職人員選舉罷免法中相同內容的規定也沒有違憲疑義。另外，部分聲請因不符規定而不受理。","held":"憲法增修條文第四條第一、二項關於並立制、政黨比例代表席次及百分之五政黨門檻的規定，並未違反自由民主憲政秩序；公職人員選舉罷免法第六十七條第二項相關規定也不生牴觸憲法的疑義。制憲聯盟關於每縣市至少一人的聲請及綠黨的聲請，均不受理。","points":[{"text":"憲法修改原則上應予尊重，除非程序有明顯重大瑕疵，或內容違反民主共和國、國民主權、人民基本權核心或權力分立制衡等自由民主憲政秩序。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"增修條文採單一選區制與政黨比例代表制混合的並立制，區域選舉與政黨選舉票結果分開計算兩類當選名額。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"並立制及三十四席政黨比例代表，反映人民兼顧選區代表性與政黨多元性的選擇，並未牴觸民主共和國與國民主權原則，也不能拿其他制度（如聯立制）來指摘它違憲。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"百分之五門檻雖可能造成選票不等值，但目的在避免小黨林立、影響國會議事效率，且未完全剝奪兩大黨以外政黨獲選的可能，未變動選舉權及平等權核心內涵，屬修憲機關可斟酌的範圍。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"選罷法第六十七條第二項是依增修條文制定，內容相同，因此沒有違憲疑義。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"制憲聯盟就「每縣市至少一人」的聲請與其權利受損無關且未敘明，綠黨只是參加人而非當事人，故這些聲請不受理。","cites":["6"]}],"who":["立法委員選舉的選民","參選的政黨","政黨比例代表候選人","聲請人（制憲聯盟、綠黨）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked how an interested party can object to a trademark that has already been approved for registration. The court said that if the party files its own application for a same or similar mark within the six-month public notice period and claims it used its mark first without interruption, the objection must be handled under the objection procedure and Article 3 of the Trademark Law.","held":"An interested party who, during the six-month notice period after approval, applies to register a same or similar mark and objects on the ground of earlier uninterrupted actual use must have the objection handled under the objection procedure and Article 3 of the Trademark Law.","points":[{"text":"Article 3 says that when two or more people apply to register the same or a similar mark for the same goods, priority goes to whoever actually used it first in the Republic of China without interruption.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"Earliest uninterrupted use is the substantive standard for deciding whether to approve or reject a registration.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"An interested party may file its own application for a same or similar mark during the six-month notice period after approval under Article 26 and object to the other's approved mark on the basis of its earlier, uninterrupted use.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"Such an objection should therefore be handled under the objection procedure and Article 3.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Interested parties objecting to trademarks","Owners of approved trademarks","Applicants for same or similar marks"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案處理的是：當事人對更審判決提起上訴時，如果第一次上訴應繳的裁判費沒有繳或繳不足，該怎麼補繳。大法官解釋認為，法院應先向第一次上訴人徵足；若該事件裁判有執行力後仍未繳足，法院應依職權以裁定確定裁判費數額，命負擔訴訟費用的一造補繳。","held":"當事人對更審判決上訴時，第一次上訴的裁判費未繳或未足額，法院應向第一次上訴人徵足；裁判有執行力後仍未繳足，應依職權裁定確定數額，命負擔訴訟費用的一造補繳。院解字第二九三六號解釋(二)有關裁判費部分，應予補充。","points":[{"text":"裁判費是國家應徵收的規費，法院應切實核定訴訟標的價額來徵收，不能讓當事人漏繳或少繳，這樣才符合民事訴訟法的有償主義原則。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"院解字第二九三六號解釋(二)說不得命第一次上訴人補繳，是指法院不得再調查第一次上訴要件有無欠缺，並不是說裁判費可以不用徵足。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此更審判決上訴時，第一次上訴裁判費未繳足，法院應向第一次上訴人徵足；裁判有執行力後仍未繳足，則裁定確定數額，命負擔訴訟費用的一造補繳，並補充原解釋。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["對更審判決提起上訴的當事人","第一次上訴人","負擔訴訟費用的一造","法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案起於聲請人因妨害婚姻案件，質疑最高法院判例及舊解釋以「告訴不可分」為由，禁止人民對與其配偶共犯告訴乃論罪的人提起自訴。大法官認為，刑事訴訟法禁止對配偶自訴是合理限制，但把限制擴及共犯並非維護家庭和諧所必要，有違保障訴訟權的意旨。因此相關解釋部分予以變更，相關判例不再援用。","held":"刑事訴訟法第三百二十一條禁止對配偶自訴，與憲法無牴觸；但院字第三六四號、第一八四四號解釋相關部分應予變更，最高法院二十九年上字第二三三三號判例前段及二十九年非字第一五號判例不再援用。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十六條保障訴訟權，但行使方式由法律規定，法律在符合憲法第二十三條意旨下可作合理限制。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"禁止對配偶自訴是為避免夫妻對簿公堂、維護人倫與家庭和諧，屬立法機關自由形成範圍；且人民仍可對配偶提出告訴，訴訟權未受侵害。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"告訴與自訴性質不同，自訴近似公訴，不準用告訴不可分原則，自訴效力主觀上可分，故禁止對配偶自訴的規定不應擴張到共犯。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"若不願追訴配偶卻無法單獨自訴相姦人，提告效力必及配偶，反不利人倫關係；先告再撤回配偶部分，又有虛耗司法資源之虞。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"因此舊解釋與判例對自訴權的限制並非維持家庭和諧所必要，與憲法第二十三條意旨不符，判例更是增加法律所無的限制。","cites":["3","6","7"]},{"text":"聲請人其他主張所涉規定或判決、座談會結論，不是確定終局裁判所適用的法令，故不受理。","cites":["8"]}],"who":["想對配偶共犯提起自訴的告訴乃論罪被害人","與他人配偶共犯告訴乃論罪的人","夫妻"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑破產法允許法院羈押有逃亡或隱匿、毀棄財產之虞的破產人，且羈押展期的次數沒有限制，是否違憲。大法官認為羈押本身為保全破產財團財產、維護債權人權益而有必要，但第七十一條第二項但書對展期次數未加適當限制，與憲法保障人身自由的本旨不合。相關規定應儘速修正，至遲於解釋公布滿一年時停止適用。","held":"破產法第七十一條第二項但書對羈押展期次數未加適當限制的部分，與憲法保障人民身體自由之本旨不合，應儘速修正，至遲於解釋公布之日起屆滿一年時停止適用；修正前適用時應慎重為之。","points":[{"text":"破產法第七十一條第一項允許羈押破產人，是為保全破產財團財產、維護全體債權人權益，使破產程序順利完成，有其必要。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"除受無期徒刑確定者外，現行法律中對人身自由的拘束都有期間限制，例如強制執行法的管收及刑事訴訟法的羈押。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"破產法上的羈押主要目的在保全財產，但展期次數不設限，與其他法律相比顯欠妥當，容易被濫用，有違憲法保障人身自由的本旨。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"應通盤檢討羈押名稱是否適當、展期次數或總期間如何限制，以及不拘束身體自由時如何管束與違反時如何制裁。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"法律修正前適用現行規定，應斟酌本解釋意旨慎重為之；破產人若涉破產法所定犯罪嫌疑，應移送檢察官偵查，必要時由檢察官依法羈押，是另一問題。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["破產人","破產債權人","法院","破產管理人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是妨害兵役治罪條例對後備軍人搬家卻無故不申報、並導致召集令無法送達者處以刑罰，是否違憲。憲法法庭認為這些規定是立法機關可以決定的事項，沒有違反憲法第十條保障的居住遷徙自由，也不違反憲法第二十三條的比例原則。另外，以意圖避免召集論處，仍不排除責任要件的適用。","held":"後備軍人居住處所遷移無故不依規定申報者處刑罰，以及致使召集令無法送達者依第六條、第七條規定處罰，均與憲法第十條、第二十三條無牴觸；第十一條第三項仍不排除責任要件之適用。","points":[{"text":"憲法規定人民有服兵役義務，但兵役制度與召集如何實施並無明文，服兵役、應召集及違反義務的制裁手段，應由立法機關衡酌國家安全與社會發展需要，以法律定之。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"違反行政法上義務要用行政罰或刑事罰，屬立法裁量，只要未逾越比例原則，就不能直接指為違憲；不同法律因目的不同可採不同處罰。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"後備軍人實際居住處所與戶籍不符，涉及兵役法規的公共利益，與一般出入國管理不同；為確保兵員召集有效實現、維護召集制度，採抽象危險犯的刑事制裁可謂相當。","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"法院個案中可在法定刑範圍內斟酌各種情狀量刑，故無立法嚴苛情形，符合憲法第二十三條比例原則。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"違反申報義務致召集令無法送達，已產生妨害召集的結果、嚴重影響國家安全，以意圖避免召集論罪屬立法形成自由。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"該規定只課予申報義務，使召集令能有效送達，並未限制居住遷徙自由，與憲法第十條無牴觸。","cites":["5","2"]}],"who":["後備軍人","立法機關","審理案件的法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the deputy representative of our country on the United Nations Korea Commission counts as an \"official\" (官吏). The court decided that this person does count as an official under Article 75 of the Constitution.","held":"The court held that the deputy representative is an official as meant in Article 75 of the Constitution, because the government appointed the person and set a one-year term, whether the body is temporary or permanent.","points":[{"text":"The deputy representative was appointed by the government.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"The post has a fixed term of one year.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"Whether the Commission is temporary or permanent does not change the result.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Deputy representative on the UN Korea Commission","Government appointees with fixed terms"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"聲請人是不動產估價師，因開設分事務所並被檢舉，受到警告及申誡的懲戒，認為不動產估價師法禁止設立分事務所違憲而聲請解釋。憲法法庭認為這項禁止規定尚未違反憲法第23條的比例原則，也不違背憲法第15條保障的工作權。不過，法庭也提醒立法者應適時檢討這項規定。","held":"不動產估價師法第9條第2項規定事務所以一處為限、不得設立分事務所，尚未牴觸憲法第23條比例原則，與憲法第15條保障工作權的意旨並無違背。","points":[{"text":"禁止設分事務所限制的是執業方式，屬執行職業自由的限制，只要目的為追求公共利益、手段與目的有合理關聯，就符合比例原則。","cites":["5","6"]},{"text":"不動產估價師的業務與公共利益及人民財產密切相關，與一般營利事業不同，國家可以加以相當的管制。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"規定的目的是統一管理事權、避免借照執業，以維護估價品質、保障委託人財產權益與交易安全，屬正當的公共利益。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"只設一處事務所，有助於主管機關有效檢查，也能減少估價師把受託業務違法交給他人執行的誘因，具有預防效果。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"估價師本來就是一處開業、全國執業，執業區域不受限制，因此不存在重大公益或緊急情況下需例外允許在其他處所執業的問題。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"綜合以上，手段與目的間有合理關聯；但立法者仍應衡酌行業發展與社會信任度等因素，適時檢討此規定。","cites":["9","10"]}],"who":["不動產估價師","不動產估價的委託人","主管機關","立法者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a court can order that a sentence may be converted to a fine when it overturns a prosecutor's refusal to allow that conversion. The court decided it can, when necessary. The court may do this in the same ruling that cancels the prosecutor's decision, or it may leave the matter for the prosecutor to reconsider.","held":"When a court finds an objection to a prosecutor's refusal to allow conversion of a sentence to a fine justified and cancels the refusal, the prosecutor may reconsider in line with the ruling. If necessary, the court may also order in the same ruling that conversion is allowed. This differs from the situations covered in the earlier interpretations numbered 2939 and 1387.","points":[{"text":"Whether conversion to a fine is allowed is normally the prosecutor's power to direct, but the law gives people a way to object to an improper direction in order to protect the sentenced person.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The law sends such objections to the court to decide and does not limit what the court's ruling may contain, so the court may also allow conversion in the ruling to provide a remedy.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"This follows the same legal reasoning as the rule allowing a court to cancel or change a prosecutor's disposition.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The earlier interpretations stated that carrying out a judgment is the prosecutor's power and that whether conversion is allowed depends on the facts at the time of enforcement.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Those earlier interpretations are different from the objection procedure, where the court cancels the prosecutor's direction and may allow conversion at the same time.","cites":["4","2"]}],"who":["Sentenced persons","Others entitled to object","Prosecutors","Courts that imposed the sentence"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a company's articles of incorporation can require more shareholders to attend a meeting, or more voting power, than the minimum set by the Company Act. The court decided that they can. The legal figures are only minimums, and setting higher ones is not forbidden.","held":"The attendance and voting figures in the cited Company Act provisions are minimums. A company may set higher attendance and voting requirements in its articles, and the law does not forbid it.","points":[{"text":"One provision requires a shareholder meeting resolution to have shareholders representing at least two-thirds of total shares present, and approval by a majority of those present.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Another provision requires shareholders representing at least three-fourths of total shares present, and approval by a majority of the voting rights of those present.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Both provisions set only a lowest limit on attendance and voting rights. Neither limits raising that minimum.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"So a company whose articles set higher attendance and voting requirements than the legal minimum is not doing something the law prohibits.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Companies and their articles of incorporation","Shareholders attending company meetings"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case was about a plan to relocate residents of three villages in the Feitsui (Jade) Reservoir catchment area to protect water quality and quantity, and about how the plan decided who could receive a relocation payment. The court found the relocation itself consistent with the Constitution's protection of residence and movement. It also found that using household registration as the only proof of residence was not an equality violation but was incomplete, and ordered the rules to be reviewed and improved quickly.","held":"The relocation plan does not violate the constitutional freedom of residence and movement, because its means are proportionate to protecting water resources. Making household registration the only test for relocation payments does not breach equality, but it is inadequate because it ignores other proof of residence, so the rules must be reviewed and improved promptly.","points":[{"text":"The plan, announced after approval by the Executive Yuan, counts as an administrative order the court can review.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Freedom of residence and movement may be limited only as far as necessary and with a clear legal basis; the Water Supply Act, Article 11, authorizes protected water zones and bans harmful acts there.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"The relocation plan aims to protect water quality and quantity, and its means help reach that aim and are objectively necessary, so it meets proportionality and does not violate Article 10.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Administrative orders that grant benefits, such as payments, must follow constitutional principles, especially equality, and such social policy needs a legitimate aim and means that are effective and necessary.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"The relocation payment aims to help residents leave the catchment area, so it should depend on actual residence; household registration is only one way to show that.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"Using registration as the only standard leaves out people who actually lived there but were not registered, which is incomplete though not an equality violation; those who can otherwise prove long residence before 1 January 1980 should still be paid.","cites":["6"]}],"who":["Residents of Bishan, Yongan and Getou villages","Residents who lived there without household registration","Administrative agencies running the relocation plan"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether it was unconstitutional that the Enforcement Act of the Civil Code Family Book made no special rule when the rules on spouses' combined property were amended. The court held that the Act's general rule (Article 1) is constitutional, but that leaving property that already existed before the 1985 amendment under the old rules, with the husband keeping the rights, fails to carry out the constitutional guarantee of equality between men and women. It told the relevant authorities to review and amend the Act promptly.","held":"Article 1 of the Enforcement Act does not conflict with the Constitution. However, because the Act made no special rule for the amended Civil Code Article 1017, combined property that arose before the amendment still goes by the old rules, which does not achieve gender equality, and the authorities must promptly review and amend the Act. The estate and gift tax provision on a decedent's spouse applies to husband or wife alike and is not unconstitutional.","points":[{"text":"Article 1 of the Enforcement Act respects legal orders that existed before the Family Book took effect or before an amendment, to protect legal stability, and allows special rules where an old order should not continue. So it does not conflict with the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The old Article 1017 gave ownership of much of the combined property, and the income from the wife's original property, to the husband. Because of the Constitution's Article 7 on equality of men and women, it was amended in 1985, and the earlier Supreme Court precedent is no longer followed.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The Enforcement Act set no special rule for the Article 1017 amendment, so combined property that arose before the amendment and still exists remains under the old rules, with the husband continuing to hold the rights. This fails to carry out the equality guarantee.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The old rules also left the husband with ownership of the income from the wife's original property and with management of the combined property. The authorities should promptly revise the Act to balance this against preserving the existing legal order.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The tax provision exempting a decedent's spouse's original or special property from the estate total covers husband and wife alike, so it does not violate Article 7.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Differences in the estate total caused by applying the old Article 1017 result from the latter part of Article 1 of the Enforcement Act, so the tax provision itself cannot be called unconstitutional.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Married couples whose combined property arose before the 1985 amendment","Wives whose property is still under the old rules","Heirs and estates affected by the tax provision","Authorities responsible for amending the Enforcement Act"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The Executive Yuan decided to stop building the Fourth Nuclear Power Plant and to stop spending its budget, and a dispute arose with the Legislative Yuan. The court held that stopping a legally approved budget item is not automatically unlawful, but because this change affected an important national policy, the Executive Yuan had to report to the Legislative Yuan and answer questions. The court did not decide whether nuclear power or other energy is better.","held":"Stopping a budget item that reflects an important national policy change requires the Premier or relevant ministers to report to the Legislative Yuan and face questioning, and the Executive Yuan must promptly make up this report; the Legislative Yuan must listen to it.","points":[{"text":"A passed budget is similar to a law in form but differs in content, who it binds and how it is reviewed. Stopping part of it is not automatically unlawful; where no important policy change is involved and budget law conditions are met, agencies have some flexibility.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"That flexibility is limited: funds needed to keep an agency running cannot be stopped if that threatens its existence, and agencies cannot freely choose which approved items to carry out. Budget rules and the budget review (veto) procedure show an approved budget has binding force.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The Legislative Yuan's power to review budgets includes taking part in forming national policy. Because the plant affects energy reserves, environment and industry, is costly and hard to unwind, and both sides agreed it is an important policy, the legislature should have a chance to take part again.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Any change of policy must follow the constitutional order of checks and balances and legal procedure. Under Article 17 of the Legislative Yuan Functions Act, important matters or policy changes require a report and questioning, which was not done here, so the process was flawed.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The legislature's boycott of the report was also not a proper way to protect constitutional operation, so it too must listen to the report.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"After the report, if most legislators back the change it can proceed; if the legislature opposes, the bodies should negotiate or use existing constitutional mechanisms, and the court leaves the choice to them.","cites":["8"]}],"who":["Executive Yuan and its ministers","Legislative Yuan and legislators","Government agencies carrying out budgets"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The Executive Yuan and the National Assembly Secretariat asked how to count the 'total number' of National Assembly delegates, because delegates could not be re-elected and many vacancies could not be filled. The court decided that, for now, the total means the number of lawfully elected delegates who are able to answer the call and attend a meeting.","held":"Under present conditions, the constitution's 'total number of National Assembly delegates' is counted as the lawfully elected delegates who can respond to the summons and assemble.","points":[{"text":"The question arose because delegates could not be re-elected, many vacancies had no one to fill them, and the Assembly's third session was about to meet and needed a total to calculate attendance.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"In the first and second sessions the total was the number of delegates who were supposed to be lawfully elected, but circumstances have since changed greatly.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"After the major upheaval in the country more than ten years earlier, some delegates lost their freedom and could not attend, and many vacancies could not be filled.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Bodies set up by the constitution are meant to be able to exercise their powers, and the framers did not foresee the Assembly being unable to perform its constitutional function because of these obstacles.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To respect the purpose of establishing the National Assembly, the total is the lawfully elected delegates able to answer the call and meet where the central government is located; those able to attend but who do not are still included.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["National Assembly delegates","Executive Yuan","National Assembly Secretariat"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論的是：當有人認為自己的商標比他人已審定的商標更早實際使用時，可以怎麼處理。大法官表示，利害關係人在審定後六個月公告期間內，另以相同或近似的商標呈請註冊，並以自己實際使用在先且未中斷為由對他人已審定商標提出異議，應依異議程序及商標法第三條規定辦理。","held":"利害關係人在公告期間內，另以相同或近似商標呈請註冊，並以自己實際最先使用且未中斷為理由提出異議的，應依異議程序及商標法第三條辦理。","points":[{"text":"商標法第三條前段規定，二人以上就同一商品以相同或近似商標各別呈請註冊時，應准在中華民國境內實際最先使用並無中斷者註冊。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"此一最先使用的規定，是審查准駁的實質標準。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"利害關係人在第二十六條審定後六個月公告期間內，另以相同或近似商標呈請註冊，並主張自己實際使用在先而未中斷，對他人已審定商標提出異議，就應依異議程序及第三條規定辦理。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["利害關係人","已審定商標的所有人","呈請商標註冊的人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance letter violated the Constitution by requiring owners to report how a building is used before getting a house tax reduction. The court held that the letter fits the House Tax Act and does not conflict with the constitutional principle that taxes must rest on law. Under it, a factory building owner who had already paid at the business rate before reporting cannot get the half-rate reduction for that earlier period.","held":"The Ministry of Finance's 1982 letter requires owners whose buildings qualify for a reduction to report the qualifying use with supporting documents. Tax already paid at the business rate before the report cannot be reduced to half. The court held this matches Article 7 of the House Tax Act and does not conflict with the constitutional principle that taxes must rest on law.","points":[{"text":"Legally registered factories get half-rate house tax on their own buildings used directly for production, and the Act requires owners to report the building's value and use.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Tax authorities may investigate on their own, but they handle many complex cases, and the facts that decide tax reductions lie within the taxpayer's own sphere, so checking every possible reduction without an application would greatly raise collection costs.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Under the constitutional duty to pay taxes according to law (Article 19), taxpayers have a duty to cooperate by reporting, which is necessary for fair and lawful taxation.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Other tax reduction rules, such as those in the Land Tax Act and the land tax reduction rules, also require the taxpayer to apply, and late applicants get the special rate only from the following year.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The current House Tax Act likewise requires reporting within thirty days, with a late report giving the reduction only from the month of reporting, so reporting is a necessary step for the preferential rate.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Ministry's letter therefore matches the legislative purpose of these provisions and does not conflict with the constitutional principle that taxes must rest on law.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Owners of legally registered factory buildings","Taxpayers seeking house tax reductions","Local tax collection authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The Legislative Yuan and the National Assembly were unsure what Interpretation No. 282 meant by National Assembly delegates being 'unsalaried' and able to receive pay 'in specific circumstances', so they asked the court to clarify. The court explained that 'unsalaried' means delegates should not receive regular, fixed stipends or equivalents from the national treasury, not that they can never be paid anything. Reasonable payments when the Assembly meets to exercise its powers are allowed, and the legislature must set the items and standards by law.","held":"'Unsalaried' means delegates are not to get regular fixed stipends or similar payments from the treasury, but it does not mean no pay at all. Pay for convening to exercise powers is allowed, and the legislature must set suitable items and standards by law, including necessary expenses within reasonable limits; the same applies when revising pay laws for other central representatives.","points":[{"text":"The request was accepted because the Legislative Yuan and National Assembly, in applying Interpretation No. 282, had doubts about its wording, and that interpretation concerns only central representatives' pay.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Pay of central representatives, whatever it is called, burdens taxpayers and is an important state matter, so suitable items and standards must first be set by law before a budget can pay them.","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"National Assembly delegates' pay had no legal basis, and the older law for other central representatives did not match actual payments, so both needed review to build a system of lawful pay.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"'Unsalaried' means no regular fixed payment from the treasury of stipends or equivalents, not no remuneration in every case; reasonable pay when meeting to exercise powers is the main example of permitted pay.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Which other circumstances allow pay is for the legislature to decide, including necessary costs directly tied to exercising powers (such as postal, telecom and transport costs) and insurance subsidies during the term, within reasonable limits.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Delegates added under the Temporary Provisions who sat with second-term delegates from 1 January 1992 should receive pay consistent with the second-term delegates, based on public interest and equality.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["National Assembly delegates","Other central representatives","Legislative Yuan","Delegates added under the Temporary Provisions"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑郵政法等規定對掛號郵件的補償條件是否違憲，例如只補償遺失或被竊，而一般掛號郵件毀損不在補償範圍。憲法法庭認為郵政法第二十五條及郵政規則第二百二十七條、第二百二十八條都沒有違憲。對於集郵品等特殊類型郵件是否需另訂規定，則交由主管機關檢討改進。","held":"郵政法第二十五條將掛號郵件補償限於遺失或被竊而不及於毀損，未逾越立法自由形成範圍，與憲法無牴觸；郵政規則第二百二十七條及第二百二十八條未逾越授權，也與憲法無牴觸。特殊類型郵件相關規定須否增訂，應由主管機關檢討改進。","points":[{"text":"郵政屬公用事業，以公營為原則；國家為照顧人民生存、達成給付行政，可限制損失補償或損害賠償責任，但須依憲法第二十三條以法律在增進公共利益必要範圍內為之。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"郵政法並非完全不補償毀損：掛號包裹、報值郵件、保價郵件毀損也補償，金額與方法依授權於郵政規則定之。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"一般掛號郵件多為文件或信函，由寄件人自行封緘，價值易受主觀影響而不易認定，故排除其毀損補償，是衡量收費、服務性質、經營成本及權益受損程度後的考量。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"此排除為維持郵政事業經營、增進公共利益所必要，符合比例原則，與保障財產權的憲法第十五條亦無牴觸。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"集郵品等特殊類型郵件損害價值缺乏客觀標準，易生爭議，其相關程序與補償等須否規定，應由主管機關檢討改進。","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"郵政規則第二百二十七條、第二百二十八條是確定補償責任要件，與萬國郵政公約的規定相符，未逾越郵政法第二十七條授權，也未增加限制。","cites":["5","2"]}],"who":["郵件寄件人","郵件收件人","郵政機關","集郵品等特殊郵件寄件人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑立法院2006年修正的三一九槍擊事件真相調查特別委員會條例（真調會條例）部分條文是否違憲。大法官認為多數條文與憲法及釋字第五八五號解釋意旨相符，但真調會自行裁處罰鍰的規定、相關罰鍰程序規定，以及行政機關不得拒絕被調用人員的規定不符，自解釋公布日起失效。","held":"第八條之二第三項關於罰鍰部分、第四項，以及第十一條第三項，自解釋公布之日起失效；其餘受審查條文與憲法及釋字第五八五號解釋意旨並無不符。","points":[{"text":"真調會是立法院在特殊例外情形下，委任非立法委員人士協助調查的暫時性特別委員會，審查標準是是否違反釋字第五八五號解釋意旨及權力分立、比例、明確性、正當程序等原則。","cites":["5","8"]},{"text":"行政機關不得拒絕調用人員的規定，未經被調用人員及其所屬機關同意，違反權力分立與制衡原則；調用行政機關人員本身則無牴觸憲法。","cites":["10"]},{"text":"立法院可決議將不適任委員除名，此為指揮監督職責，其涵義可由司法審查確認，不違反法律明確性原則；經費由立法院預算支應，必要時動支第二預備金，於符合預算法令時亦不違憲。","cites":["12","14"]},{"text":"調查方法如通知到場、調閱資料、勘驗及封存、攜去證件，是取得真相的有效手段，與強制搜索、扣押不同，且設有同意、假處分及確認訴訟等保障，未逾越調查權範圍。","cites":["18","20"]},{"text":"罰鍰得由立法院院會決議裁處，真調會逕行裁處罰鍰不符解釋意旨，相關程序規定也失所附麗；但向立法院報告並公布違法行為，並無不合。","cites":["22"]},{"text":"請求政府機關或憲警協助，須經該機關同意而提供，不是真調會指揮調度，故不違反權力分立；其他條文的聲請因未具體指摘而不受理。","cites":["24","28"]}],"who":["立法院與真調會委員","受調查的機關、團體、事業或個人","被調用的行政機關人員及所屬機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於刑法第41條第2項規定，各罪原本都可易科罰金的數罪併罰，若定出的應執行刑超過六個月，就不能再易科罰金，這樣是否違憲。大法官認為，這部分規定過度限制人民身體自由，違反憲法第23條，也與釋字第366號解釋意旨不符。該部分自解釋公布之日起失效。","held":"九十四年二月二日修正公布的刑法第41條第2項中，數宣告刑均得易科罰金、但定應執行刑逾六個月即排除易科罰金的部分，違反憲法第23條，並與釋字第366號解釋意旨不符，自解釋公布之日起失效。另兩名聲請人的暫時處分聲請均予駁回。","points":[{"text":"立法院雖有廣泛的立法形成空間，但不得逾越憲法規定及司法院所作的憲法解釋。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"釋字第366號已指出，各罪原得易科罰金，卻因併罰執行刑逾六個月而不能易科，會對人民自由權利造成不必要限制；九十年修法曾符合該意旨，但九十四年修正後又使這種情形出現。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"身體自由受憲法保障，能以較輕手段達成目的時不應用嚴厲手段；易科罰金可避免短期自由刑的流弊，數罪併罰也無使受刑人更不利之意，卻因逾六個月而喪失易科機會，是更不利的評價，逾越併罰制度本意。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"立法理由擔心准予易科會鼓勵犯罪，目的雖正當，但法官可宣告逾六個月不得易科的刑，檢察官也可依第41條第1項但書不准易科，故准易科並不當然鼓勵犯罪，一律不許易科屬過度限制身體自由。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"一名聲請人對刑法第53條、第54條的聲請不合審理案件法規定而不受理，相關暫時處分聲請失所附麗，另第41條第2項的暫時處分因本案已作成解釋而無審酌必要，均予駁回。","cites":["8","9","3"]}],"who":["數罪併罰且各罪均得易科罰金的受刑人","聲請釋憲的人","法官與檢察官","立法機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論公營事業在轉為民營之前，其原有人員在刑法上是否仍屬公務員。大法官表示，依公司法組織的公營事業，即使已確定移轉日期，仍須等到移轉後民股超過百分之五十以上，才能視為民營。在尚未實行交接之前，原有依法令服務的人員仍是刑法上的公務員。","held":"依公司法組織之公營事業在移轉民營時，須待移轉後民股超過百分之五十以上才視為民營；尚未實行交接前，其原有依法令服務之人員仍是刑法上的公務員。","points":[{"text":"依公司法組織的公營事業，即使已確定盈虧及一切權利義務的移轉日期，仍須等移轉後民股超過百分之五十以上，才得視為民營。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"在尚未實行交接之前，該事業原有依法令服務的人員仍屬刑法上的公務員。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["公營事業原有人員","移轉民營中的公營事業"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A licensed Taipei street performer had his permit revoked after repeated violations, and he challenged the city rules that require street performers to get a permit after being reviewed. The court found that the permit system was set up without the required legal basis, and that reviewing a performer's skill or the content of their act violates constitutional freedoms. Reviewing whether an act suits a designated public space was found acceptable.","held":"The three permit rules, taken together, violate the rule that restrictions on rights need a legal basis, because they were not passed by the local legislature or authorized by a local ordinance. The parts that review performers' skill or the content of their acts are unconstitutional, while the part that checks whether an act suits a designated public space is not.","points":[{"text":"The permit rules limit occupational freedom and artistic expression, so they needed a local ordinance passed by the local legislature or clear authorization from one. They were only administrative rules issued by the city government, so they violate the principle that restrictions need a legal basis.","cites":["9","10"]},{"text":"Street performing can be a livelihood, and artistic expression is protected as free expression of high value, so both freedoms are protected.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Reviewing performers' skill limits who may choose this occupation. The aim of keeping poor performers off the street offers quality entertainment but is not an important public interest like protecting life or health, so this part violates the freedom to choose an occupation.","cites":["12","13"]},{"text":"Rules on the time, place and manner of performing, including whether an act suits a designated space, only regulate how the job is carried out. They serve the legitimate aim of keeping public spaces orderly and safe, so they do not violate the proportionality principle.","cites":["14"]},{"text":"Reviewing performance quality or content is a direct intervention that needs strict scrutiny. Artistic value is a personal judgment the government should not replace, and weak skill does little harm to the public, so the aim is not a especially important public interest and this part violates freedom of artistic expression.","cites":["16","17","18"]},{"text":"The review of suitability for the space has no hidden aim of suppressing expression, affects content only incidentally, and leaves applicants enough chance to show their skills, so it is not disproportionate.","cites":["19"]}],"who":["Street performers in Taipei","Taipei city government and its permit authority","Public users of Taipei public spaces"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Taiwan's road traffic law violates the constitution by allowing repeated tickets and fines for a car that stays illegally parked. The court held that repeated ticketing does not punish the same act twice, and that the rule on ticketing every two hours does not go beyond what is necessary. It added that the law should itself spell out the authority to set the ticketing interval.","held":"Allowing continuous ticketing and multiple fines for ongoing illegal parking does not conflict with the principle against punishing one act twice. The two-hour interval in the regulations is not excessive, though the court said the purpose and scope of the delegation should preferably be set clearly in the law.","points":[{"text":"An illegally parked car keeps violating the rule while it stays, so each ticket counts as a separate violation and several fines are not a double punishment for one act.","cites":["2","6"]},{"text":"Continuous ticketing with repeated fines can deter ongoing violations and is useful and necessary for traffic order and safety, but it must still meet proportionality and clear-delegation requirements.","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"The law gives no general standard for how continuous ticketing should be done, but the 'every two hours' rule in the regulations limits the number of fines and total cost, and so is not beyond what is necessary.","cites":["4","8"]},{"text":"The court said the delegation of continuous ticketing power is better set out clearly in the law itself.","cites":["4","8"]},{"text":"Letting officers tow a car after ticketing is a matter the legislature reasonably left to officers' discretion, so it does not show that continuous ticketing breaches proportionality.","cites":["5","9"]},{"text":"The later law fixes a two-hour interval, but the court noted that authorities should be allowed to shorten it for busy roads or rush hours.","cites":["10"]}],"who":["Drivers who park illegally","Traffic police and enforcement officers","Traffic authorities that set the rules"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是刑法第329條（竊盜或搶奪者，為防護贓物、脫免逮捕或湮滅罪證而當場施強暴、脅迫，以強盜論）是否違憲。憲法法庭認為該規定未逾越立法者合理的自由形成範圍，也未違反罪刑相當原則與比例原則，因此不違憲。","held":"刑法第329條未違反憲法：未對相同事物作不合理的差別對待，其所指的強暴、脅迫須達使人難以抗拒的程度，與強盜罪同其法定刑，並不違背罪刑相當原則及憲法第23條比例原則。","points":[{"text":"該條旨在以刑罰保障人民的身體自由、人身安全及財產權，免受非法侵害，以實現憲法第8條、第22條及第15條的意旨。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"防護贓物、脫免逮捕或湮滅罪證，是竊盜、搶奪事發時經常導致強暴、脅迫的原因，立法者選擇這些情形論以強盜罪，以有效保護被害人或第三人。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"其他財產犯罪的取財行為與強暴、脅迫行為間鮮有時空緊密連接關係，所以只擬制竊盜與搶奪為強盜，未逾越立法形成範圍，也不是不合理的差別對待。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"準強盜罪的取財與強暴、脅迫有時空緊密連接，兩種故意可視為複合的單一故意，主觀不法與強盜幾無差異；順序倒置對財產與人身法益的損害也無二致，客觀不法可相同評價。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"準強盜罪的強暴、脅迫必須已達使人難以抗拒的程度，客觀不法才與強盜相當，因此可與強盜罪同其法定刑。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"該條不適用於僅虛張聲勢或短暫輕微肢體衝突的情形，沒有對輕微犯行施以重罰，故不違背罪刑相當原則與比例原則。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["竊盜或搶奪的行為人","被害人或第三人","立法者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked what the phrase \"local public body\" (地方公共團體) means in Article 3, item 2 of the Temple Supervision Act (監督寺廟條例). The court decided that it means a group that handles public affairs within a certain area, under laws or established custom. The paragraphs given do not set out the court's reasons or the facts of the underlying dispute.","held":"The phrase \"local public body\" in Article 3, item 2 of the Temple Supervision Act means a group that, under laws or custom, handles public affairs within a certain area.","points":[{"text":"The question was what \"local public body\" means in Article 3, item 2 of the Temple Supervision Act.","cites":["1"]},{"text":"The court defined it as a group that handles public affairs within a certain area, whether by law or by custom.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Temples covered by the Temple Supervision Act","Groups that handle public affairs in a particular area"],"covered":false}

{"answer":"本案是在審查刑法第235條處罰散布、播送、販賣猥褻資訊或物品等規定，是否違反憲法保障言論及出版自由。憲法法庭認為，在依本解釋意旨限縮適用範圍的前提下，這些規定並未違憲，且「猥褻」一詞也沒有違反法律明確性原則。另有一項關於聲請人指摘確定終局判決的部分，因不符規定而不予受理。","held":"刑法第235條第一項至第三項，依解釋所限定的範圍理解，對言論及出版自由的限制尚屬合理，不違反憲法第11條與第23條比例原則；「猥褻」一詞也不違反法律明確性原則。","points":[{"text":"憲法保障性言論與性資訊，不論是否營利，但這項自由並非絕對，國家可依憲法第23條意旨用法律明確加以適當限制。","cites":["2","6"]},{"text":"社會風化由社會多數人的觀念形成，立法機關的判斷原則上應受尊重；但仍須保障少數性文化族群的性言論表現與性資訊流通，限制以維護多數共通性價值秩序所必要者為限。","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"猥褻資訊會危害社會性價值秩序，立法管制目的正當，以刑罰處罰手段也合理，但處罰範圍應限於必要者。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"法院將處罰範圍限縮為：含暴力、性虐待或人獸性交且無藝術、醫學、教育價值者，或其他猥褻物品未採適當安全隔絕措施而傳布者；製造、持有及沒收也限於相應情形，因此未過度封鎖與歧視。","cites":["4","9"]},{"text":"「猥褻」雖是不確定法律概念，但其意義一般人可理解、可預見，且能經司法審查確認，故不違反法律明確性原則。","cites":["5","10"]},{"text":"社會觀念會隨時代改變，法官審判時應依本解釋意旨，衡酌個案判斷是否達到猥褻而應處罰的程度。","cites":["9"]}],"who":["發表或流通性言論、性資訊的人","少數性文化族群","法官","散布或持有猥褻物品的人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether certain rules in a supplementary regulation on filling vacant seats of First National Assembly delegates conflict with the Constitution. The rules treat a delegate whose whereabouts have been unknown for three or more years, and who did not report in person within the government's announced deadline, as having left the seat. The court decided these rules do not conflict with the Constitution.","held":"Article 3, item 1 and Article 4 of the supplementary regulation on filling vacancies among First National Assembly delegates do not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution says the election and removal of National Assembly delegates are to be set by law.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The supplementary regulation adds to the existing election and removal law for delegates and its enforcement rules.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 3, item 1 treats a delegate missing for three or more years who did not report in person to the designated office by the announced deadline as having left the seat. Article 4 makes a reserve candidate in that situation lose candidate status.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"These rules were created to meet the nation's needs after the central government moved to Taiwan, and they do not conflict with the relevant constitutional provisions.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["First National Assembly delegates","Reserve candidates for delegate seats","Delegates whose whereabouts are unknown"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及原住民與非原住民結婚所生子女，須從具原住民身分之父或母之姓或原住民傳統名字，才能取得原住民身分的規定。憲法法庭認為這項附加要件限制了原住民身分認同權，也造成種族上的差別待遇，不符合憲法，因此宣告違憲。","held":"原住民身分法第4條第2項及相關準用規定違憲，相關機關應於判決宣示後2年內修正；逾期未修法，這些規定失效，原住民與非原住民結婚所生子女即取得原住民身分，並可辦理身分及民族別登記。其餘聲請不受理。","points":[{"text":"原住民身分認同權是受憲法第22條高度保障的重要人格權，限制它應採嚴格審查。","cites":["20","21","24","25"]},{"text":"促進文化認同是特別重要公益，但要求從漢姓，未必有助於促進原住民文化認同，因原住民族本無姓之傳統。","cites":["29","31"]},{"text":"姓名只是形式手段，登記本身即可彰顯認同；要求先從姓或取名才有身分，並非侵害最小的手段，另有較小侵害的替代方式，故不符比例原則。","cites":["32","33","35"]},{"text":"此規定在原原結婚與原與非原結婚所生子女間形成種族或族群分類的差別待遇，應適用嚴格審查。","cites":["38","40"]},{"text":"以姓名分類與促進認同的關聯有疑，原與非原所生子女的原住民血緣未必較低，卻須更多認同表現，差別待遇無據且顯然恣意，牴觸憲法第7條種族平等。","cites":["45","46","47"]},{"text":"法院並指出，因子女從父姓的習慣，母為原住民者的子女較難取得身分，主張性別實質不平等亦非顯然無據。","cites":["48"]}],"who":["原住民與非原住民結婚所生子女","原住民女性或男性之家庭","聲請人","相關機關（負責修法者）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論已登記不動產的所有人，若要請求除去他人對其所有權的妨害，是否會因時間經過而消滅。大法官認為，這種除去妨害請求權雖不在釋字第一０七號解釋的範圍內，但依其性質，同樣不適用民法第一百二十五條的消滅時效規定。","held":"已登記不動產所有人的除去妨害請求權，不在釋字第一０七號解釋範圍內，但依其性質，也不適用民法第一百二十五條的消滅時效規定。","points":[{"text":"民法第七百六十七條所定的返還請求權、除去請求權與防止請求權，都是為了維護所有權的圓滿行使，性質相同。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"這些請求權是否適用消滅時效，彼此之間不應有差別；若解釋不同，理論上自相矛盾，實際上也難以發揮所有權的功能。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"已登記不動產所有人的回復請求權，已經釋字第一０七號解釋認定不適用民法第一百二十五條消滅時效。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"若除去妨害請求權（如對登記有無效原因的登記名義人請求塗銷登記）適用十五年時效，會因不行使而消滅，造成權利名實不符。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"這樣會使真正所有人無法確實支配其所有物，難以貫徹民法第七百六十七條的意旨，所以不適用消滅時效。","cites":["3","2"]}],"who":["已登記不動產所有人","登記名義人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論依耕地三七五減租條例訂立的租約，在租期還沒屆滿前，出租人可以用什麼方式終止。大法官表示，這類租約提前終止的情形，該條例第十七條已有規定，不能再適用土地法第一百十四條及民法第四百三十八條的終止規定。","held":"依耕地三七五減租條例訂立的租約，在租佃期限屆滿前得終止的情形，以同條例第十七條規定為準，不適用土地法第一百十四條及民法第四百三十八條有關終止租約的規定。","points":[{"text":"土地法和民法雖然都有終止耕地租約的規定，但耕地三七五減租條例第十七條明文規定，租期未屆滿前，除該條所列情形外不得終止。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此出租人終止租約，只限於符合該條各款所定情形之一，文義十分明顯。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"依該條例第一條前段，沒有再適用土地法第一百十四條及民法第四百三十八條來終止租約的餘地。","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"承租人若違反民法及土地法的規定，出租人可依法請求回復原狀或損害賠償，或依該條例第十六條第二項主張租約無效，這屬於另一問題。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["出租人","承租人","耕地租約當事人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Ministry of Finance letters on how to calculate fines for using farmland for non-farm purposes were unconstitutional. The letters said the fine is based on the original land value increment tax exemption for the whole parcel, not just the part whose use was changed. The court decided the letters do not conflict with the Constitution.","held":"The three Ministry of Finance letters, which set how the fine under Article 55-2 of the Land Tax Act is calculated, fit that article's purpose, are necessary to stop illegal use of farmland and promote the public interest, and do not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The state offers a land value increment tax exemption when farmland is transferred to farmers who farm it themselves, to keep and expand farm operating scale.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"If the land is later transferred to a non-farming person or changed to non-farm use without legal authority, the Land Tax Act Article 55-2 provides a fine of twice the exempted tax amount.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Agricultural Development Act sets a principle that each parcel of farmland may not be divided, so changing part of a parcel to non-farm use without legal basis is also not allowed.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The letters say the fine is based on the exempted tax for the whole land, not in proportion to the area wrongly used. This was an interpretation within the agency's authority that fits Article 55-2.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"This method is necessary to deter illegal use of farmland and advance the public interest, so it is not unconstitutional.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The court added that the competent authority should still review whether fines of different amounts should apply depending on how serious the violation is.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Owners of farmland changed to non-farm use","Farmers who receive farmland under the tax exemption","Ministry of Finance and tax authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether, after the Constitution took effect, the secretaries-general (書記長) of political parties' offices were public officials. The court decided they should not be regarded as public officials. The paragraphs give no reasons for this conclusion.","held":"After the Constitution took effect, the secretaries-general of political parties and of party offices at every level may not be regarded as public officials.","points":[],"who":["Political party secretaries-general","Secretaries-general of party offices at all levels"],"covered":false}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a rule in the Wrongful Imprisonment Compensation Act is constitutional. The rule denied compensation to people who were detained but then not prosecuted or found not guilty, if their conduct violated public order or good morals. The court found the rule does not fully fit the constitution's proportionality principle and ordered that the conflicting part not be applied.","held":"Article 2, item 2, first part of the Act, to the extent it conflicts with this ruling, is not to be applied. It denies compensation based only on a violation of public order or good morals, without considering how serious the conduct was or whether it went beyond what society commonly tolerates.","points":[{"text":"The Wrongful Imprisonment Compensation Act is a special law on state liability. Under Article 24 of the Constitution, the legislature must make state compensation laws, and the conditions they set for claims must meet the proportionality principle.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Detaining a criminal defendant seriously restricts personal freedom before a final guilty verdict, so compensation for detention must especially respect the constitution's protection of personal liberty.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The rule aims to protect social order and public morals, but it bars compensation merely because public order or good morals were violated, without asking whether the conduct was serious enough to be intolerable to society's common view.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Compared with the other grounds for denial in the same item and article, this ground is out of balance, so it does not fully fit the proportionality principle.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The Review Committee's decisions are treated as equal to final court judgments, so people may ask for a constitutional interpretation of the laws those decisions applied.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["People detained but then not prosecuted or acquitted","Claimants for wrongful imprisonment compensation","Officials deciding compensation claims"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a court precedent that barred public servants from challenging decisions affecting their property rights was unconstitutional. The court said public servants who are dismissed under the civil service performance appraisal law may bring an administrative lawsuit, but other appraisal results that leave their status unchanged still cannot be challenged that way. It also said a public servant whose property claim, based on a final appraisal result, is refused may file an administrative appeal or lawsuit, and the old precedent no longer applies to the extent it conflicts.","held":"A dismissal under the performance appraisal law can be challenged in an administrative lawsuit, but other appraisal results that do not change status cannot. A public servant whose property claim based on a final appraisal result is refused may seek an administrative appeal or lawsuit, and the 1959 Administrative Court precedent (No. 11) is no longer to be applied where it conflicts with this.","points":[{"text":"Whether a public servant can sue over an administrative decision depends on what the decision does, in keeping with the constitutional protection of people's rights.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"A dismissal changes the person's status and directly affects the constitutional right to hold public office, so the dismissed public servant may bring an administrative lawsuit.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Appraisal results that do not change status still cannot be challenged through an administrative lawsuit.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Refusal of a property claim based on a final appraisal result affects the property right, so an administrative appeal or lawsuit is not ruled out.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The 1959 precedent treated disputes within a special power relationship or private-law employment as barred from appeal, and to the extent it conflicts with this reasoning it is no longer to be applied.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Whether a claim is truly based on a final appraisal result is a question of fact to be decided case by case and is outside this interpretation.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Public servants dismissed under the performance appraisal law","Public servants refused property claims based on final appraisal results","Public servants with other appraisal results that don't change status","Administrative courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an Executive Yuan order and an Interior Ministry letter were unconstitutional for using a fixed sum to estimate a tenant farmer's living costs. The court found that this method was unrealistic and unreasonable and conflicted with the Constitution's protection of farmers. It ruled that the order and letter should no longer be applied.","held":"The Executive Yuan order and the Interior Ministry letter, which applied a fixed-amount minimum living cost standard to work out a tenant's family living expenses, do not fit the Constitution's aim of protecting farmers and may no longer be applied.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution protects the right to live and requires the state to protect farmers and improve their livelihood.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The Land Rent Reduction Act's rule barring a landlord from taking back land when the tenant would lose the family's livelihood aims to protect tenant farmers from serious harm to their family life and survival.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The order and letter used a fixed, unchanging sum from a military service classification table to estimate the tenant's living costs.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"This method ignored price differences between regions and each farm family's actual income, spending and hardship, such as medical and insurance costs.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"So the method is not close to reality, is unreasonable, and conflicts with the Constitution's protection of farmers.","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["Tenant farmers","Landlords seeking to take back leased land","Farm families dependent on rented land"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本號解釋處理的問題是：依法應在審判期日調查的證據卻沒有調查，確定判決是否算違背法令。大法官表示，如果因此造成適用法令錯誤，而且明顯影響判決結果，該確定判決就是判決違背法令，可以適用刑事訴訟法第四百四十七條第一項第一款的規定。","held":"依法應於審判期日調查的證據未調查，導致適用法令違誤，且顯然影響判決者，該確定判決即屬判決違背法令，應適用刑事訴訟法第四百四十七條第一項第一款。","points":[{"text":"刑事訴訟的目的在確定國家具體刑罰權，以發現真實，使刑罰權能正確行使。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"非常上訴是對審判違背法令的確定判決所設的救濟方法。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"審判違背法令可分為判決違法與訴訟程序違法：前者可撤銷原判決另行判決，具有實質上的效力；後者僅撤銷程序。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"兩者理論上可以區分，實際上常相牽連。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"應調查的證據未調查，致適用法令違誤而顯然影響判決結果，若不救濟，就無法維持刑罰權的正確行使，因此屬判決違背法令，而非僅是訴訟程序違法。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["刑事案件的被告","受確定判決的人","刑事審判法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是施行細則規定，被繼承人重病無法處理事務期間所舉的債務或出售財產所得，若繼承人不能證明用途，仍要列入遺產課稅，這是否違憲。大法官認為這項規定沒有牴觸憲法第十九條，因為它是為了正確認定課稅遺產、防止逃漏稅及維持課稅公平，並未增加法律所定的納稅義務。","held":"遺產及贈與稅法施行細則第十三條的規定，並未增加法律所定人民之納稅義務，與憲法第十九條並無牴觸；至於具體案件有無應稅遺產，仍依舉證責任分配法則，由稅捐稽徵機關或納稅義務人各自負舉證責任。","points":[{"text":"遺產及贈與稅法規定遺產應課稅，繼承人有申報繳納義務，且被繼承人死亡前確實證明的未償債務可從遺產總額中扣除。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"被繼承人重病無法處理事務時所舉的債或出售財產，依一般情形難以自行處理所得款項，因此應由繼承人證明款項用途，以防繼承人藉被繼承人名義舉債或賣財產來隱匿遺產。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"施行細則第十三條是為貫徹該法第一條及第十七條第一項第八款而訂，目的在兼顧繼承人利益與認定課稅遺產之正確，並為防止逃漏稅及維持課稅公平所必要。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"此規定並未增加法律所定人民之納稅義務，因此與憲法第十九條並無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"具體案件有無應稅遺產，仍應依舉證責任分配法則，由稅捐稽徵機關或納稅義務人負舉證責任。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["被繼承人之繼承人","納稅義務人","稅捐稽徵機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the government could use an enforcement regulation and a Ministry of Finance letter to set which interest income is tax-exempt under the Statute for Encouragement of Investment. The court decided that doing so by regulation, when the statute simply said 'all kinds of interest', went against the constitutional principle that taxes must rest on law.","held":"The enforcement rules and the Ministry of Finance letter, which defined the scope of exempt interest and excluded interest on private loans, conflict with the statute's words 'all kinds of interest'. They therefore violate Article 19 of the Constitution, even if they fit the aim of encouraging investment.","points":[{"text":"Under Article 19 of the Constitution, people pay tax according to law, which covers both what is taxed and what is exempt; both must be set out clearly in a statute.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Enforcement rules may only deal with matters of carrying out the parent law; where tax or exemption scope is involved, the law itself must decide it.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The statute exempted 'all kinds of interest' except postal savings and short-term bills, and did not exclude private non-investment loan interest, yet the rules and letter excluded private loan interest.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Serving the goal of encouraging investment does not justify setting this by regulation when it conflicts with the statute's explicit wording.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The statute was later amended to list exempt interest and the rule was deleted, so the letter no longer applies, but the court still interpreted it because an earlier interpretation gives effect to the applicant's own case.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Taxpayers claiming interest exemptions","Private lenders","Tax authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance rule on managing cargo containers is unconstitutional. The rule lets customs stop accepting a container depot's applications to bring in goods for a period of time when goods go missing from the depot. The court held that customs may do this because it is needed for the public interest, but the period has no maximum length, so a law or a law-authorized order must set limits by the end of 1994 or the rule stops applying.","held":"Article 26 (first part) of the Customs Container Management Rules is acceptable in letting customs suspend a depot's intake applications for a set period after goods go missing. However, the period has no maximum, so a law or law-authorized order must set it by December 31, 1994, or the suspension rule stops applying.","points":[{"text":"Depots are licensed and registered with customs, and their work is closely tied to customs inspection and anti-smuggling duties, which is why the Finance Ministry made rules making depots responsible for stored goods.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"When stored goods go missing, smuggling or other illegal acts may occur, so customs may suspend intake to protect its monitoring of stored goods and prevent smuggling.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Suspension pushes depots to improve their facilities or management and stops harm from continuing or growing, so it serves the public interest and fits customs' legal duties.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The rule sets no maximum length for the suspension, so the period must be set by a law or law-authorized order, drawing on Article 63 of the Shipping Act, to match Article 23 of the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Because depot operators must give customs a written guarantee, public-law contract issues arise, and the relevant bodies should promptly legislate basic rules for them, in line with administration according to law.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The part making the depot pay import duties needs no new interpretation, since the depot is the holder when the shortage occurs and Interpretation No. 219 applies.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Container depot operators","Customs authorities","Importers whose goods are stored in depots"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case challenged Taiwan's Urban Renewal Act, under which owners can apply to government to carry out urban renewal projects that can affect other owners' property and homes. The court found that the procedures for approving a project outline and a project plan, and the low consent threshold for applying for outline approval, did not meet constitutional due process. It upheld the higher consent thresholds for approving project plans and a special rule for disaster areas.","held":"The rules on approving renewal outlines and plans, and the one-tenth consent threshold for outline applications, are unconstitutional because they fail due process and harm property and residence rights; the authorities must fix them within one year or those parts lose effect. The consent thresholds for plan approval and the disaster-area rule (limited to its stated conditions) were held constitutional.","points":[{"text":"Property rights and the freedom of residence can be limited by law only for the public good and within the proportionality principle.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Approving a renewal outline or plan is an administrative act that limits property and residence rights, and can even lead to loss of rights and forced moves.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Due process requires a fair, professional and diverse review body, ways for interested people to learn the information and state their views, and for plan approval a public hearing with reasons given for accepting or rejecting views.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The outline approval rules set up no proper review body and did not ensure interested people could learn the information; a public meeting was not enough to let them state views.","cites":["9"]},{"text":"A consent threshold of just over one-tenth for applying for outline approval is too low, lets a small minority force the majority into the process, and fails due process.","cites":["10"]},{"text":"The plan approval rules did not require individual delivery of information to other owners or a public hearing, so they fail due process.","cites":["11"]},{"text":"The plan-approval consent thresholds (all over one-half) serve legitimate aims and are proportionate, though they should be reviewed; the disaster-area rule is proportionate only within its stated limits.","cites":["13","14"]}],"who":["Owners of land and lawful buildings in renewal areas","Residents of renewal areas","Applicants and renewal implementers","Government renewal authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問，財政部對法院強制執行拍賣財產時，如何計算財產交易所得並課稅所作的函釋，是否違憲。大法官認為，法院依強制執行法拍賣所得的價金，應減除成本費用後計算財產交易所得，併同其他所得課稅。財政部該函釋沒有超出所得稅法的規定，也不牴觸憲法第十九條。","held":"法院依強制執行法拍賣，賣得價金應依所得稅法第十四條第一項第七類，減除成本費用後計算財產交易所得，併同其他各項所得課稅；財政部六十六年十一月二日函釋未逾越所得稅法規定，與憲法第十九條並不牴觸。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十九條規定人民有依法律納稅的義務，有中華民國來源所得的個人，應依所得稅法繳納綜合所得稅。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"財產及權利因交易而取得的所得，依所得稅法第二條第一項及第十四條第一項，應計入綜合所得總額課稅。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"法院依強制執行法拍賣債務人財產，賣得價金減除原始取得成本及取得、改良、移轉所支付的一切費用後如有餘額，仍是財產交易所得，應計入債務人的綜合所得總額課稅。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"財政部函釋認為房屋被法院查封拍賣，仍應依拍賣價額減除成本費用後計算所得並課稅，沒有超出所得稅法的規定，故不違反憲法第十九條。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["債務人","財產被法院強制執行拍賣的人","納稅義務人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether it is unconstitutional to revoke a driver's license, bar them from getting a new one for three years, and revoke all their license classes when they refuse an alcohol test. The court decided these rules do not violate the constitution's proportionality principle and are consistent with protecting freedom of movement and the right to work. It also suggested the legislature add more flexible rules for different situations.","held":"The rules revoking the license of a driver who refuses an alcohol test, barring a new license for three years, and revoking all license classes held do not violate the proportionality principle or the protection of freedom of movement and the right to work.","points":[{"text":"Freedom of movement, which includes driving, and the right to work are protected, but they can be limited by law if the constitution's requirements are met.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Drivers already have a legal duty to cooperate with alcohol tests, and police must first advise a person who refuses and explain the legal consequences.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The rules serve a legitimate purpose of traffic safety, and revoking licenses encourages drivers to take the test and helps curb drunk driving.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The rules are necessary because drivers might refuse tests to escape criminal punishment for drunk driving, and no milder measure was found that would work as well.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The harm to the driver is not clearly out of balance with the interests protected, since drunk driving endangers lives, safety and traffic order; professional drivers are held to higher standards and are warned beforehand, so the penalty is not excessive.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Although the rules pass, the legislature is encouraged to add provisions letting enforcers weigh individual circumstances, and to set testing methods and procedures in law or clearly authorized rules.","cites":["8"]}],"who":["Drivers who refuse alcohol tests","Professional drivers and people who depend on driving for work","Police officers enforcing alcohol tests","The legislature and the authorities responsible for the rules"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of the Interior circular was unconstitutional. The circular said that even when a main urban plan had been in force over two years, a building permit could be refused if the plan required a detailed plan first. The court held that this went beyond what the Urban Planning Act allows and conflicts with the constitutional protection of property, so it must not be applied.","held":"The Ministry of the Interior's 1984 circular, and the matching condition in the Miaoli County plan notice on issuing building permits, exceeds the law and conflicts with the constitutional protection of property rights, so it should not be applied.","points":[{"text":"The 'other matters to be stated' clause in the main plan covers only matters similar in nature to the items before it. It cannot be used to restrict or contradict matters the law already expressly provides for.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Restricting building and land alteration in areas without a detailed plan serves the public interest. But property rights cannot be left in limbo because the authority delayed issuing a detailed plan beyond two years.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So the proviso lets building authorities designate building lines and issue permits once the main plan has been published for over two years and a building line can be fixed or main public facilities are built. This lifts the building restriction and protects people's right to use their property.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"A main plan therefore cannot require that a detailed plan be completed before a permit is issued, because that would block the proviso from applying.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Ministry's circular and the Miaoli County notice condition on permits go beyond the Act and add a restriction the proviso does not contain. They conflict with property protection and should not be applied.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Landowners applying for building permits","Urban planning authorities","Building permit authorities","Local governments such as Miaoli County"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a member of the Control Yuan (a supervisory official) may also work as the publisher of a newspaper or magazine. The court decided that a publisher's work falls within the \"business\" that Article 103 of the Constitution bars these officials from doing.","held":"The work done by publishers of newspapers and magazines belongs within the scope of the \"business\" mentioned in Article 103 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Control Yuan members hold a supervisory post and are meant to stand in an impartial position, which is why Article 103 bars them from doing business.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Publishing a newspaper or magazine needs approval from an administrative authority, and publishers' work is supervised by that authority.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Because of this, the publisher's work is plainly incompatible with the supervisory powers of a Control Yuan member, so it falls within the business covered by Article 103.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Control Yuan members","Newspaper and magazine publishers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是行政法院一則決議認為，徵收補償費即使逾期未發給，已確定的徵收處分也不會因此失效。大法官認為，補償不僅要相當，還要儘速發給，補償費逾法定期限未發給時，徵收土地核准案應失其效力。該決議與此意旨不符的部分違反憲法保障人民財產權之意旨，不予適用。","held":"行政法院八十五年一月十七日庭長評事聯席會議決議中，認為逾期未發補償費也不會使徵收處分失效的部分，與本解釋意旨不符，違反憲法保障財產權之旨，不予適用。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十五條保障人民財產權；國家因公益徵收須給予合理補償，因為這是所有人為公共利益所受的特別犧牲。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"補償不僅要相當，還應儘速發給，以減少財產所有人的損害。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"土地法第二百三十三條規定補償費應於公告期滿後十五日內發給；經評定或評議而展延時，評定後通知與繳交的期限仍不得超過十五日。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"徵收程序要求嚴格，是為了在增進公益之餘兼顧確保人民財產權益；補償的發給與徵收處分的效力不可分。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"若補償數額過於龐大或有特殊情事而未能於十五日內發給，仍應於評定或評議結果確定之日起相當期限內儘速發給，否則徵收土地核准案即失其效力。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"因此該決議認為逾期也不會使徵收處分失效的部分，違反憲法保障人民財產權之旨，不予適用。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["被徵收土地的所有人","需用土地人（機關）","主管地政機關","行政法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在審查所得稅法施行細則規定，納稅義務人要減除其他親屬或家屬的扶養免稅額，必須與受扶養人登記在同一戶籍是否合憲。大法官認為，是否為家屬應看有無共同生活的客觀事實，不能只以戶籍為唯一標準。因此該細則要求「同一戶籍」的部分限縮了母法，違反租稅法律主義，不予援用。","held":"所得稅法施行細則第二十一條之二以「同一戶籍」為要件的部分，限縮母法適用，違反憲法第十九條租稅法律主義，與解釋意旨不符的部分不予援用。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十九條的租稅法律主義，要求稅捐構成要件都要由法律明定；施行細則只能規範實施母法的相關事項，不得增減或創設納稅義務及其要件。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"免稅額的目的是讓納稅義務人善盡對特定親屬或家屬的法定扶養義務，是其應享的優惠，若施行細則可任意增減要件，就不符租稅法律主義。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"所得稅法規定受扶養的其他親屬或家屬，除確係受扶養外，還須符合民法相關規定，即須具備家長家屬關係。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"民法上的家採實質認定，以永久共同生活為目的而同居為準，不一定要登記同一戶籍；例如警察人員的戶籍必須設在服務地區。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"施行細則以「同一戶籍」為唯一認定標準，使納稅義務人無法舉證證明受扶養人確為共同生活的家屬，限縮了母法，因此違憲而不予援用。","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["納稅義務人","受扶養的其他親屬或家屬","戶籍與家人不在同處的人（如警察人員）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether directors of state-run enterprises who represent private shareholders are covered by the Civil Servants Service Act when they are paid. The court said the earlier Interpretation No. 92 meant only those who receive a salary. Directors and supervisors who receive no salary are not covered.","held":"The Civil Servants Service Act applies to directors and supervisors representing private shares in public enterprises only if they receive a salary (俸給). Interpretation No. 92 is clarified accordingly.","points":[{"text":"Directors and supervisors representing private shares in a public enterprise are service personnel of that enterprise, so under Article 24 of the Civil Servants Service Act the Act should apply to them.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"However, that article is limited to service personnel of public enterprises who receive a salary, so those representing private shares who receive no salary are not covered by the Act.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"For this reason, Interpretation No. 92 needed to be supplemented and explained, and it was read as referring to salaried people.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Directors of public enterprises representing private shares","Supervisors of public enterprises representing private shares","Salaried personnel of public enterprises","Unsalaried private-share representatives"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the Code of Criminal Procedure's rule letting a court extend a suspect's detention by ruling is unconstitutional. The court decided that the rule does not conflict with Article 8 of the Constitution. It also added that the court's extension ruling should be made known to the accused in time.","held":"Article 108, paragraph 1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on court rulings extending detention, does not conflict with Article 8 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Article 8 of the Constitution protects personal freedom, and arrest or detention must follow legally set procedures by judicial or police authorities.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 108, paragraph 1 limits the length of detention to make those carrying out detention act carefully, and lets a court extend it by ruling before the period ends if continued detention is needed. This carries out the purpose of Article 8.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 8, paragraph 2 concerns arrest or detention by bodies other than courts, so it does not cover a court ruling extending detention. Therefore a court's detention does not raise the issue of giving written notice and applying for a writ of habeas corpus.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To protect personal freedom, a court's extension ruling should be made known to the accused in time, following the relevant Code of Criminal Procedure provisions.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["People detained on suspicion of a crime","Accused persons whose detention is extended","Courts ruling on detention"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a serving military officer may move to a civilian government job through \"outside-post suspension of service\" without breaking the constitutional rule that active-duty soldiers cannot hold civil office. The court decided this is not unconstitutional, because the officer is no longer an active-duty soldier once service is suspended. It also said the current arrangements should be thoroughly reviewed and set directly by law.","held":"Moving an officer who has the legal qualifications for a civil post, and who is under retirement age, into a civilian job suited to their expertise through outside-post suspension of service is not shown to conflict with the Constitution. The current practices should be reviewed and set directly by law.","points":[{"text":"Article 140 bars only soldiers currently serving from holding civil office at the same time, to prevent soldiers from meddling in politics and to protect normal democratic government.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Soldiers who have retired, been discharged or had service suspended and serve in the reserves have no military power, so there is no risk of political interference.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Under the cited service rules, an officer approved for a public post outside the military has service suspended, enters the reserves, and is placed under reserve management, so they are a reserve soldier and no longer in active service.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Such a move to a suitable civilian job differs from an active-duty soldier holding civil office, so it is hard to call it contrary to the Constitution.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The current rules only provide for \"suspension of service\" and do not directly provide for \"outside-post suspension,\" which appears only in the implementing rules.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Because those who move to civilian posts can return to active service or be promoted in rank, there is a worry that military and civil roles blur. When such a move is allowed and how return works concern personnel systems, so they should be reviewed and set by law.","cites":["2","5"]}],"who":["Active-duty military officers moving to civilian posts","Reserve soldiers on outside-post suspension","Civilian government agencies needing staff"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是國民大會議長、副議長可否由國庫支給報酬，以及可否兼任其他公職或執行業務。大法官認為，議長、副議長屬經常性職位，可由國庫支給固定報酬，立法院通過八十六年度總預算中的相關歲費、公費及特別費，與憲法並無牴觸。同時，由於其為憲法上的國家機關並領有定期報酬，除法律另有規定外，不得兼任其他公職或執行業務。","held":"立法院通過八十六年度中央政府總預算中，議長、副議長的歲費、公費及特別費部分，與憲法尚無牴觸；議長、副議長除法律另有規定外，不得兼任其他公職或執行業務。","points":[{"text":"憲法增修條文規定國民大會自第三屆起設議長、副議長，議長對外代表國大、對內綜理會務並主持會議，屬經常性職位，與一般代表不同，所以可由國庫支給固定報酬。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"報酬的項目及額度，在合理限度內屬立法機關的權限。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"先前相關解釋及報酬條例都是在增修條文修正前作成，未包括議長、副議長的報酬，因此立法院通過其歲費、公費及特別費與憲法尚無牴觸。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"今後修正國民大會代表報酬及費用支給條例時，應明定議長、副議長的部分，作為支給依據。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"議長、副議長是憲法上的國家機關，對外代表國大，職位經常性，且受有國庫定期支給的相當報酬，所以除法律另有規定外，不得兼任其他公職或執行業務。","cites":["3","5"]}],"who":["國民大會議長、副議長","國民大會代表","立法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及公務人員保險法對保險費繳付後可否返還，以及養老給付只規定給依法退休人員、未規定其他離職人員是否違憲。大法官認為保險費繳付後不得返還的規定並不違憲，但養老給付只給退休人員、未規範其他離職人員，與憲法保障財產權的意旨不符，應即檢討修正。","held":"保險費繳付後法律未規定可返還，與憲法並無牴觸；但第十六條第一項養老給付僅規定依法退休人員可請領，未規定其他離職人員，違反憲法第十五條保障財產權的意旨，應即檢討修正。","points":[{"text":"保險費由被保險人與政府按一定比例負擔，是承保機關給付保險的財務基礎。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"保險費繳付後即由承保機關運用於保險事務，並作為保險事故發生時的給付基金，除別有規定外不得請求返還，因此未規定返還並不違憲。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"保險費除作為個人給付的資金來源外，也用來分擔保險團體中其他成員的危險責任。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"養老保險部分，承保機關依規定須提撥一定比率作養老給付準備，這些準備的本利類似全體被保險人存款的累積，不是承保機關的資產。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"被保險人繳足一定年限保險費後離職，自有請求給付之權；現行規定只給依法退休人員、未規定其他離職人員，與憲法第十五條財產權保障意旨不符。","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"請領的要件和金額如何，屬於立法問題。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["公務人員保險的被保險人","繳足年限後離職的非退休人員","依法退休的公務人員","公務人員保險承保機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於行政法院就「判決所憑證物被偽造或變造」而提起再審時，要求須有罪判決確定等條件的判例，是否違憲。憲法法庭認為，再審是對確定裁判的非常救濟，會影響法秩序安定，因此可以限制提起要件。該判例符合此意旨，與憲法保障訴訟權的規定尚無牴觸。","held":"行政法院七十六年判字第一四五一號判例，要求證物偽造或變造須經有罪判決確定，或刑事訴訟不能開始或續行且非因證據不足，才可提起再審，與憲法第十六條保障訴訟權的規定尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"訴訟權受憲法第十六條保障，但訴訟應遵循的程序與要件，應由立法機關衡量訴訟性質，以法律作正當合理的規定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"判決確定後紛爭即告解決、法律秩序得以安定；再審是確定裁判的非常救濟，會影響法秩序安定，所以提起要件應有所限制。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"證物偽造或變造須是確實如此，不能只靠再審原告片面主張；確實與否，以有罪判決確定，或刑事訴訟不能開始或續行且非因證據不足為限。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"這些要件是立法機關為平衡法律安定性與裁判正確性所作的決定，應無違憲可言。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"行政訴訟舊法曾引用民事訴訟法第四百九十六條全條，可見行政訴訟與民事訴訟的再審要件相同。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"修正為現行第二十八條第七款後，仍沿用原文，修正理由也無刪除有罪判決確定等限制之意，所以該判例符合此意旨。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["提起再審之訴的當事人","行政法院","立法機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the chairman and general manager of a shipping company are criminally liable for professional negligence when a ship suffers a disaster at sea after the company issued a sailing notice. The court decided they are not automatically liable just because the notice was issued. They can be liable if their own negligence in urging the ship to sail caused the disaster.","held":"Issuing a sailing notice does not by itself make a shipping company's chairman or general manager criminally liable for professional negligence if the ship has a disaster. The exception is where they negligently pushed the ship to sail and that caused the harm.","points":[{"text":"The Maritime Law says only the ship's captain is responsible for commanding the ship.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Because the captain is employed by the company, he is still subject to the company's direction and supervision within the scope of his work.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Seamen's service rules require a sailing or moving notice from the company or its agent before a ship may sail or move.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The sailing notice only tells the ship it may sail, so issuing it in the course of their duties does not by itself make the chairman or general manager liable if a disaster follows.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Liability remains where their negligence in urging the ship to sail caused the disaster.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Shipping company chairmen","Shipping company general managers","Ship captains"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a rule implementing the Soldiers' Land Grant Certificate Handling Act was unconstitutional in how it defines \"officers without posts\" (無職軍官). The Act mentions such officers in Article 10 but does not define them. The court held that the implementing rule's definition is a supplementary rule that fits the Act's purpose and does not conflict with the Constitution.","held":"Article 3, item 16 of the Act's implementing rules, which defines an officer without a post, supplements the Act, does not go against its legislative purpose, and does not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Act was made to take back land grant certificates already issued and to pay compensation at different rates. Article 10 treats certain discharged officers without posts as if they had already received certificates, to protect their rights.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Act does not define \"officer without a post\", but its purpose points to the Executive Yuan's 1959 measures for handling officers without military posts.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Those measures list the kinds of people covered, limit them to people living in government-controlled areas up to 30 June 1958, and treat those who skipped the registration survey as discharged and not handled later.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The registration period ran from 8 June to 18 October 1959. The measures were repealed in 1964 once that period ended.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So the implementing rule, which requires registration on file by 18 October 1959, a discharge order, and confirmation of status by the Ministry of National Defense, is a supplementary rule needed to carry out the Act. It does not go against the Act's purpose or the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Former officers without posts who left their units in Taiwan","People claiming compensation under the Soldiers' Land Grant Certificate Handling Act","Officers who registered with the Ministry of National Defense by 18 October 1959"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A former conscript soldier was convicted by military courts of robbery (snatching property) together with a civilian, but the ordinary courts later acquitted the civilian of the same act. The Constitutional Court held that the military trial law allowing appeals to a higher ordinary court only on the ground that the judgment violated the law was not unconstitutional. It also held that the soldier must be able to seek a retrial because the two courts reached conflicting findings on the same facts.","held":"The rule that allows appeals to the High Court only for violation of law is not found contrary to the constitutional right to sue (Article 16). The petitioner may apply for a retrial of the military judgment at the Taiwan High Court Kaohsiung Branch within 30 days of service of this ruling; the remaining requests were not accepted.","points":[{"text":"The right to sue under Article 16 covers soldiers too, and military trials must meet the minimum of due process; fairness is required when a soldier is tried separately from a civilian co-offender.","cites":["19","21"]},{"text":"How appeal levels are designed, including the split between fact-finding and legal review, is mainly for the legislature.
