{"answer":"The case asked how the President of the Judicial Yuan, the Vice President, and the Grand Justices should be appointed if seats became vacant before the sixth-term Grand Justices' terms ended in 2003. The constitutional amendments did not say. The court decided that the President nominates and the Legislative Yuan must consent.","held":"Until the sixth-term Grand Justices' terms end in 2003, vacancies among the Grand Justices and the Judicial Yuan's President and Vice President are to be filled by Presidential nomination with the Legislative Yuan's consent.","points":[{"text":"The current amendments say nothing about how vacancies are filled before 2003, yet these offices are part of the constitutional system and have set powers, so their appointment cannot be left without a rule. The court must fill this gap in line with the constitution as a whole.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Across the constitution and its amendments, the President nominates and appoints, while consent comes from a body with a popular mandate. The consent body was first the Control Yuan, then the National Assembly.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The 2000 amendments reduced the National Assembly's role and moved consent for Judicial, Examination and Control Yuan appointments to the Legislative Yuan, so the National Assembly can no longer consent to these appointments.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Democratic government needs a popular basis to be legitimate, so the Legislative Yuan, as the representative body, must give consent. Consequently, when a vacancy affects the Judicial Yuan's normal operation, the President nominates and the Legislative Yuan consents.","cites":["2","6"]}],"who":["The President","The Legislative Yuan","Grand Justices and Judicial Yuan leaders","The National Assembly"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A court asked whether Taiwan's juvenile law is unconstitutional in how it handles teenagers who often skip school or run away from home and might commit crimes. The court said bringing such teenagers under the juvenile court system is not by itself unconstitutional. But it struck down the parts allowing them to be held in a juvenile detention center or sent to correctional education, because these limit personal freedom more than necessary.","held":"The rule putting habitually truant or runaway youths under the juvenile court is not clearly unconstitutional, though it is too broad and unclear and should be reviewed soon. The provisions allowing detention or correctional education for these youths lose effect within one month of the ruling.","points":[{"text":"The court accepted the request for review. It also covered the later detention and correctional education provisions because they are closely tied to the main rule.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The state has a special duty to protect children and youth and act in their best interests. Lawmakers have freedom in designing this, but it has limits.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Handling truant or runaway youths in juvenile court is a protective system lawmakers set up, so it is not simply unconstitutional. Provisions limiting constitutional rights still need separate review.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Detention in a juvenile detention center and correctional education are both judicial measures, held for up to six months and up to three years respectively.","cites":["6","7"]},{"text":"Placing youths who have not committed a crime in judicial facilities does not fit their best interests. Both measures confine them, so they face strict review.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Less restrictive options, such as placement in suitable welfare or care institutions, could achieve the goals. So the confinement fails the proportionality principle and conflicts with protection of youth personality rights.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The wording on 'frequent' truancy or running away is too broad, and the phrase on the risk of committing a crime is unclear, so the rule should be revised soon.","cites":["10"]}],"who":["Youths who often skip school or run away","Youths already detained or sent to correctional education under these rules","Juvenile court judges"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於商標法第二條第八款所說的「世所共知」到底指哪個範圍。大法官會議解釋認為，這是指在中華民國境內，一般人所共同知道的情形。","held":"商標法第二條第八款所稱「世所共知」，是指在中華民國境內，一般所共知者而言。","points":[{"text":"商標法是中央立法，適用於全國，商標註冊的效力也及於全國。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"商標法第三條各項都有「中華民國境內」的規定，可見該法以境內為範圍。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此第二條第八款的「世所共知」應解為中華民國境內一般所共知；院字第一００八號解釋之二是針對修正前商標法第二條第六款所作，應予補明。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["商標註冊申請人","商標權人","一般民眾"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a earlier court precedent was unconstitutional for saying state-run enterprises cannot be sued as defendants in administrative lawsuits. The court held that a group set up by law, which the government has legally given public authority over particular matters, can be a defendant in an administrative suit, but only for cases about administrative acts done using that authority. The part of the precedent that conflicts with this will no longer be followed.","held":"A lawfully established body that the government has given public authority for specific matters can be a defendant in administrative lawsuits, limited to cases about administrative acts it takes using that authority. The 1971 Administrative Court precedent (No. 232) is no longer to be applied to the extent it conflicts with this.","points":[{"text":"People who think a central or local government agency's administrative act is unlawful or improper and harms their rights or interests may file appeals and administrative lawsuits.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So the defendant in an administrative dispute should in principle be the government agency that made the decision, and bodies outside government generally cannot be defendants.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"However, a lawfully established body given public authority by a government agency for specific matters acts like a government agency within that authority, so it can be a defendant in cases about administrative acts using that authority.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The precedent said state-run enterprises set up under the Company Act are not government offices and so cannot be defendants; this broadly denied defendant capacity to all non-office bodies, which conflicts with the court's view, so that part is no longer applied.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Whether disputes under Article 84 of the Labor Standards Act belong in administrative or civil court is not covered by this ruling; if parties already got a final civil judgment, their right to sue was not harmed.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Bodies given public authority by government","People challenging administrative acts","State-run enterprises","Parties in Labor Standards Act Article 84 disputes"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Several people who finished prison terms for sex crimes, plus two judges, asked Taiwan's Constitutional Court whether forced treatment after a sentence, held until the risk of reoffending drops markedly, is constitutional. The court found the core rules mostly constitutional, including having no fixed maximum period and applying the rule to people who offended before mid-2006. It ruled that the procedures lack a hearing and defense counsel, and it said the system risks being too much like punishment, so the authorities must fix these.","held":"The rules on post-sentence forced treatment are not vague, and treatment lasting until the risk of reoffending drops markedly is not unconstitutional in itself. But the law must give the person a chance to appear or send counsel to court, with a defender if they cannot speak fully, and the authorities must revise this within 2 years. They must also adjust the system within 3 years so it is clearly separate from punishment and long-term cases are handled better.","points":[{"text":"Terms like 'risk of reoffending' and 'risk markedly reduced' are understandable and can be judged by experts and reviewed by courts, so they are not too vague.","cites":["35","36"]},{"text":"Forced treatment in a fixed place serves the especially important public interest of protecting people from sexual crimes, and no less restrictive method has been widely recognized as equally effective.","cites":["38"]},{"text":"No fixed maximum period is acceptable in general because the time needed differs by person, but very long or indefinite treatment could amount to life confinement and raises constitutional doubt, so more support measures and periodic judge review are needed.","cites":["41","42","43","44","45"]},{"text":"Applying the rule to people who offended before the 2006 change does not breach non-retroactivity because it depends on current risk, and their trust interest yields to the major public interest in safety.","cites":["49","50","51"]},{"text":"Because treatment greatly restricts liberty, the person must be able to appear or send counsel to court when treatment is ordered or stopped, with a defender if they cannot speak fully.","cites":["53","54"]},{"text":"In practice treatment is run by the same authority as punishment, in facilities attached to prisons, with uniform management and little detailed law, so it may drift toward punishment and must be clearly separated.","cites":["58","59","60","61"]}],"who":["People ordered into forced treatment after serving a sex-crime sentence","People who committed sex offenses before July 2006","Patients with mental disorders or cognitive impairments","Courts and agencies running treatment"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是高雄市於民國六十八年改制為直轄市後，是否仍適用台灣省內菸酒專賣暫行條例。大法官認為，該條例當時的施行區域包括高雄市，在施行區域未依法定程序變更前，仍應繼續適用於改制後的高雄市。","held":"台灣省內菸酒專賣暫行條例的施行區域在未依法定程序變更前，仍繼續適用於改制後的高雄市。","points":[{"text":"該條例公布施行時，其施行區域就包括高雄市在內的台灣省所屬各縣市。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"高雄市改制為直轄市後，這項法律的施行區域並未改變，在依法定程序變更前，條例仍適用於改制後的高雄市。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"行政院函所定原則，指冠有「台灣省」等名稱的中央法令於改制後的高雄市繼續適用，就此條例而言符合立法原意，也不違反中央法規標準法第十五條。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因行政區域變更使法規名稱與施行區域不符，宜由有關機關從速依法檢討修正，使名實相符。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["高雄市","有關機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Several courts asked Taiwan's Constitutional Court whether it is constitutional that anyone on parole who intentionally commits a new crime and gets a prison sentence must automatically have parole revoked and serve the rest of the old sentence. The court held that this automatic rule goes too far where the new sentence is suspended or is 6 months or less and there is no special need to send the person back. In those cases, the rule violates the principle of proportionality and the protection of personal liberty.","held":"Article 78(1) of the Criminal Code is unconstitutional insofar as it automatically revokes parole when the new sentence is suspended or 6 months or less in prison and there is no special-prevention need, and it loses effect from the date of the ruling. Until the law is amended, the authorities must decide case by case whether to revoke parole in such cases.","points":[{"text":"Personal liberty is protected, and any restriction must be proportionate; revoking parole sends a person back to prison, so it must meet that standard.","cites":["10","11"]},{"text":"Prison and parole both aim to help prisoners return to society; parole is a transition, and revocation is meant for people who prove unsuited to life in society.","cites":["12"]},{"text":"The rule serves an important legitimate purpose, returning unsuitable parolees to prison, but whether to revoke should depend on whether the person is still suited to society and has betrayed the purpose of parole.","cites":["13"]},{"text":"Where the new offense got a suspended sentence or 6 months or less, the authorities should examine each case for specific reasons, such as danger to society, risk of reoffending and signs of remorse, that call for return to prison.","cites":["13"]},{"text":"Automatic revocation without that examination is not necessary to achieve its purpose, so it violates proportionality and the protection of personal liberty to that extent.","cites":["14"]}],"who":["People on parole who commit a new intentional crime","People given a suspended sentence or 6 months or less for a new crime","Authorities deciding on parole revocation"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案審查菸酒稅法第二十一條：菸酒稅法施行前專賣的米酒，若超過原專賣價格出售，每瓶一律罰新臺幣二千元。大法官認為立法目的正當、處罰手段也有必要，但這種劃一的處罰方式在個案過苛時，法律沒有設調整機制，與比例原則尚有未符。有關機關應儘速修正，並至遲於解釋公布滿一年時停止適用。","held":"菸酒稅法第二十一條關於每瓶一律罰二千元的處罰方式，因未設適當調整機制，限制財產權顯不妥當，與憲法第二十三條比例原則尚有未符；有關機關應儘速修正，至遲於本解釋公布滿一年時停止適用。修正前，個案有處罰顯然過苛之虞者，應斟酌相關情狀另為符合比例原則的適當處置。","points":[{"text":"對違反行政法上義務處罰鍰，應依情節輕重使責罰相當；採固定方式計算罰鍰雖或非憲法所不許，仍應設適當調整機制，避免個案顯然過苛。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"該規定為穩定米酒價格、維持市場供需而設，立法目的正當，以罰鍰督促履行義務的手段也適合。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"立法者在處罰方式上有形成空間；因欠缺其他同樣有效的手段，且違法態樣與效果明確、易收遏阻之效，該規定屬維護公益的必要措施。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"但以單一標準按瓶計罰，行政機關或法院無從綜合個案情狀裁量，罰鍰金額可能無限擴大，造成個案顯然過苛，嚴重侵害財產權，而立法者未設調整機制，因此與比例原則不符。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"修正前，若有造成個案過苛處罰之虞，應依立法目的與個案實質正義，斟酌出售價格、販賣數量、實際獲利、影響交易秩序程度等情狀，另為適當處置。","cites":["3","7"]}],"who":["超過原專賣價格出售米酒者","受罰鍰處分的人民","行政機關與法院","立法者與有關機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是組織犯罪防制條例第三條第三項要求犯該罪者在刑期執行完畢或赦免後，一律令入勞動場所強制工作（三年或五年），是否違憲。憲法法庭認為這項規定不違反憲法第八條對人民身體自由的保障，也不違反第二十三條的比例原則。","held":"組織犯罪防制條例第三條第三項關於強制工作的規定，與憲法第八條人民身體自由之保障及第二十三條比例原則之意旨不相牴觸。","points":[{"text":"強制工作的目的，是讓有犯罪習慣者從事勞動，培養勤勞習慣與一技之長，使其日後重返社會能自立更生，達成教化、矯治。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"該條例規範的是三人以上、有內部管理結構、具集團性、常習性、脅迫性或暴力性的犯罪組織，與釋字第四七一號所處理、不問個人情況一律強制工作的規定不同。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"犯罪組織內部階層化、控制嚴密，對社會的危害、衝擊及對民主制度的威脅，遠超過一般非組織性犯罪。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"設強制工作可補充刑罰不足、協助再社會化，並有防制組織犯罪的功能，為維護社會秩序、保障人民權益所必要。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"同條第四項、第五項已有免予執行與免予繼續執行的規定，個別情況無必要者，可由法院斟酌裁處，所以不違反身體自由保障與比例原則。","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["犯組織犯罪防制條例第三條之罪者","犯罪組織的成員","檢察官與法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是直轄市的自治以中央頒行的行政命令為依據，是否違憲。大法官指出憲法第一百十八條明定直轄市自治以法律定之，但該法律迄未制定，現行制度都依中央頒行的法規運作。大法官要求斟酌實際狀況，從速制定直轄市自治的法律，在法律制定前，現行中央法規繼續有效。","held":"直轄市自治應依法律制定，應斟酌當前實際狀況制定直轄市自治之法律；在該法律未制定前，現行由中央頒行的法規繼續有效。","points":[{"text":"憲法第一百十八條明定直轄市的自治以法律定之，直轄市雖不必依省、縣自治相同的程序，仍應依憲法意旨制定法律實施。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"直轄市自治的法律迄未制定，現行直轄市各級組織及實施地方自治事項，都是依據中央頒行的法規進行。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"為貫徹憲法實施地方自治的意旨，應斟酌當前實際狀況，從速制定直轄市自治的法律，以謀求改進。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"在法律未制定前，直轄市的自治與地方行政事務不能中斷，所以現行中央頒行的法規應繼續有效。","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["直轄市","中央主管機關","直轄市居民"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked how a detained defendant in Taiwan can go to court when unhappy with a decision on their complaint about how the detention center treated them. The court said that until the detention rules are amended, such a defendant may seek relief from the court that ordered the detention, using the rules on a challenge to a court order (準抗告) in the Code of Criminal Procedure. This adds to an earlier ruling, Interpretation No. 653.","held":"Until the relevant rules are amended and promulgated, a detained defendant who disagrees with an authority's decision on their complaint may ask the court that ordered the detention for relief, using the Code of Criminal Procedure article 416 rules on challenges to court orders. Interpretation No. 653 is supplemented accordingly.","points":[{"text":"Detention seriously interferes with personal liberty, so a detainee who says the detaining authority's adverse decision went beyond what was needed for the detention's purpose or the order of the facility, and unlawfully harmed constitutional rights, should be able to seek court relief.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Interpretation No. 653 already found that the provisions barring detainees from suing in court conflict with the constitutional protection of the right to bring lawsuits, and told the authorities to revise the rules within two years.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"That two-year period expired long ago and the rules were still not amended.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To protect the litigation rights of detainees unhappy with the treatment or measures of the detention center, the court allows court relief in the meantime through the challenge-to-court-order rules, before the court that ordered detention.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The petitioner may seek relief over the isolation measure and the complaint decision in the underlying case within five days after this interpretation is served.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Detained defendants","Detention centers and related authorities","Courts that order detention","The petitioner in the underlying case"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a public official who holds a second post under a law or regulation may receive the public expense allowance attached to that second post. The court said yes where the official's main post has no such allowance but the second post does. The official still may not collect a second salary or a second allowance where the main post already provides one.","held":"Under Article 14, paragraph 2 of the Civil Servant Service Act, an official holding a concurrent post under law may receive only the salary and allowance of the main post. If the main post has no public expense allowance but the concurrent post does, the official may receive the concurrent post's allowance.","points":[{"text":"The question was whether an official serving in a concurrent post under law or regulation may receive that post's public expense allowance.","cites":["1"]},{"text":"The rule against receiving a second salary or a second allowance for a concurrent post is read to mean the official can draw only the main post's salary and allowance.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"Because of that reading, an official whose main post has no allowance but whose concurrent post has one may receive the concurrent post's allowance.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Public officials holding concurrent posts under law","Public officials whose main post has no public expense allowance"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭執財政部依保險法授權所訂的保險代理人經紀人公證人管理規則，其中關於警告、停止執業、撤銷執業證書等裁罰性處分的規定是否違憲。大法官認為，這類處分限制人民權利，構成要件與法律效果應由法律規定，或由法律具體明確授權；保險法第一百七十七條並未具體授權，因此該規定與憲法保障人民權利的意旨不符，須在一年內失效。","held":"管理規則第四十八條第一項第十一款對保險代理人、經紀人及公證人等從業人員訂定裁罰性行政處分，與憲法保障人民權利的意旨不符，自解釋公布日起至遲屆滿一年時失效。","points":[{"text":"對違反行政法上義務者作裁罰性處分，涉及權利限制，其構成要件與法律效果應由法律規定；若授權命令補充，授權的目的、範圍及內容須具體明確，才符合憲法第二十三條。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"若只是概括授權，所訂命令只能規定細節性、技術性事項，不能超出授權而自行訂定裁罰性處分條款。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"保險法第一百七十七條雖讓主管機關訂定管理規則作必要規範，但並未就處罰的構成要件與法律效果作具體明確授權。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"警告、停止執業、撤銷執業證書都屬裁罰性行政處分，涉及權利限制，管理規則該款超越授權自行規定，因此與憲法意旨不符。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"考量規定的必要性及修法所需時間，該款不立即失效，而是至遲於公布日起屆滿一年時失效；管理規則其他裁罰性處分也應從速檢討修正。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["保險代理人","保險經紀人","保險公證人","財政部"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a 2003 resolution of Taiwan's Supreme Administrative Court was unconstitutional. The resolution said that if a person made a gift before death and the tax office had not yet issued a gift tax bill, the heirs should be treated as the taxpayers and be billed for gift tax. The court found the resolution went beyond the law and added a tax duty the law does not provide, so it can no longer be applied.","held":"The part of the resolution making heirs the gift-tax taxpayers, where no bill had been issued by the date of inheritance, goes beyond Article 15 of the Estate and Gift Tax Act and conflicts with Articles 19 and 15 of the Constitution. It may not be applied from the date of this interpretation.","points":[{"text":"A Supreme Administrative Court resolution that courts rely on in judgments is treated like an administrative order, so it can be reviewed, and the request was accepted.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 19 requires the key elements of a tax to be set by statute. Orders or resolutions cannot go beyond the law or add tax duties the law does not contain.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Article 15 of the Estate and Gift Tax Act only treats gifts made shortly before death as part of the estate for estate tax. It does not make heirs the taxpayers for gift tax on gifts not yet billed.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Under Article 14 of the Tax Collection Act, heirs and others pay the deceased's unpaid tax from the estate as substitute payers, not as inheriting taxpayers. They become liable themselves only if they break that rule.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Other rules already cover collection: enforcement against the estate, and the recipient as taxpayer if the donor has no property available.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"So the resolution added a tax duty for heirs that the law does not provide, which conflicts with the Constitution. The court did not need to decide the equality question.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["Heirs of people who made gifts before death","Executors, legatees and estate administrators","Recipients of gifts","Tax collection authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是行政院聲請解釋，質疑通傳會組織法第4條有關通傳會委員由各政黨依立法院席次比例推薦、並由審查會審查的選任方式，以及第16條的覆審規定是否違憲。憲法法庭認為委員選任的相關規定幾乎完全剝奪行政院的人事決定權，違反責任政治與權力分立原則，也不符通訊傳播自由的意旨，須限期失效。至於委員由行政院院長任命的規定與第16條覆審規定，則未被認定違憲。","held":"通傳會組織法第4條第2、3、4、6項有關委員選任的規定違憲，至遲於97年12月31日失效，失效前通傳會所作行為的適法性不受影響；第4條第3項後段、第5項及第16條則未違憲。","points":[{"text":"行政院為最高行政機關，基於行政一體與責任政治，須為所屬機關施政負責，因此應保有對通傳會委員的人事決定權；立法院可制衡，但不能實質剝奪或取而代之。","cites":["2","7","8","10"]},{"text":"依系爭規定，行政院院長只能推薦18名候選人中的3名，審查階段無從表示意見，還受審查會名單拘束，人事決定權幾近完全被剝奪，牴觸責任政治與權力分立。","cites":["12"]},{"text":"由各政黨依席次比例推薦委員及組成審查會，等於把人事權移給政黨，反而讓政黨積極介入，影響人民對通傳會超越政治的信賴，違背獨立機關的目的與通訊傳播自由的意旨。","cites":["9","13"]},{"text":"通傳會屬獨立機關，憲法第56條的規範範圍不及於獨立機關，故委員由行政院院長任命、正副主委由委員互選再任命，並不違反該條。","cites":["14"]},{"text":"第16條的覆審是立法者基於制度變革等政策考量所設的特別救濟，立法者對訴願制度有廣泛形成空間，且回復原狀或補償的配套設計也未逾越憲法容許範圍。","cites":["15","16"]},{"text":"因修法需要時間，規定若立即失效會使通傳會職權停擺，不利人民通訊傳播自由，故給予至97年12月31日的緩衝期，期間內通傳會的行為仍有效。","cites":["17"]}],"who":["行政院","立法院與各政黨（團）","通傳會委員","受特定不利處分而申請覆審的人民"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論被依法通緝的人，其時效是否停止計算。大法官認為，審判中的被告被依法通緝時，追訴權時效應停止進行；執行中的受刑人被依法通緝，致無法開始或繼續執行時，行刑權時效也應停止進行。但停止期間仍須注意刑法第八十五條第三項的限制。","held":"審判中被告經依法通緝，追訴權時效停止進行，院字第一九六三號解釋未變更；執行中受刑人經依法通緝，不能開始或繼續執行時，行刑權時效也停止進行，但仍須注意刑法第八十五條第三項規定。","points":[{"text":"被告不到庭原則上不能審判，被告逃亡或藏匿時可以通緝，所以審判中被告被通緝，審判程序無法開始或繼續，追訴權時效應停止進行。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"關於追訴權時效，仍須注意刑法第八十三條第三項的規定；院字第一九六三號第一項的解釋至今未變更。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"為強制受刑人到場，執行時可依法通緝，相關刑事訴訟法規定對此十分明確。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"受刑人因有到場受執行之必要而逃亡或藏匿，經依法通緝，致無法開始或繼續執行時，依刑法第八十五條第一項，行刑權時效應停止進行。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"停止原因持續的期間，仍須適用同條第三項；達到第八十四條第一項各款所定期間四分之一時，停止原因視為消滅，若仍未行使且無其他停止原因，時效即恢復進行。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["審判中被通緝的被告","執行中被通緝的受刑人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a 2007 amendment to the Bookkeeper Act (記帳士法), Article 2, paragraph 2, was unconstitutional. The amendment let people who were registered as bookkeeping and tax-filing agents, but had never passed the state exam, swap their registration for a bookkeeper certificate. The court held that this conflicts with the Constitution's requirement that professionals be qualified through exams run by the Examination Yuan, so the provision loses effect.","held":"Article 2, paragraph 2 of the Bookkeeper Act gave non-exam-qualified agents the same status as exam-qualified bookkeepers, which goes against Article 86, item 2 of the Constitution. It ceases to have effect from the day the interpretation was announced.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution requires professionals to get their practice qualification through exams the Examination Yuan runs under the law.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Bookkeepers are a type of professional, because the work covers business accounting, registration, tax filing and tax advice. It is broader than ordinary business accounting work and affects taxpayers' property rights and the public interest in tax collection and business administration.","cites":["3","4"]},{"text":"The provision let agents who never passed the exam switch their registration for a certificate and gain the same qualification as exam-passed bookkeepers.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Their expertise had not been verified by exam, yet they would practice under the bookkeeper title. Consumers could not tell the difference, so their interests are hard to protect, and it is unfair to those who passed the exam.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Article 35 of the Act, which lets existing agents keep practicing by registration, was not under review and the ruling does not decide on it.","cites":["6"]}],"who":["Registered bookkeeping and tax-filing agents without exam qualification","Exam-qualified bookkeepers","Consumers who use bookkeepers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the voluntary retirement rules in the Taiwan Province Factory Workers Retirement Rules conflict with the Constitution. The court decided they do not conflict with it. It reasoned that the rules protect workers and also help factories run well.","held":"The provisions on voluntary retirement of workers in the Taiwan Province Factory Workers Retirement Rules do not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution calls for laws and policies protecting labor, and for labor and management to cooperate to develop production.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The provincial government may make separate rules to protect workers and promote labor-management cooperation when central rules are incomplete, as long as they do not conflict with them.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Ministry of the Interior's enforcement rules under the Factory Act already require factory rules to state retirement, pension, severance and welfare matters.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The voluntary retirement provisions support workers' livelihood after retirement, so they fit the constitutional policy of protecting labor.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"They also renew the workforce, raise productivity and encourage dedicated service, which benefits factories and fits the constitutional spirit of labor-management cooperation.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Factory workers","Factory operators","Taiwan Province government"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問財政部一則函釋是否違憲。該函釋說，生產事業除自行生產產品的所得外，兼營非自行生產產品買賣的所得及非營業收入，不適用獎勵投資條例的納稅限額規定。大法官認為這則函釋沒有違反憲法的租稅法定主義。","held":"財政部六十六年十二月十四日臺財稅字第三八四五二號函，是主管機關依職權所作的釋示，符合獎勵投資條例的意旨，未變更法律規定的稅賦優惠，也未增加生產事業的租稅負擔，與憲法租稅法定主義並無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"獎勵投資條例是為獎勵投資、加速國家經濟發展而制定，主要以稅捐減免優惠作為獎勵方法。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因經濟發展需求會變動，條例第三條第三項及第十五條授權行政院規定獎勵類目及標準，符合者才能享受第十五條第一項的租稅優惠。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"該函釋是主管機關基於職權，為執行第十五條及行政院依第三條授權發布的「生產事業獎勵類目及標準」，對計算全年課稅所得額所作的釋示。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"該函釋與條例把稅捐減免優惠限於受獎勵生產事業自行生產獎勵類目產品所得的意旨相符，沒有變更法律的優惠規定，也沒有增加租稅負擔，所以不違反租稅法定主義。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["受獎勵的生產事業","兼營非自行生產產品買賣的生產事業","財政部等稅務主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於土壤及地下水污染整治法第48條，要求在該法施行前就已造成污染的行為人，對施行後仍然存在的污染狀況負整治義務，是否違憲。憲法法庭認為，這項規定只規範施行後仍繼續存在的污染狀況，沒有違反法律不溯及既往原則，也沒有違反比例原則，與憲法第15條保障工作權及財產權的意旨並無違背。","held":"土污法第48條中「於本法施行前已發生土壤或地下水污染之污染行為人適用之」部分，是針對施行後污染狀況仍繼續存在的情形而規範，未牴觸法律不溯及既往原則及憲法第23條比例原則，也不違背憲法第15條保障工作權、財產權的意旨。","points":[{"text":"整治義務是以仍繼續存在的污染狀況為對象，不論污染行為發生在施行前或施行後；施行前的污染若施行後已不存在，就不適用，所以不算溯及既往。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"施行前的污染行為本來就是非法，污染行為人沒有值得保護的信賴，因此不需要制定過渡條款或其他補救措施。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"要求整治、支付費用及停業、停工等義務，限制了工作權、財產權及營業自由，所以必須符合比例原則。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"規定的目的是整治污染、維護環境與國民健康，目的正當，手段也有助於達成目的。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"若不要求施行前的污染行為人負責，危害會由其他人或國家承擔，有違社會正義並衝擊財政，且沒有侵害較小而效果相同的手段，所以是必要手段。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"現存污染危害健康與環境，必須整治；且污染行為原本非法，本應負除去責任，對財產權等的限制與公共利益之間並非顯失均衡。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["施行前的污染行為人","土壤及地下水受污染地區的國民","國家及其他可能分擔整治負擔的人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance directive explaining what counts as a government 'affordable-price' public housing unit for a property tax cut was unconstitutional. The court decided the directive does not conflict with the Constitution. It reasoned that the directive stayed within the purpose and wording of the law.","held":"The 1975 Ministry of Finance directive explaining the meaning of this kind of public housing, for the half-rate house tax under Article 15, paragraph 2, item 1 of the House Tax Act, does not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution requires paying taxes according to law, which covers both the scope of taxation and of exemption, and both must follow the written law. But when applying the law raises doubt, the responsible agency may interpret it in line with the legislature's purpose.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The half-rate house tax for government affordable-price public housing was meant to ease the burden on low-income people's homes, so it covers only housing sold at affordable prices to them, not homes the government sells otherwise.","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"The Ministry issued its directive to avoid doubt in applying the law, based on the legislative intent and the social and economic conditions of the time. It set conditions on size, buyer eligibility and price, and serves as a standard for finding the facts.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Because the directive did not go beyond what the law provides, it does not conflict with the Constitution.","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"The standard should be adjusted reasonably as conditions change, and the Ministry has since set other standards for particular cases, such as rebuilt housing for households whose illegal structures were demolished.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Low-income people buying government public housing","Owners of affordable-price public housing","Ministry of Finance and tax authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of the Interior circular was unconstitutional. The circular set a time limit for landowners to ask the government to expropriate the leftover part of their land as well. The court decided the circular does not conflict with the Constitution.","held":"The circular says a request for joint expropriation of the remaining land should be made from the time of negotiation until one year after expropriation is completed, and late requests are not accepted. The court held this is necessary to carry out Article 217 of the Land Act and does not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Article 217 of the Land Act lets an owner request expropriation of a leftover part that is too small or oddly shaped to be used properly, but it sets no time limit for the request.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Article 219 of the Land Act lets the original owner take back the land at the original price if it is not used as planned, or not put to use within one year after expropriation is completed.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So an owner's request for joint expropriation cannot be without a time limit, and the limit cannot be longer than the one in Article 219.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Without a limit, the agency needing the land could not use it under the approved plan within the legal period, which would harm the public interest and delay settling people's rights.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Ministry's circular carries out the intent of Article 219 and is necessary to carry out Article 217, so it does not conflict with the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Landowners whose land is expropriated","Owners of leftover land parcels","Government agencies that need land","Ministry of the Interior"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"聲請人的未成年女兒遭3名少年侵害，案件由少年法院依少年保護事件處理，但被害人及其法定代理人沒有到庭陳述意見的機會。憲法法庭認為，少年事件處理法第36條及相關規定整體上未明文賦予被害人到庭陳述意見的機會，不符正當法律程序原則，也違反保障被害人程序參與權的意旨。","held":"少年事件處理法第36條及其他少年保護事件相關規定，整體上未明文規範被害人（及其法定代理人）得到庭陳述意見，在此範圍內違憲。有關機關應自解釋公布日起2年內修法；修法前，少年法院除有正當事由認不適宜外，應傳喚被害人（及其法定代理人）到庭並給予陳述意見的機會。","points":[{"text":"被害人（含少年事件被害人）雖非訴訟當事人，但屬重要關係人，依正當法律程序原則應享有程序參與權，到庭陳述意見是其基本內涵；少年保護事件的被害人在不牴觸立法目的的範圍內，也應享有此權利。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"國家對少年的健全成長負有特別保護義務，少事法的目的是健全少年自我成長、調整成長環境與矯治性格。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"被害人到庭陳述，有助於法院釐清事實，也有助於法院採取適當的保護措施，促成少年健全成長；少事法本來就賦予被害人獨立的程序地位與權利，所以立法者除保護少年外，也應使被害人至少有到庭陳述意見的機會，非有正當事由且符合比例原則，不得一律排除。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"第36條只規定少年的法定代理人、現在保護少年之人及輔佐人可陳述意見，未納入被害人；其他條文雖可能因徵求同意而使被害人到庭，但不是常態性權利，因此被害人可能無法適當表達意見，也無法協助法院。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"法庭因此宣告在此範圍內違憲，要求2年內修法，修法前由少年法院傳喚被害人到庭，並應斟酌少年健全成長的立法意旨決定陳述方式。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["少年事件被害人","被害人的法定代理人","少年保護事件中的少年","少年法院"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及考試院修正發布的考試法施行細則，規定公務人員考試及格者，若要同時取得專門職業及技術人員考試及格資格，總成績須達到後者的錄取標準。大法官認為，當時有效的考試法第七條已規定及格人員同時取得兩種資格，施行細則增設法律所無的限制，與法律不符，也違反憲法保障人民權利的意旨，依憲法第一百七十二條應不予適用。","held":"考試法施行細則第九條第二項要求公務人員考試及格者須達專門職業及技術人員考試錄取標準，才能同時取得兩種資格，增設法律所無的限制，與法律不符並違憲法保障人民權利之意旨，應不予適用。","points":[{"text":"人民依法參加考試，是取得公務人員任用資格或專門職業及技術人員執業資格的必要途徑；這些資格關係工作權，受憲法保障，不得逕以命令限制。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"考試法第七條規定兩種考試應考資格及應試科目相同者，及格人員同時取得兩種資格，原意是避免應考人分別應試的麻煩。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"法律並未要求兩種考試的錄取標準必須相同，所以標準不同時，對公務人員考試錄取者，難以不讓其兼取專門職業及技術人員考試及格資格。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"如認為該條規定不夠周全，應先修正法律；考試院曾提出修正草案，但立法院議決維持原條文，不予修正。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"考試院仍以施行細則增設法律所無的限制，使同為公務人員考試錄取的人，有的不能同時取得兩種資格，與當時有效的法律不符，並違反憲法保障人民權利的意旨，故依憲法第一百七十二條不予適用。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["參加公務人員考試的應考人","公務人員考試及格人員","專門職業及技術人員考試應考人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether \"clerical workers\" (事務性工人) count as \"workers\" under the Factory Act's enforcement rules. The court decided they do, as long as they are hired by an employer, work at the factory's work site or business site, and earn wages. The definition is not limited to people doing manufacturing, processing, repair or dismantling.","held":"A \"worker\" means anyone hired who does work and earns wages, not only those in manufacturing, processing, repair or dismantling. Clerical workers hired by an employer and working at the factory's work or business site for wages are included.","points":[{"text":"The meaning of \"worker\" under the Factory Act has changed over time. An older 1932 enforcement rule defined it more strictly, as people directly doing or assisting production work.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The 1975 amendment widened the Act's reach by dropping the 30-worker minimum and applying it to all factories using power-driven machines. The old enforcement rule was repealed and the Ministry of the Interior was authorized to make new enforcement rules.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To carry out the amendment's purpose, the 1976 enforcement rules, modeled on the Labor Safety and Health Act, defined workers more broadly in Article 3 as those hired to work who earn wages.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"So anyone hired by an employer who works at the factory's work site or business site (including an office) for wages counts, not just those in manufacturing, processing, repair or dismantling.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Taiwan Province factory worker retirement rules, as amended in 1979, use the same definition in their Article 3, so clerical workers are included there too.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Clerical workers in factories","Factory employers","Factory workers covered by the retirement rules"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭執財政部函釋與內政部令，是否使依法不能建築、仍作農業用地使用的都市畸零地無法適用課徵田賦的規定。大法官認為這兩項命令增加了法律所無的要件，違反憲法第十九條租稅法律主義。相關部分自解釋公布之日起不再援用。","held":"財政部函及內政部令中，使都市依法不能建築、仍作農業用地使用之畸零地無法適用課徵田賦規定的部分，增加法律所無之要件，違反租稅法律主義，自本解釋公布之日起不再援用。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十九條要求租稅構成要件須以法律明文規定；主管機關解釋法律不得逾越範圍而增加法律所無之租稅義務。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"依法不能建築、仍作農業用地使用的都市土地課徵田賦，是因其收益有限，為減輕農民負擔，且田賦負擔一般較地價稅為輕。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"土地稅法及平均地權條例未明定「依法不能建築」的意義，也未明確授權主管機關以命令補充。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"依建築法第四十四條，畸零地在與鄰接土地合併使用前不得單獨建築，應屬「依法不能建築」，仍作農業使用者依立法意旨應課徵田賦。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"兩項命令使此類畸零地無從適用田賦規定，逾越法律解釋範圍、增加法律所無之要件，違反租稅法律主義。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"聲請人對另一函釋未具體指摘其如何侵害憲法所保障之權利，該部分不受理。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["仍作農業使用的都市畸零地所有人","財政部與內政部等主管機關","納稅義務人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"This ruling (Interpretation No. 527) deals with how local self-governing bodies in Taiwan set up their offices and positions, and who may ask the Constitutional Court for an interpretation when disputes arise under the Local Government Act. The court explained that offices must generally be created through an organizational self-government ordinance, and it set out which bodies may apply for an interpretation and by what route in disputes with higher authorities.","held":"Local bodies must create offices and positions under an organizational ordinance, with a limited temporary exception where a law clearly requires a position. The court also set out who may apply for an interpretation, and how, in disputes over resolutions, local rules and supervisory actions, and said pure disputes over authority must follow the procedure in Article 77 of the Act.","points":[{"text":"Local self-governing bodies have the power to organize themselves and to make and carry out rules on their own affairs, within the Constitution and the law. Offices and positions must be set up by the local legislature through an organizational ordinance based on the central authority's standards.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Where a law clearly requires a position and making the rules will take time, the local executive may set it up first and appoint staff as a temporary measure for real operational needs. Positions the law merely allows need an ordinance as their basis.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"The Act's provisions on asking for an interpretation apply when a supervising authority doubts that a resolution or local rule conflicts with higher law but has not declared it void. If the local body disagrees with a notice declaring something void, its legislature (for an ordinance) or its executive (for an administrative rule) may apply, without the forwarding step of Article 9, because the higher authority is a party to the dispute.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"Local executives cannot go straight to the court over disputes with their own legislature on carrying out resolutions, and a legislature cannot pass a resolution and then seek an interpretation that it conflicts with higher law. The Act has no provision letting some members apply, and doing so would breach the principle against contradicting oneself.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"A local body may apply directly under Article 75, paragraph 8 only if the supervisor's action involves the validity of a local rule said to violate higher norms and that rule has not been declared void. The court reviews norms, not individual administrative acts, so other harm must go through administrative lawsuits and, after all appeals, possibly an application; pure authority disputes follow Article 77.","cites":["4","7"]},{"text":"For other applications, a local legislature may apply by resolution without forwarding. A local government may apply directly on its own affairs where it is not bound by the central authority's views, but for centrally commissioned matters the Article 9 procedure still applies.","cites":["8"]}],"who":["Local self-governing bodies","Local legislatures","Local executive agencies","Central and higher-level supervisory authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a National Assembly delegate who has not taken the required oath may still carry out the duties of the office. The Court said no: a delegate who did not take the oath, or who deliberately did not take it in the legal form and with the legal wording, may not exercise the powers of the office. This adds to the Court's earlier Interpretation No. 199.","held":"The oath under Article 4 of the National Assembly Organization Act is an oath for exercising office. A delegate who did not take it, or who deliberately did not complete it in the legal form and wording, may not exercise powers. Interpretation No. 199 is supplemented accordingly.","points":[{"text":"The Court accepted the request because the requesting body had doubts about Interpretation No. 199 and asked for a supplementary interpretation, as earlier interpretations allow.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The oath is meant to let the person publicly and solemnly declare their resolve to obey the Constitution and carry out their duties lawfully on behalf of the nation's people. Under Interpretation No. 199 it is an oath for exercising office.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The oath is a formal act in public law. Its wording is fixed by the Organization Act, and its procedure and manner follow Articles 3 to 7 of the Oath Act.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"A delegate who did not take the oath breaches the duty to do so and may not exercise powers. Where clear evidence shows deliberate departure from the legal manner or wording, the formal act is not treated as done, which equals not swearing, so powers may not be exercised.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Whether a delegate who has not properly sworn may attend meetings is left to the National Assembly to decide itself, under the principle of self-regulation of the assembly.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["National Assembly delegates","The National Assembly","Delegates who did not swear or who deliberately swore improperly"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a 1962 rule implementing the Public Servants Insurance Act was unconstitutional for limiting to five years the time an insured person could keep their insurance service years on record. The court decided the rule added a time limit that the law itself did not contain, goes against the constitution's protection of people's rights, and should not be applied.","held":"Article 68 of the 1962 enforcement rules, which limited reserved insurance years to five years and treated later re-enrollment as new enrollment, does not match the Act, adds a limit the law lacks, and is not to be applied.","points":[{"text":"The Act's Article 21 said that a person who left a job and chose to reserve their insurance years instead of seeking a refund would have all their original years count when they resumed insurance.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The Act's Article 24 authorized the making of enforcement rules but did not authorize limiting the substantive right of insured people to reserve their insurance years.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The enforcement rule's five-year limit, with later re-enrollment treated as new enrollment, added a period restriction the law does not contain.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Adding that restriction goes against the constitution's protection of people's rights, so the rule should not be applied.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Insured public servants","Public servants who left their jobs and reserved insurance years","Public servants who later re-enrolled in insurance","The examining authority that issued the rule"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"立法院與行政院對中央政府建設公債發行條例第二條的適用見解不同，聲請大法官統一解釋。爭點是「公債」是否包括政府一年以上的賒借。大法官認為廣義公債包括一切公共債務，但該條例所稱公債僅指依法以債票方式發行的建設公債，同時指出國家全部舉債上限宜綜合考量以法律訂定。","held":"廣義的公債指包括政府賒借在內的一切公共債務；中央政府建設公債發行條例所稱公債，則只指依法以債票方式發行的建設公債。為維護國家財政健全，國家全部舉債的上限宜綜合考量以法律訂定。","points":[{"text":"本案由立法院與行政院對該條例第二條的見解不同而聲請統一解釋，符合受理規定，經言詞辯論後作成解釋。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"政府在收支不平衡時，承諾還本付息而向各方借款，都屬廣義公債；狹義公債則是以發行債票方式募款。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"該條例是針對中央政府為籌建設資金而依法發行債票或憑證所訂，第二條的「未償總餘額」只指這類建設公債，不含其他法律發行的短期債票或向銀行賒借一年以上的借款。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"賒借與發行公債同屬政府公共債務，實質上都是財政工具，而其他舉債方式都有法律規範及額度或比例限制。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"一年以上賒借的最高數額不受該條例上限限制，也無其他法律限制，會使上限規定形同具文，與其他舉債方式相比也失均衡，且僅編列預算送審，難免有捨發行公債以規避限制的情形。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"因此為維護國家財政健全，宜綜合考量以法律訂定國家全部舉債的上限。","cites":["2","7"]}],"who":["立法院","行政院","中央政府","人民（納稅人）"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"這號解釋處理的問題是：曾任薦任審計職務三年以上的人，能不能報考會計師檢覈。大法官認為，只要在政府機關曾任薦任審計職務三年以上，並經銓敘合格，就應認為符合會計師法第二條第一項第四款的規定。解釋文沒有說明理由。","held":"在政府機關曾任薦任審計職務三年以上、經銓敘合格的人，都應認為符合會計師法第二條第一項第四款的規定。","points":[],"who":["曾任薦任審計職務三年以上且經銓敘合格者","想應會計師檢覈的人"],"covered":false}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Ministry of Finance rules that estimate a small business's sales by dividing its operating expenses by an expense rate, and then tax those sales, are unconstitutional. The court decided they are not. It found the method is simpler for small businesses, allows for regional differences, and lets a business opt for the ordinary calculation instead.","held":"The Ministry of Finance's rules for assessing business tax on small businesses, which use the expense-restoration method (operating expenses divided by an expense rate) to estimate sales, do not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution's Article 19 requires paying tax according to law but does not forbid laws that allow tax to be set by estimation in particular situations, as an earlier interpretation (No. 218) had explained.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Business Tax Act, in its 1980 and 1985 versions, itself provided for assessing small businesses' tax by fixed determination, and left the assessment methods to the Ministry of Finance, so these were legal rules for estimated taxation.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Ministry's successive rules were consistent and could be applied one after another, all using the expense-restoration formula to estimate sales and apply the legal tax rate, which simplifies tax procedures for small businesses.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"The expense standards take regional economic conditions into account, because local tax authorities set grade tables by area or district and file them with the Ministry, so the estimates fit reality.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"A small business that does not want this special method may apply to calculate its tax by the ordinary method, the same as other businesses, which is consistent with tax fairness.","cites":["3","2"]},{"text":"The court declined to interpret Article 8 of the Uniform Invoice Prize Measures because no final court judgment had applied it.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Small-scale business operators","Tax authorities","Ministry of Finance"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Two people whose land was expropriated by the government asked to take it back, but were refused as being past the deadline. They argued the law never required the government to tell former owners how the land was later used. The court held that this gap violates the constitutional protection of property, and the law must be reviewed and fixed within 2 years.","held":"Article 219, paragraph 1 of the Land Act is unconstitutional to the extent that it sets the deadline to start running without requiring regular notice or public announcement of how expropriated land is used, and it must be reviewed and amended within 2 years. Until then, unfinished time limits for taking land back are paused.","points":[{"text":"Expropriation is the most serious intrusion on property rights, so the state must follow the strictest procedures, both before and at the time of expropriation.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Once expropriation is complete, if the land is not used as planned or by the deadline, the reason for expropriation is gone. The former owner's right to take the land back is an extension of constitutional property protection, and the state keeps some duty to protect it by fair procedure.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Former owners usually cannot easily learn whether the land is no longer needed or unused, so the authority should regularly notify them, or publicly announce if individual notice is not possible.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The Land Act provision starts the time limit one year after compensation is paid and requires no regular notice or announcement, so people cannot get enough information to decide whether to seek return. This is inconsistent with proper administrative procedure and with the property protection in Article 15.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"When adding a notice duty, the law should set shorter or longer reasonable time limits depending on whether notice was given, balancing property protection and legal stability. How the two periods fit together is left to the legislature.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"Time limits not yet run out are paused as of the ruling, resume once the authority gives notice or announcement, and then follow the new law once it is passed.","cites":["3","9"]}],"who":["Former owners of expropriated land","Municipal and county authorities in charge of expropriated land","Legislators and agencies revising the law","Persons whose land was taken in general expropriation"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an adoption can be ended by court order when both sides have in substance agreed to end it but the required formalities were not completed. The court held that in a specific situation, where an adoptive daughter was formally married to the adoptive parent's biological son and the parent then died, she may ask a court to end the adoption.","held":"Where an adopted daughter was formally married by her adoptive parent to the parent's biological son, the substantive requirement for ending the adoption is met. If the adoptive parent died before the written formality could be completed, she may ask a court for a ruling ending the adoption under Article 1081, item 6 of the Civil Code.","points":[{"text":"Article 1080 requires both sides to agree to end an adoption and to put it in writing, and the writing requirement exists to make the act solemn.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"When the adoptive parent presides over the daughter's formal marriage to the parent's biological son, both sides have agreed to change their status, which meets the substantive requirement in the first paragraph of Article 1080.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"If the adoptive parent dies before completing the written formality, completing it becomes impossible.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"So the daughter may seek a court ruling ending the adoption under Article 1081, item 6, as a remedy.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Adopted daughters who were formally married to the adoptive parent's biological son","Adoptive parents who arranged such a marriage","Courts handling requests to end adoptions"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a 2001 Ministry of Finance rule on duty-free imports of military goods was unconstitutional. The rule says that when a military agency runs a tender and the winning company imports the goods, the tender documents must say duty-free application is allowed and the bid price must exclude the exempted taxes. The court held that the rule stays within what the Customs Act authorized and does not violate the constitution's principle that taxes must rest on law.","held":"Article 8, paragraph 1 of the 2001 revised Regulations on Duty-Free Import of Military Articles is a supplementary rule made under authority granted by the Customs Act. It does not exceed that authority and does not conflict with Article 19 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Article 19 of the Constitution requires that tax duties and tax breaks have their key elements set by law or by an order clearly authorized by law. Any authorization to a ministry must be specific and clear. Whether an order fits the authorization is judged by the law's purpose and overall structure, not just its wording.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Customs Act exempts military weapons, equipment, vehicles, ships, aircraft, their accessories and goods used only for military purposes. It authorizes the Ministry of Finance to set rules on the scope, items, quantities and limits of the exemption. The Ministry issued the regulations under that authority, and Article 8, paragraph 1 requires tender documents to state that exemption may be sought and that the bid price excludes exempted taxes.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Customs needs further rules to check whether declared goods really are military goods and whether the quantities and items declared match what is actually imported. The authorization lets the Ministry set such rules so that the duty exemption is carried out, taxes are collected according to law and tax evasion is prevented.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The rule makes it public whether duty exemption is being sought, so all bidders know and can set their prices accordingly. This supports fair tendering and gives customs a basis for review, which speeds clearance. It is therefore necessary for carrying out the Customs Act. Judged by the Act's purpose and overall structure, it does not exceed the authorization.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Military agencies that run tenders","Companies bidding for or winning military procurement contracts","Importers of military goods","Customs and tax authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the rules for taxing individuals' profit from selling a house were unconstitutional, in particular the method of setting taxable income when a seller cannot prove the price and cost. The court decided that the Enforcement Rules provision and the Ministry of Finance's 20% standard for Taipei in 1987 do not violate the Constitution.","held":"Article 17-2 of the Income Tax Act Enforcement Rules, as amended in 1988, does not violate the principle that taxes must be set by law. The Ministry of Finance's 1988 notice setting Taipei's 1987 house-sale income at 20% of the house tax assessed value was set with year, area and economic conditions in mind, and does not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Profit from an individual's house sale is a kind of property transaction income under Article 9 of the Income Tax Act.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"When a taxpayer does not file or show documents, tax authorities may estimate income, which is not unconstitutional, but the estimate should be objective and reasonable, close to actual income, to keep taxes fair.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Applying one fixed percentage of assessed value regardless of year, area or economic conditions would stray from actual income and be unfair, as Interpretation No. 218 already said.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 17-2 lets sellers with proof of price and costs be taxed on actual figures, and otherwise the authorities apply a standard that local tax offices draft from the year's economic conditions and the housing market and the Ministry of Finance approves. This does not violate the principle that taxes must be set by law.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The 20% standard was based on a sample survey of many Taipei cases for 1987, where the average was 22.02% and 73% of cases were at 20% or above, and it was set with year, area and economic conditions in mind rather than as a fixed percentage, consistent with Interpretation No. 218.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Individuals who sell houses","Sellers who cannot prove price or cost","Tax authorities","Taipei house sellers for 1987"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Supreme Court precedent limiting retrial claims based on 'newly discovered evidence' violates the Constitution. The precedent says only evidence that already existed before the final fact-finding hearing ended, but that the party did not know about, counts. The court held the precedent does not conflict with the Constitution.","held":"The Supreme Court precedent (1940 Shang-zi No. 1005) is not unconstitutional. Evidence that only came into existence after the final fact-finding hearing ended cannot be a ground for retrial, though whether the facts it shows are bound by the final judgment depends on each case.","points":[{"text":"Parties may submit attack or defense methods, including evidence, at any time before the fact-finding hearing ends, and the appeal court on law must rely on the facts the second instance settled. So parties should submit all existing, known evidence by then.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The binding effect of a final judgment is measured at the close of the fact-finding hearing, for the same reasons.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Holding back known, available evidence to use in a retrial later would abuse the retrial system, waste litigation efficiency and undermine the stability of final judgments.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The precedent pushes parties to submit all existing, known evidence early and prevents arbitrary retrial suits after a judgment becomes binding, protecting the stability of final rulings, so it does not conflict with the Constitution.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Evidence that arose after the hearing ended cannot ground a retrial, but whether the facts it proves are bound by the final judgment depends on the individual case. Whether evidence made from earlier-existing evidence counts as newly discovered is a question of fact-finding and legal interpretation.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["Parties to civil lawsuits","Parties seeking a retrial","Courts handling retrial petitions"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A Taoyuan district court judge, hearing two public-order cases, asked whether a person can be fined under the Social Order Maintenance Act after already being prosecuted for the same act under criminal law. The Constitutional Court said no where the person has already been convicted by a final judgment, because that is double punishment. That part of the fine rule loses effect from the date of the ruling.","held":"Where the same act has already been prosecuted under criminal law and ended in a final guilty judgment, the proviso in Article 38 allowing an additional fine is double punishment, violates the principle of no double punishment for one offense, and ceases to have effect from the ruling's announcement.","points":[{"text":"The principle bars the state from pursuing and punishing the same criminal act twice. It rests on legal stability, protection of reliance and proportionality, and it can also apply to administrative penalties that are equal or similar to criminal punishment in nature, purpose and effect.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The Act's offenses already include minor-crime conduct comparable to criminal offenses. Its penalty factors match those of the Criminal Code, and courts hearing its cases apply the Code of Criminal Procedure where the Act is silent.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"So the wrongs and harms under the Act and the criminal offense for the same act differ only in degree, not in essential nature.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Allowing a fine after a final guilty judgment for the same act is therefore double punishment and conflicts with the principle.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The ruling does not decide whether a fine is allowed after a final acquittal, and it finds no conflict in business suspension, closure orders and confiscation, which aim to remove or prevent harm.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["People already convicted by a final judgment for an act that also breaches the Social Order Maintenance Act","Courts handling Social Order Maintenance Act fine cases"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"嘉義市、臺北市、臺南市、臺中市和桃園市的議會各自訂定自治條例，規定肉品（尤其是含萊克多巴胺的豬肉）不得檢出萊劑，與中央訂定的安全容許量標準不同，因此被衛福部或行政院函告無效或不予核定。憲法法庭認為，進口肉品殘留乙型受體素的安全容許量標準屬中央立法事項，中央的函告沒有逾越監督地方自治的權限，因此合憲。","held":"進口肉品及其產製品殘留乙型受體素的安全容許量標準屬中央立法事項；衛福部和行政院對五個地方議會自治條例所作的函告無效或不予核定，並未逾越中央監督地方自治的權限，均屬合憲；其餘聲請不受理。","points":[{"text":"我國憲法採單一國體制，專屬中央的事項地方不得另行立法，即使是地方自治事項，自治條例也不得牴觸憲法及中央法律。","cites":["65","66"]},{"text":"地方自治立法的範圍以轄區內的人、事、物為限；若規範效果對轄區外會產生直接、密切的實質影響，就屬跨轄區或全國性事項，不應完全交由各地方自行立法。","cites":["69","70"]},{"text":"肉品殘留萊克多巴胺的安全容許量標準應全國一致，屬憲法所定「商業」及「公共衛生」的中央立法事項，食安法也只授權中央主管機關訂定，並未授權地方另訂。","cites":["73","74"]},{"text":"五個自治條例所訂的零檢出標準欠缺授權且牴觸中央法律，並逾越地方自治立法權的範圍，與司法院釋字第738號解釋的情形不同，不能援引。","cites":["76","78","81"]},{"text":"各自治條例禁止含萊劑肉品販售及運送，阻礙合法貨物在各地流通，也違反憲法第148條保障國內貨物自由流通的意旨，並可能間接影響國際貿易政策的執行。","cites":["85","87","88"]},{"text":"中央標準是否足以保障健康、地方標準有無科學依據，屬風險評估的專業問題，不在本案審理範圍；平等原則的主張也與中央、地方的權限爭議無關。","cites":["82","83"]}],"who":["提出聲請的五個直轄市、縣（市）議會","衛福部與行政院等中央主管機關","地方自治團體","進口肉品業者與消費者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a court precedent was unconstitutional for denying withholding-at-source tax treatment to overseas Chinese and foreign investors whose spouse lived in Taiwan. The Constitutional Court held the precedent added a spouse-residence condition that the statute does not contain, which violates the constitutional principle that taxes must be based on law. The precedent therefore must not be applied.","held":"The 1974 Administrative Court precedent (No. 673) added a condition, that no spouse lives in Taiwan, that the law does not contain. It violates the principle of taxation by statute and must not be applied.","points":[{"text":"The investment incentive laws were meant to encourage production businesses and speed economic growth, and withholding tax at a set rate was meant to ease investors' tax burden and attract overseas Chinese and foreign investment.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Because those laws are special laws relative to the Income Tax Act, people who benefit from the investment incentives should get the tax-reducing rules in them.","cites":["3","5"]},{"text":"The Constitution's Article 19 means people owe tax only under what the law sets, such as who pays, tax items, rates, methods and reductions. Precedents cannot add rules the law lacks or increase the tax burden.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The incentive law's article 17 refers only to individuals not residing in Taiwan and sets no condition about a spouse's residence. Those who meet its terms get withholding at the set rate rather than year-end filing under the Income Tax Act.","cites":["5","2"]},{"text":"The precedent added a no-spouse-in-Taiwan condition, which adds a limit the law does not have, so it conflicts with taxation by statute.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"The Court did not decide whether a person or spouse actually counts as non-resident because of a home or other facts, which is a question of fact and law application. It also did not address the Civil Code equality complaint, which was not specifically argued.","cites":["5","6"]}],"who":["Overseas Chinese investors approved to invest in Taiwan","Foreign investors approved to invest in Taiwan","Investors who are company directors, supervisors or managers","Investors whose spouse lives in Taiwan"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案有八位聲請人因在臉書、網站、書面公告等處發表貶損他人名譽的言論，被法院依刑法誹謗罪判刑確定，認為誹謗罪規定違反言論自由而聲請審查。憲法法庭認為誹謗罪處罰規定整體上沒有違憲，但要求所誹謗的事涉及公共利益時，表意人若事前經合理查證，即使無法證明為真實也不罰。八位聲請人的聲請均被駁回。","held":"刑法第310條及第311條的誹謗罪規定整體上不違反比例原則與言論自由，但涉及公共利益的言論，若表意人事前經合理查證、可合理相信為真實，即不罰；聲請人一至八的聲請均無理由而駁回。","points":[{"text":"言論自由與名譽權同受憲法保障，兩者衝突時須適當衡量；刑罰限制誹謗言論須符合比例原則，並特別考量言論對公益論辯的貢獻度。","cites":["53","54","55","56","57"]},{"text":"誹謗罪的目的在保護憲法上的重要權利，刑罰手段適當且必要，且立法者另以第三項、第311條的不罰規定縮小處罰範圍。","cites":["62","63","64"]},{"text":"涉於私德而與公共利益無關的言論，不適用真實性抗辯，因為舉證會侵犯被指述者隱私，此時言論自由應退讓，這部分不違反相稱性要求。","cites":["69","70","71"]},{"text":"涉及公共利益的言論，真實性不限於絕對真實，表意人經合理查證、可合理相信為真實即不罰；引用不實證據若無明知或重大輕率的惡意，仍不罰。","cites":["75","76","77","78"]},{"text":"查證是否合理須依個案判斷，在傳播媒體上發表須更周密嚴謹，公益論辯貢獻度愈高則容錯空間愈大。在此前提下誹謗罪規定整體合憲，釋字第509號解釋予以補充。","cites":["79","80","82"]},{"text":"聲請人七、八的確定判決已充分考量言論自由與名譽權，其解釋適用未牴觸憲法，聲請被駁回。","cites":["84","86","88"]}],"who":["被控誹謗罪的表意人","被指述而主張名譽權的人","社群媒體、網路與傳播媒體的發言者","本案八位聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked how forging or altering New Taiwan Dollars should be punished. The court decided that, from the date the Central Bank entrusted the Bank of Taiwan with issuing them, forging or altering these notes is punished under the Act for Punishing Harm to National Currency.","held":"New Taiwan Dollars issued by the Bank of Taiwan, from the date the Central Bank entrusted it to issue them as agent, are covered by the Act for Punishing Harm to National Currency if forged or altered.","points":[{"text":"The New Taiwan Dollar was originally a local currency issued by the Bank of Taiwan.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"After the Central Bank entrusted the Bank of Taiwan to issue it, the Central Bank handled printing and storage, paid the issuing costs, and held the related assets and liabilities.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Public and private accounting was also done in New Taiwan Dollars.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"So from the entrusting date it should be seen as having the function of national currency under the Act, and forgery or alteration is punished under that Act to protect major national financial and economic interests during the period of mobilization against rebellion.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The ruling supplements the explanation given in Interpretation No. 63.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["People who forge or alter New Taiwan Dollars","Bank of Taiwan","Central Bank"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A court referred a drug case to Taiwan's Constitutional Court, asking whether Article 205-2 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which lets police take a urine sample from a lawfully arrested suspect against their will, is constitutional. The court held that the rule covers only non-invasive urine collection, where the person urinates on their own. It found the rule lacks the fair-procedure safeguards the Constitution requires, so it will lose effect within 2 years, and interim rules apply until it is amended.","held":"Article 205-2 is unconstitutional as it stands and loses effect no later than 2 years after the judgment is announced. Until it is amended, police must ask a prosecutor for a permit before taking urine, or in urgent cases report to the prosecutor within 24 hours. Prosecutors must revoke within 3 days any collection they find should not be allowed, and the person tested may ask a court to revoke it within 10 days. Cases already concluded or still pending under the old rule are handled under current rules.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution protects information privacy and freedom from bodily and mental harm. The state may collect personal information by limiting these rights only if it meets Article 23 and follows fair legal procedure, including a chance for remedy.","cites":["11","12"]},{"text":"The rule covers only non-invasive collection, where the person urinates on their own. Invasive methods such as catheterization are not covered, because they would seriously harm the person's rights and police should not be authorized to use them.","cites":["14","15","16"]},{"text":"Even non-invasive collection against a person's will limits their information privacy and bodily rights, though less severely than invasive collection. It therefore needs proper legal procedure like other compulsory evidence-gathering such as searches and body examinations.","cites":["18","19"]},{"text":"Because the harm is lighter, letting prosecutors decide on non-invasive collection is acceptable. Police may be given exceptional power to act without prior permission, but only with later oversight and a remedy.","cites":["20","21"]},{"text":"Urine evidence can be lost with time, so in urgent cases where delay would prevent preserving evidence, police may collect first and report to a prosecutor afterward.","cites":["22","23"]},{"text":"The rule makes no distinction for urgency, requires no permission, has no prosecutor review afterward, and gives the person no way to seek a remedy. That does not meet fair legal procedure.","cites":["23","25"]}],"who":["Lawfully arrested suspects and defendants","Judicial police officers and police","Prosecutors and prosecutor's investigators","Courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是民法規定收養者年齡須比被收養者大二十歲以上，違反者收養無效，是否違憲。大法官認為這些規定符合倫常觀念，且為維持社會秩序、增進公共利益所必要，並不違憲。不過，夫妻共同收養或一方收養他方子女時，宜有彈性規定，有關機關應檢討修正。","held":"民法第一千零七十三條的年齡差距規定及第一千零七十九條之一違反者無效的規定，與憲法保障人民自由權利之意旨並無牴觸。但夫妻共同收養或夫妻一方收養他方子女時，宜有彈性之設，有關機關應予檢討修正。","points":[{"text":"規定是為尊重世代傳統，限制收養者與被收養者的年齡差距，符合我國倫常觀念。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"這些規定為維持社會秩序、增進公共利益所必要，與憲法保障人民自由權利之意旨並無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"年齡合理差距屬立法裁量事項。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"現行收養制度以保護養子女利益為宗旨，社會親子關係日趨複雜。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"夫妻共同收養或收養他方配偶之子女時，若不符年齡規定致收養無效，反而有損被收養人利益，影響家庭幸福。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"基於家庭和諧並兼顧養子女權利，這類情形宜有彈性之設，以符合社會生活實際需要，有關機關應檢討修正。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["收養者","被收養者（養子女）","夫妻共同收養的家庭","收養配偶子女的一方"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是平均地權條例及其施行細則對土地自然漲價計徵土地增值稅的規定，是否違憲。大法官認為，這些規定是以漲價總數額減去土地所有權人為改良土地已支付的全部費用後之餘額來徵稅，與憲法第十五條及第一百四十三條第三項的意旨尚無牴觸。","held":"平均地權條例第三十五條、第三十六條第一項、第二項及其施行細則第五十三條有關計徵土地增值稅的規定，與憲法第十五條及第一百四十三條第三項意旨尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"憲法第一百四十三條第三項旨在實施土地自然漲價歸公政策，土地增值稅即據此徵收。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"土地所有權人申報地價後的自然漲價，依漲價總數額減去為改良土地已支付的全部費用後之餘額計算徵稅。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"因改良土地而增加的價值，認定及計算不易，難以與自然漲價部分明確劃分。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"土地增值稅並未就漲價部分全額徵收，已足以兼顧土地所有權人的利益，因此與憲法規定意旨尚無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"如何核實訂定扣減改良土地費用的標準，可有從嚴從寬的選擇，且與稅率調整及是否另徵所得稅密切相關，應由有關機關在立法裁量範圍內適時通盤檢討改進。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["土地所有權人","負責徵收土地增值稅的有關機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"When an employer owes workers unpaid wages, a fund paid by employers covers the wages, and the Bureau of Labor Insurance then seeks repayment from the employer. The question was which court system hears disputes over that repayment claim. The court decided that the ordinary (civil) courts hear them, because the claim is still a private-law debt.","held":"Disputes between the Bureau of Labor Insurance and an employer over the repayment claim it acquires after paying workers' wages from the fund are private-law disputes, and the ordinary courts have jurisdiction over them.","points":[{"text":"Under the Labor Standards Act, employers must pay into a wage-advance fund, which covers unpaid wages of under six months when the employer closes, liquidates or goes bankrupt, protecting workers' wages.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"What the Bureau pays out from the fund is the employer's original private-law debt to the workers for wages.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The fund is paid for by employers, and paying from it is not the state giving public-law benefits from the national treasury; the Bureau acts as manager of a fund pooled by employers.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"After paying, the Bureau acquires a claim against the employer that has the same scope, content and private-law nature as the workers' wage claim, and it stands in the workers' position.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The claim passes to the Bureau by operation of law, and its private nature does not change because a state body exercises it, the fund is managed by the central authority, or the fund serves a public purpose.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"Fines for an employer failing to pay into the fund breach a public-law duty and go through the administrative courts, a separate matter. The court also did not address the right to sue or the procedure laws themselves.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Employers who owe wages","Workers owed wages","Bureau of Labor Insurance"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"一位法官審理兒童保護安置事件時，認為要適用的法律可能違憲，想聲請大法官解釋，但為免兒童受不利益，先作出了終局裁定，並請求釋明聲請釋憲時是否一定要停止程序。大法官說明，法官聲請釋憲時必須裁定停止訴訟或非訟程序，但若有急迫情形，仍應作必要的保全、保護或其他適當處分；至於本件，因案件已終結，不受理該釋憲聲請。","held":"法官聲請釋憲必須先裁定停止訴訟或非訟程序（包括非訟事件），停止後遇急迫情形，應為必要的保全、保護或其他適當處分，並補充釋字第371號及第572號解釋；本件聲請因原案已終結而不受理。","points":[{"text":"「法官於審理案件時」包括刑事、行政訴訟、民事及非訟事件，所以「裁定停止訴訟程序」也包括非訟程序的停止。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"宣告法律是否違憲專屬大法官職掌，法官只能依據法律審判，無權自行認定違憲而拒絕適用；若不停止程序就等於適用自己確信違憲的法律裁判，所以必須停止程序。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"停止程序後若有急迫情形，為保障人民訴訟權並兼顧公共利益，法官除不得終結本案外，應探究立法目的、權衡各方利益、斟酌個案情況，為必要處分，且處分前當事人與利害關係人應有陳述意見機會，事後亦可尋求救濟。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"以兒童及少年性交易防制條例的安置規定為例，若停止程序導致兒童繼續被安置而權益保障欠缺，法官應作妥適處分，如暫交付親權人或監護人，或交付社會福利機構輔導教養。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"聲請釋憲須以原案件仍在繫屬中為限；本件原案已作終局裁定而脫離繫屬，不符要件，故不受理。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["審理案件的法官","訴訟或非訟程序的當事人與利害關係人","受安置的兒童或少年及其親權人、監護人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於內政部訂定的時效取得地上權登記審查要點，禁止占有「耕地」的人申請時效取得地上權登記，是否違憲。大法官認為耕地性質上不適合設定地上權，所以這項規定與憲法保障人民財產權的意旨並無牴觸。","held":"占有農業發展條例所稱耕地的人，依內政部審查要點第三點第二款不得申請時效取得地上權登記，此規定與憲法保障人民財產權的意旨尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"依民法第八百三十二條，地上權是以在他人土地上有建築物、其他工作物或竹木為目的而使用土地的權利，所以設定地上權的土地須適合建築、設置工作物或種植竹林；因時效取得而請求登記者也一樣。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"所謂種植竹林，不包括以定期收穫為目的、施人工於土地栽培植物的情形。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"依土地法第八十二條前段，編為某種使用地的土地，不得供其他用途使用。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"耕地依農業發展條例第三條第十一款的定義，僅供耕作之用，不適合建築房屋、設置其他工作物，也不適合種植竹木作林地。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此耕地性質上不符合設定地上權的要件，也無法依時效取得地上權而請求登記。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"基於上述理由，審查要點禁止占有耕地者申請時效取得地上權登記，與憲法保障財產權的意旨尚無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["占有耕地的人","申請時效取得地上權登記的人","耕地所有人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是中醫師特種考試規定，只要有一科零分、專業科目平均未滿五十分，或特定科目未達最低分數，即使總成績滿六十分也不予及格，是否違憲。憲法法庭認為這些規定沒有牴觸法律保留原則、比例原則與平等權，也沒有違背工作權及應考試權的保障意旨。","held":"考試法施行細則、總成績計算規則及中醫師特種考試規則中，有關零分、專業科目平均不滿五十分、特定科目未達最低分數即不予及格的規定，未牴觸憲法第二十三條、第七條，與第十五條、第十八條意旨無違。","points":[{"text":"工作權及應考試權包含選擇專門職業與取得執業資格的權利，限制須符合法律保留、比例及平等原則；但考試機關涉及專業判斷的規定，應給予適度尊重。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"考試法已授權考試機關決定及格方式、考試規則與總成績計算規則，系爭規定把「總成績滿六十分及格」的內容具體化，未逾越授權範圍，不違反法律保留原則。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"考試院依醫師法規定，按應考人是否受正式中醫學教育分辦高等與特種考試，所定及格方式是鑑別應考人是否具執業資格的合理手段，不違反比例原則，也未違背工作權及應考試權。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"以學經歷分類考試、採不同及格標準，與鑑別知識能力的目的有合理關聯；中醫內科學五十五分、其餘專業科目四十五分的要求是依法定程序的專業判斷，並非恣意，不違反平等權。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"綜合以上，系爭規定與法律保留、比例原則、平等權均無牴觸，也未違背工作權及應考試權意旨。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["中醫師特種考試應考人","中醫師高等考試應考人","考試機關（考試院、考選部）","欲取得專門職業執業資格者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Two petitioners, a judge hearing a lawsuit and a person in a compensation case, asked whether a rule requiring land once provided for farmland irrigation use to keep being used that way, with no compensation, violates the constitutional protection of property. The court held that the rule can stand only if privately owned land used this way is backed by a legal basis such as a lease or purchase, or else is expropriated with fair compensation. The government must draw up compensation plans within 3 years.","held":"Where privately owned land must keep being used for irrigation and the government has not obtained a right to use it by lease, purchase or other means, the owner has borne a special sacrifice. The land must then be expropriated with fair compensation, and plans and funding must be set up within 3 years so this is completed gradually within a reasonable time.","points":[{"text":"Property rights protect an owner's freedom to use, profit from and dispose of their property. If the state turns private property into public-use property without a legal basis, the owner bears a special sacrifice and must be compensated through expropriation.","cites":["10"]},{"text":"Irrigation land is public-use property serving an especially important public interest, such as farming, the economy and people's livelihoods. It has been used continuously for a long time, so it should stay in use unless it is no longer needed and is formally retired.","cites":["12","15","16"]},{"text":"Owners of such land must tolerate its use for irrigation and cannot freely use it, so their property rights are seriously restricted. The state therefore needs a legal basis, such as a lease or purchase. Without one, it must expropriate with compensation and set up plans within 3 years.","cites":["18","19"]},{"text":"Official figures show that acquiring rights to the land has been slow and the dedicated fund is far too small. Authorities should set a deadline, raise funds, and consider ways other than full expropriation to obtain rights.","cites":["21"]},{"text":"Privately owned land used this way may serve only irrigation purposes and must be used in the least harmful way. Authorities should review each case and formally retire land no longer needed for irrigation.","cites":["22"]}],"who":["Private owners of land used for irrigation","Agricultural irrigation authorities","The government agency in charge of irrigation land","Courts handling these disputes"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether rules implementing the University Act were unconstitutional. The rules let the Ministry of Education set common required subjects for all universities and said students who fail them cannot graduate. The court held that two of these provisions went beyond the University Act and conflicted with the constitutional protection of academic freedom and university self-governance.","held":"Article 22, paragraph 1 (latter part) and paragraph 3 of the University Act's implementing rules are inconsistent with the Constitution. They lose effect no later than one year after the interpretation is announced.","points":[{"text":"Constitution Article 11 protects academic freedom as an institutional guarantee, which includes research, teaching and learning freedom and recognizes university self-governance.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Government supervision of universities must rest on law and meet the legal reservation principle of Article 23; the education authority should avoid intruding on matters protected by academic freedom.","cites":["2","3","4"]},{"text":"Course design and subject setting relate to teaching and learning freedom, so how a university sets its curriculum falls within university autonomy.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The University Act does not authorize the Ministry to convene universities to set common required subjects, so the implementing rules cannot add restrictions the Act does not contain.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Making failure of common required subjects a bar to graduation limits graduation conditions, which belong to university autonomy under the cited University Act and degree law provisions, so that clause exceeds the Act.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"During the one-year period, common required subjects should be set either by explicit statute or by each university through its own curriculum process.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Universities","University students","Ministry of Education"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A man was prosecuted for several related offences. Courts found him not guilty on some of them, and only the guilty findings (or other parts) were appealed. The higher court nonetheless sent the unappealed not-guilty parts back for retrial, and he was later convicted on one of them. The Constitutional Court ruled that the old appeal rule does not reach not-guilty parts nobody appealed, and that a 1940 precedent saying otherwise is unconstitutional.","held":"The pre-2021 Code of Criminal Procedure Article 348(2), which treats related parts of a judgment as also appealed, does not apply to parts where the original judgment found not guilty, and on that reading it is consistent with the Constitution. The part of Supreme Court precedent 29 Shang 3382 that treats unappealed not-guilty parts as appealed is unconstitutional, and the remaining requests were not accepted.","points":[{"text":"The principle that courts act only on charges and appeals brought before them protects defendants' right to a fair trial and to predict the scope of the case so they can defend themselves.","cites":["20"]},{"text":"A prosecutor's view of how the charged facts should be classified does not bind the court. If the court finds some charges not guilty, there is no single-penalty rule linking them to the guilty ones.","cites":["22","23"]},{"text":"The scope of an appeal is set by the parties and by the original judgment's reasoning, not worked out backwards from the appeal court's result. Unappealed not-guilty parts do not conflict legally with appealed parts.","cites":["25","27"]},{"text":"Pulling unappealed not-guilty parts into the appeal would surprise the defendant, risk a second guilty verdict after a final acquittal, and let the prosecutor's charging decide the question instead of the court.","cites":["27","29"]},{"text":"The precedent says unappealed not-guilty parts are treated as appealed, letting the appeal court go beyond what the parties asked. That violates the principle and the constitutional protections of personal liberty and the right to sue.","cites":["32"]},{"text":"Requests about other rulings and precedents were not accepted because they were not applied in the case. Review of the court judgments themselves was barred because they were served before the Constitutional Court Procedure Act amendment took effect.","cites":["35","37"]}],"who":["Criminal defendants acquitted on some charges","Prosecutors who appeal","Appeal courts","The applicant in this case"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論地方議會審議地方政府年度總決算的審核報告時，可否要求審計機關提供原始憑證。大法官表示，議會可以通知審計機關提供資料，但不包括審計機關已依法審定的原始憑證。","held":"地方各級議會準用決算法第二十七條審議審核報告時，固得通知審計機關提供資料，但不包括審計機關依審計法第三十六條及第七十一條審定之原始憑證。","points":[{"text":"地方政府年度總決算的編造、審核、審議，準用中央政府總決算的相關規定，包括決算法第二十七條「提供資料」的規定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"決算法第二十七條所稱「提供資料」，是指為審議審核報告之需要而提供與審核報告有關的資料，所以不包括審計機關已依法審定的原始憑證。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"審計權屬於監察院，由審計機關及審計人員依法獨立行使，各機關須將會計報告連同原始憑證送審計機關審核。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"各機關人員對財務上行為的責任，經審定後即解除；議會可要求的資料以審核報告中有關預算執行、政策實施及特別事件審核、救濟等事項為限，與審核時所根據的原始憑證並無直接關係。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["地方各級議會","審計機關","地方政府及其所屬機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A man whose wife died in 2010 applied for survivor's pension under the National Pension Act only in January 2012, and was paid only from the month he applied. The Constitutional Court held that, for deaths on or before 29 February 2016, limiting payment to start from the month of application violates the Constitution.
