The authorities must promptly review and improve how crossing alarms work when two or more trains pass one after another.","points":[{"text":"The rules limit general freedom of action, property (fines) and the right to work (license revocation for professional drivers), so they must meet the proportionality principle.","cites":["6","7"]},{"text":"The purpose is to stop drivers running crossings, protecting the safety, lives, bodies and property of many people; this is a major public interest and a constitutional purpose.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The lifetime ban is harsh because it ignores how serious the violation was, but Article 67-1 lets drivers re-apply after 6, 8, 10 or 12 years, so it is not truly lifelong and is substantially related to the purpose.","cites":["9"]},{"text":"The fine, and the limits on general freedom of action including the safety course, have a reasonable connection to the purpose and do not breach proportionality.","cites":["9"]},{"text":"The state has a constitutional duty to build sound rules and safeguards for crossings, yet the existing rules set no minimum safe interval between one train's alarm ending and the next starting, sometimes only a few seconds.","cites":["10"]},{"text":"Such short gaps can mislead drivers, especially of large vehicles, into entering the crossing and then being penalised, so the authorities must promptly improve this, for example with extended alarms.","cites":["10","3"]}],"who":["Motor vehicle drivers, including professional drivers","Railway passengers and the public using crossings","Railway and transport authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是八十六年修正公布的私立學校法第三十二條第一項，允許主管教育行政機關在董事會發生糾紛無法開會或違反教育法令時，解除或停止全體董事職務，是否違憲。大法官認為，該規定的用語並不違反法律明確性原則，其但書規定的限制手段也符合比例原則，與憲法保障工作權的意旨尚無違背。","held":"系爭規定中「董事會因發生糾紛，致無法召開會議或有違反教育法令情事」的部分，與法律明確性原則尚無違背；其但書規定未牴觸憲法第二十三條比例原則，與憲法保障人民工作權之意旨尚無違背。","points":[{"text":"私立學校董事執行職務屬職業自由，受憲法工作權保障；國家為增進公共利益，可在符合憲法第二十三條的限度內以法律加以限制。","cites":["3","4"]},{"text":"教育具高度公共性與公益性，憲法規定公私立教育機關依法律受國家監督；系爭規定讓主管機關及時介入，目的在維護學校健全發展、保障學生受教權及教職員工作權益，目的正當。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"解除全體董事職務屬對選擇職業自由的主觀條件限制，須基於重要公益目的，且手段與目的有實質關聯。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"「無法召開會議」是指無法依舊私立學校法規定召開會議，不問糾紛是否可歸責於個別董事；「違反教育法令」以教育法令明確存在為前提，範圍可確定；兩者有其一即合監督要件，受規範董事可理解、可預見，並可經司法審查，故不違反明確性原則。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"董事會職權影響學校運作甚大，在情節重大且情勢急迫時，立法者賦予主管機關緊急處置權；處置方式不只解除職務，也可選擇停止職務。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"解除或停止全體董事職務前，須先經由學者專家、學校代表等組成的私立學校諮詢委員會決議，具客觀性；即使未規範延長停止職務的期限與次數，限制仍非過當，符合比例原則。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["私立學校董事","私立學校主管教育行政機關","學生","私立學校教職員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Eight petitioners, including judges hearing drug cases and people already sentenced, argued that the law setting death or life imprisonment as the only penalties for selling Class 1 drugs is unconstitutional. The Constitutional Court held that, for very minor cases, the rule is too harsh even after a judge reduces the sentence under Criminal Code Article 59, so it violates the Constitution. It gave lawmakers two years to fix the law and allowed courts to reduce sentences further in the meantime.","held":"The fixed minimum of life imprisonment for selling Class 1 drugs is unconstitutional for cases with no other crimes and extremely minor, forgivable circumstances; the relevant authorities must amend it within 2 years, and until then courts may cut the sentence by up to half beyond the Article 59 reduction. Part of petitioner 8's request was not accepted.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution protects personal liberty, and a prison sentence must match the harm caused and the offender's blame; a punishment beyond that is unconstitutional.","cites":["27"]},{"text":"The law's purpose is serious: Class 1 drugs are the most addictive and harmful, and selling drugs feeds the supply of harm, so lawmakers chose heavy punishment to protect public health and order.","cites":["32","33"]},{"text":"Even so, Class 1 drug selling covers a huge range, from large smuggling groups to small sales between users or merely handing over drugs, yet the law gives one fixed minimum of life imprisonment.","cites":["36"]},{"text":"Courts usually apply Article 59 and sentence within 15 to 20 years, but for extremely minor, forgivable cases with no other crimes this is still too harsh and out of proportion to blame, so the rule violates the proportionality principle.","cites":["36"]},{"text":"As a temporary measure until the law is amended, courts may reduce the sentence by up to half in such cases, and petitioners 4 to 8 may ask the Prosecutor General to file an extraordinary appeal.","cites":["37","38"]},{"text":"The court also suggested lawmakers consider adding fixed-term prison sentences or setting penalties by quantity or number of sales, noting that possession and transfer of Class 1 drugs already vary by quantity.","cites":["40","41","42","43","44"]}],"who":["People convicted of selling Class 1 drugs in very minor cases","Judges hearing such cases","Petitioners 4 to 8","Legislators and authorities who must amend the law"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問，先前院解字第三八二七號解釋所說的「認為聲請退休或命令退休」，適用範圍到哪裡。大法官認為，這項解釋只適用於民國三十二年公布的公務員退休法施行期間內所發生的事件。","held":"院解字第三八二七號解釋所稱認為聲請退休或命令退休，僅就其事件在民國三十二年公布之公務員退休法施行中發生者有其適用。","points":[{"text":"院解字第三八二七號解釋，是對民國三十二年公布施行的公務員退休法第十一條「退職」涵義所作的解釋。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"後來法律內容多次變更，所以該解釋只適用於該法有效期間內發生的事件。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"事件在該法施行中合於認為聲請退休或認為命令退休者，可據此聲請退休金；但自辭職獲准免職或裁遣的次月起已經過五年者，不在此限。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["適用民國三十二年公布之公務員退休法期間的公務員","聲請退休金的退職公務員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於耕地承租人因出租人終止租約而取得的補償金，是否要課徵所得稅。大法官認為，這筆依法給與地價三分之一的補償金，在扣除必要費用及實際所受損失後，如果仍有所得，就應依所得稅法第十四條第一項第九類課稅。","held":"出租耕地依法編為建築用地，出租人為自行建築或出售作建築使用而終止租約時，給與承租人的補償金，依具體事實扣除必要費用及實際所受損失後，如仍有所得，應依所得稅法第十四條第一項第九類課徵所得稅。","points":[{"text":"租約因編為建築用地而終止，並非出於承租人的自由意思，法律因此規定出租人要給予補償，以兼顧承租人生活、減少租佃糾紛並利於都市建設。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"相關條例規定，除補償改良土地費用及尚未收穫的農作改良物外，還要給與土地地價（或扣除土地增值稅後餘額）三分之一的補償。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"這項補償是用來填補承租人遷徙、轉業或其他必要支出，以及租約預期存續期間實際所受的損失，這些金額不是應課所得稅的所得。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此補償金扣除必要費用及實際損失後若仍有所得，該部分應依所得稅法第十四條第一項第九類課稅。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["耕地承租人","耕地出租人","出租耕地被編為建築用地的當事人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在審查所得稅法中，要求納稅義務人與有所得的配偶及其他受扶養親屬合併申報綜合所得稅的規定，是否違憲。大法官認為，就申報程序而言，這項規定與憲法尚無牴觸。但如果合併計算後稅負比單獨計算更重，就不符合租稅公平原則，主管機關宜檢討改進。","held":"合併申報綜合所得稅的規定，就申報程序而言與憲法尚無牴觸；但合併計算稅額若比單獨計算增加稅負，即與租稅公平原則不符，主管機關仍宜隨時檢討改進。","points":[{"text":"合併申報的目的，是減少申報及稽徵件數，節省徵納雙方的勞費。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"就合併申報的程序而言，這是增進公共利益所必要，因此與憲法尚無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"合併計算稅額若比單獨計算增加稅負，即與租稅公平原則不符。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"規定雖已於七十八年十二月三十日部分修正，主管機關仍宜隨時斟酌相關法律及社會經濟情況，就免稅額及扣除額等規定通盤檢討改進。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["綜合所得稅納稅義務人","有所得的配偶","其他受扶養親屬","稅務主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a person whose petition led the court to declare a law unconstitutional, with the law set to expire on a later date, can get relief in their own underlying case during that waiting period. The court said yes: the petitioner can seek a retrial or other relief, and courts cannot refuse just because the law stays valid until the deadline. The ruling also supplements two earlier interpretations and stops one administrative court precedent from being used.","held":"When the court declares a law applied in a final judgment unconstitutional but lets it expire later, the petitioner can seek retrial or other relief in the underlying case, and the Prosecutor General can file an extraordinary appeal. Courts may not reject these on the ground that the law is still valid until the deadline; if the ruling does not set a specific remedy, the case is decided under the new law once it takes effect.","points":[{"text":"Delayed expiry is meant to respect the lawmaking authority of other bodies and avoid a legal vacuum or sudden shock, and it does not change the fact that the law was declared unconstitutional.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Earlier interpretations Nos. 177 and 185 already let petitioners seek retrial or extraordinary appeal when a law was struck down with immediate effect, but they did not say what happens when expiry is delayed, so a supplement was needed.","cites":["3","4"]},{"text":"To carry out those earlier interpretations, petitioners in delayed-expiry cases should likewise get retrial or other relief, and courts cannot reject it because the law remains valid until the deadline.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"For real relief, the court's own specified remedy applies if it gives one; otherwise the case is decided under the new law after it takes effect.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"An administrative court precedent (No. 615 of 1997) that denied retroactive effect where the law stays valid for a period conflicts with this ruling and is no longer to be applied.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Article 273, paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Act, allowing a retrial suit, does not exclude laws declared unconstitutional with delayed expiry, so it is consistent with the ruling and not unconstitutional.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Petitioners whose petitions led to the ruling","Prosecutor General","Courts hearing underlying cases","Parties in administrative litigation"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Four people who had lost civil defamation-type cases challenged a Civil Code provision that lets courts order a wrongdoer to take 'appropriate measures' to restore a victim's reputation. In practice courts used it to order forced public apologies. The Constitutional Court held that the provision cannot be read to include court-ordered apologies, because that would violate free speech and, for individuals, freedom of thought.","held":"The 'appropriate measures' in Civil Code Article 195(1), second part, cannot include a court judgment ordering the wrongdoer to apologize, and the earlier Interpretation No. 656 is changed to that extent. The four petitioners may file for retrial within 30 days of receiving the judgment, and where an apology was already carried out, the retrial court may replace it with another measure at the victim's request, without undoing the apology or allowing that new measure to be enforced.","points":[{"text":"Forcing someone to apologize interferes with free speech, including the freedom not to speak. It forbids silence and compels a self-negating statement, so it faces strict review.","cites":["11","13"]},{"text":"Restoring a victim's reputation is a legitimate aim, but it is doubtful that every such case involves a especially important public interest, since some disputes are purely private.","cites":["14"]},{"text":"Less harmful alternatives exist, such as publishing a notice of the victory or the judgment in the media, and a court can also encourage an apology. A forced apology is therefore not the least harmful necessary means, and it is also doubtful that an insincere apology truly helps the victim.","cites":["15","16"]},{"text":"When the wrongdoer is an individual, a forced apology also violates freedom of thought, which is absolutely protected. It turns a legal judgment into the person's own moral judgment, causing self-denial and harming conscience and dignity.","cites":["18","19"]},{"text":"A legal person (such as a company) cannot claim freedom of thought, so for them only the free speech problem applies.","cites":["20"]},{"text":"Where an apology was already carried out, the retrial court should not apply Civil Procedure Code Article 505-1 or order restoration of the prior state, to avoid a second injury to the victim. The replacement measure cannot be enforced, so the dispute can end sooner.","cites":["24"]}],"who":["The four petitioners","Defendants ordered by courts to apologize","Victims of reputation harm","News media and companies"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether it is constitutional for Taiwan's immigration agency to detain foreigners awaiting deportation without giving them quick access to a court, and to keep detaining them past a short period without a court deciding. The court held that the detention rules were unconstitutional in two respects: no prompt court review for short-term detention, and no court decision for detention beyond that short period. The rules lose effect after two years unless the law is fixed.","held":"The detention provision in the immigration law is contrary to the constitutional protection of personal liberty because it gives no prompt court remedy during temporary detention and lets the agency, not a court, decide on longer detention. It will lose effect no later than two years after the ruling is published.","points":[{"text":"Personal liberty is a basic human right protected by Article 8 of the Constitution, and it covers foreigners as well as citizens.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Detaining foreigners for removal is a serious restriction of liberty, so it needs court procedures or other due process, though not necessarily the same as for criminal defendants.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"A short temporary detention by the agency, to carry out deportation arrangements, is reasonable and needs no court order, but the detainee must get prompt court review (transfer to a court within 24 hours if they object or ask) and be told of reasons and remedies in a language they understand. The temporary period may not exceed 15 days.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Detention beyond the temporary period deprives liberty for a long time, so an impartial, independent court must decide, with the agency applying to court before the period ends.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The law lacks prompt, effective court relief for temporary detention, and lets the agency alone order longer detention, so it violates due process and Article 8.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"Because fixing the law needs time and a complete set of supporting rules, the authorities have two years to revise it; otherwise the unconstitutional part loses effect.","cites":["8"]}],"who":["Foreigners detained pending deportation","Taiwan's immigration agency","Courts that would review detention","Lawmakers and related authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是兩位聲請人認為刑事訴訟法第33條第2項前段只讓無辯護人的被告在審判中預納費用請求卷內筆錄影本，侵害其訴訟權。憲法法庭認為該規定未讓有辯護人的被告直接獲知卷證資訊，也未讓被告請求筆錄以外的卷宗及證物影本，妨害防禦權的有效行使，在此範圍內與憲法第16條正當法律程序原則不符。有關機關須於1年內修正，逾期則由法院依請求付與全部卷證影本。","held":"系爭規定在未賦予有辯護人之被告直接獲知卷證資訊、未賦予被告請求筆錄以外卷宗及證物影本的範圍內，與憲法第16條保障訴訟權之正當法律程序原則不符；應於公布後1年內修正，逾期法院應依審判中被告請求，於其預納費用後付與全部卷宗及證物影本。暫時處分之聲請駁回。","points":[{"text":"憲法第16條的訴訟權保障被告充分防禦權，包括卷證資訊獲知權，審判中原則上應使被告適時以適當方式獲知全部卷宗及證物內容。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"被告有權親自直接獲知卷證，不因有無辯護人而不同；辯護人閱卷也不能完全取代被告本人的獲知權。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"卷宗及證物全部內容是法院審判的重要憑藉；只給筆錄影本，使被告無法就筆錄以外的證據充分表示意見，妨害防禦權。","cites":["10"]},{"text":"以預納費用付與影本（解釋上包括複本）的方式，因影本通常與原本效用相同，並不妨害防禦權，未牴觸憲法；必要時被告還可經許可檢閱卷證。","cites":["11"]},{"text":"除刑事訴訟法第33條第2項但書所示得限制的情形外，系爭規定在上述範圍內不符正當法律程序，須於1年內修正，逾期法院應付與全部卷證影本。","cites":["12"]},{"text":"暫時處分之聲請因本案已作成解釋而無必要，故駁回；聲請人二其他部分聲請則不受理。","cites":["13","14"]}],"who":["審判中有辯護人的被告","審判中無辯護人的被告","辯護人","法院及有關修法機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於公營事業的所得額，究竟應以徵收機關核定的數額為準，還是以審計部審定的數額為準。大法官會議解釋認為，審計部對各機關送交的決算有最終審定權，兩者不一致時，應以決算書上審計部審定的數目為準。","held":"徵收機關核定公營事業所得額，如與審計部審定同一事業的盈餘有歧異，應以決算書所載審計部審定的數目為準。","points":[{"text":"爭點是公營事業所得額應以徵收機關核定或審計部審定為準。","cites":["1"]},{"text":"審計部對各機關編送的決算有最終審定權。","cites":["2"]},{"text":"因此徵收機關核定的所得額與審計部審定的盈餘不同時，以決算書所載審計部審定的數目為準。","cites":["2"]}],"who":["公營事業","徵收機關","審計部"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是公職人員選舉罷免法規定選舉訴訟二審終結、不得提起再審之訴，是否違憲。大法官認為這是立法機關自由形成的範圍，符合選舉訴訟的特性，並未侵害人民的訴訟權，也不違反憲法第二十三條。","held":"民國八十三年七月二十三日修正公布的公職人員選舉罷免法第一百零九條規定，選舉訴訟採二審終結、不得提起再審之訴，沒有侵害憲法保障的訴訟權，且為增進公共利益所必要，與憲法第二十三條並不牴觸。","points":[{"text":"憲法保障訴訟權，旨在確保人民能依法定程序起訴並受公平審判；至於審級制度與程序，立法機關可衡量訴訟性質以法律合理規定。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"選舉、罷免訴訟重在公益維護，與保障私權的民事訴訟不盡相同。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"公職人員任期有限，審級過多會拖延時間，可能任期屆滿訴訟仍未終結，也影響當選人安於職位及公務推行，因此需要速審速結以安定法秩序。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"再審是非常程序，與確定判決的安定性要求相違，是否設置應視權利內涵與案件性質決定，屬立法機關自由形成的範疇；限制若合乎權利維護目的且有必要，就不算侵害訴訟權。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"選舉、罷免訴訟採當事人進行主義和合議制，第一審已慎重進行，疏漏可由上訴補救，經兩次辯論後應可信賴認事用法已臻理想。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"基於目的性要求和訴訟特性，排除再審是增進公共利益所必要，難認逾越憲法第二十三條。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["選舉訴訟的當事人","參選人與當選人","公職人員選舉罷免的相關人民"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是在問，內政部發布的土地登記專業代理人管理辦法中，關於請領專業代理人證書資格的規定是否違憲。憲法法庭認為，該辦法第四條是依土地法第三十七條之一第四項的授權訂定，沒有超出法律授權範圍，也與憲法沒有牴觸。","held":"土地登記專業代理人管理辦法第四條有關得請領專業代理人證書資格的規定，未逾越法律授權範圍，與憲法無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"法律不可能把所有事項規定得鉅細靡遺，細節性、技術性的事項可以授權主管機關以命令訂定；命令只要未逾越授權範圍並符合授權目的，憲法就允許。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"土地法第三十七條之一第二項是依憲法第八十六條第二款制定，與憲法無牴觸，這點已經釋字第三五二號解釋釋示。","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"內政部於七十九年六月二十九日發布的管理辦法，是依土地法該條第四項的授權訂定，其第四條所列三種得請領證書的資格，並未逾越法律授權範圍，與憲法也無牴觸。","cites":["4","2"]}],"who":["土地登記專業代理人","請領專業代理人證書者","土地代書人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是所得稅法第八十三條之一，允許稽徵機關對有重大逃漏稅嫌疑的案件調查納稅義務人的資產淨值、資金流程及不合營業常規的營業資料，是否違憲。大法官認為這項規定是以法律明定調查方法，且允許納稅義務人提出反證，與憲法尚無牴觸。","held":"所得稅法第八十三條之一對重大逃漏稅嫌疑案件的調查方法及舉證規定，與憲法尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"這項規定是針對有重大逃漏稅嫌疑的案件，以法律明定調查方法。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"稽徵機關可調查資產淨值、資金流程及不合營業常規的營業資料等間接證據，據以核算所得額。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"須依調查結果經合理判斷，認為足以證明有逃漏稅情事，納稅義務人才須就有利於己的事實負舉證之責。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"法律許納稅義務人提出反證，以維護其權益。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"此規定只是為了發現真實，不生溯及既往的問題。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["納稅義務人","稽徵機關","財政部指定之調查人員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a pledgee (someone holding a pledged item as security) must first obtain an enforcement title before asking a court to auction the item. The court decided that when the pledgee auctions under the situation described in Article 893 of the Civil Code, the earlier Interpretation No. 980 still applies. If the pledgee does not auction it personally and instead asks a court to do so, an enforcement title must be obtained first.","held":"A pledgee who sells the pledged item in a situation covered by Civil Code Article 893 must still follow Interpretation No. 980. If they ask a court to auction it rather than doing so themselves, they must first obtain an enforcement title.","points":[{"text":"The question was whether a pledgee asking a court to auction the pledged item must first obtain an enforcement title.","cites":["1"]},{"text":"Even in a situation under Civil Code Article 893, the pledgee must still follow Interpretation No. 980.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"If the pledgee does not auction the item personally but applies to a court, an enforcement title must be obtained first.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Pledgees (holders of pledged items)","Courts asked to auction pledged items"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance letter was unconstitutional for charging land value increment tax when co-owned land is divided and one co-owner ends up with land worth more than their share, without paying the others. The court found that such a division counts as a free transfer, so the co-owner who gains extra value is taxed on the extra part. It held that the letter's tax-collecting part is consistent with the law and does not conflict with Article 19 of the Constitution.","held":"When co-owned land is divided and a co-owner receives land worth more than their share without compensating the others, it is a free transfer, and that co-owner is taxed on the increased value. The Ministry of Finance letter's part on collecting this tax is consistent with the Land Tax Act and not contrary to Article 19 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"The Land Tax Act makes the person who receives land for free the taxpayer for land value increment tax, and 'free transfer' is not limited to bequests and gifts but includes other similar kinds of transfer.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"In a division of co-owned land, co-owners effectively transfer their shares to each other. If one gets more value than their share and does not compensate those who get less, that is a kind of free transfer, taxable on the extra part, so natural rises in land value are not left untaxed.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Implementing rules that tax the co-owner who ends up with less value conflict with the Act on this point and cannot be applied.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The Ministry letter's reasoning was flawed, but its part on taxing the person who gains ownership by free transfer matches the Act, is not affected by those rules, and does not conflict with Article 19.","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"Whether tax applies when a division gives each co-owner value equal to their share, but the land has risen in value, was outside the request and was not decided.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["Co-owners of land who divide it","Co-owners who receive land worth more than their share","Co-owners who receive less without compensation","Tax authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the Negotiable Instruments Act's criminal penalty for writing a check without enough money in the account is unconstitutional. The court decided it is not. It admitted the rule has been misused to stretch credit improperly, but said that is a question of whether the rule is well designed, which falls within the legislature's discretion.","held":"Article 141, paragraph 2 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, which sets criminal penalties for bad checks, stays within the legislature's discretion and does not conflict with Articles 15 and 22 of the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"A check is a payment instrument meant to be paid at once and works like cash. The law makes the issuer guarantee payment, and it punishes issuers who knowingly write checks beyond their funds, in order to protect circulation, actual payment and transaction safety.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Post-dated checks can still circulate, so the penalty also applies when one is not paid on its stated date. However, using criminal punishment to secure circulation can lead holders to ignore the issuer's credit, and the rule has been used to expand credit improperly.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"That flaw only raises the question of whether the provision is well designed. It stays within legislative discretion and does not conflict with Articles 15 and 22 of the Constitution.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"An issuer may raise defenses against the holder. If a criminal court convicts without examining whether such a defense bears on intent, that is a question of whether the judgment was proper, not of whether the provision is constitutional.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Check issuers","Check holders","Criminal courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the rules for charging a vehicle fuel usage fee, including who pays and how the fee is calculated, were unconstitutional. The court decided they were not: the Highway Act gave clear authority for the fee, and the charging rules did not violate the principles of legal reservation, equality or proportionality. It also found the fee is not double taxation together with the vehicle license tax.","held":"The Highway Act's fuel fee provision and the 1997 fee collection measures (Articles 2 and 3) stay within the authority granted by law and do not violate the Constitution's equality or proportionality principles. The fee and the vehicle license tax do not amount to double taxation.","points":[{"text":"Non-tax money duties imposed for a public purpose affect property rights, so the purpose, who pays and the amount must be set by law or by a clear, specific delegation of authority.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"The Highway Act sets the purpose, the payers and the maximum rate, and clearly delegates the collection method and distribution to the authorities, so the delegation is sufficiently clear.","cites":["3","5"]},{"text":"Charging vehicle owners and estimating fuel use from engine displacement, mileage and efficiency stays within the Act's delegation, because the fee funds highway needs and need not track actual fuel use, given collection cost and technical choices.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Charging vehicle owners is not arbitrary: it serves a major public interest, owners benefit from the highways, and the money is used for road upkeep. Using one rate for all gasoline grades is reasonable too.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The calculation method is reasonably related to the purpose: larger engines tend to burn more fuel and may burden roads more, commercial vehicles use more, and the lower diesel rate rests on transport and industrial policy. So it is proportionate.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The vehicle license tax serves general government revenue while the fuel fee funds road upkeep, so their nature and purpose differ and there is no double taxation.","cites":["9"]}],"who":["Vehicle owners","Drivers of gasoline and diesel vehicles","Highway and transport authorities"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是選民能否因國民大會代表與立法委員的言論及表決不當而罷免他們。大法官認為，言論及表決免責權只是免除刑事、民事及行政責任，並不排除政治責任，所以經國內選舉區選出者，原選舉區選舉人可以依法罷免。","held":"國民大會代表及立法委員經國內選舉區選出者，其原選舉區選舉人得以其言論及表決不當為理由依法罷免，不受憲法第三十二條及第七十三條限制。","points":[{"text":"憲法第三十二條、第七十三條的免責權，是讓代表和委員能暢所欲言、表達民意而無所瞻顧。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"免責權的範圍是不受刑事訴追、不負民事賠償責任，除違反內部自律規則而受懲戒外也不負行政責任，即對外不負法律上責任。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"憲法第一百三十三條規定被選舉人得由原選舉區依法罷免，是基於直接民權理念所設的制度。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"代表和委員行使職權的言論及表決，應對原選舉區選舉人負政治上責任，選舉人可就其言行操守、議事態度、表決立場監督檢驗，所以提議罷免的理由無須限制。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"全國不分區及僑居國外國民選出者因無原選舉區，不適用罷免規定。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["國民大會代表","立法委員","原選舉區選舉人","全國不分區及僑選當選人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭議在於行政院的函令未把公教人員眷屬喪葬補助費列入退休金，也不准退休人員請領，是否違憲。大法官認為退休金的月薪額本來就不包括這項補助費，而相關津貼要點只適用於現職人員，因此行政院函及要點都沒有違反憲法。","held":"行政院未將眷屬喪葬補助費列入退休金範圍的函，以及退休人員不得請領該補助費的生活津貼支給要點，均與憲法無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"學校教職員退休條例所稱月薪額，依該條例第八條包括實領本薪及其他現金給與，但眷屬喪葬補助費並非按月給付，而是特定事故發生時才能支領，性質上無從納入。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"因此行政院六十九年函未把此項補助費列入退休金範圍，與退休條例的立法意旨無違。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"中央公教人員生活津貼支給要點是為安定公教人員生活而訂定，屬主管機關依職權所作的裁量措施。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"該要點第四點明定以各機關學校預算員額內的現職人員為適用對象，退休人員自然不能請領眷屬喪葬補助費。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"主管機關為照顧退休人員生活，可衡量國家財力及津貼性質，在法定退休給與之外酌予補助，屬行政權裁量範圍，並非所有津貼都要比照現職人員。","cites":["3"]}],"who":["退休教職員與公教人員","現職公教人員","主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是行政院決議停止興建核能第四電廠並停止執行相關預算，與立法院發生適用憲法的爭議。大法官認為停止執行法定預算不一定違憲，但此案屬國家重要政策的變更，行政院未向立法院報告並備質詢，程序有瑕疵，須儘速補行報告。至於核能與其他能源孰優，則屬能源政策的專業判斷，不在解釋範圍。","held":"停止執行法定預算是否違憲違法，要分情況而定；若涉及國家重要政策變更，行政院院長或有關部會首長應向立法院報告並備質詢。本件核四停建屬重要政策變更，行政院須儘速補行報告程序，立法院有聽取之義務。","points":[{"text":"法定預算形式上與法律相當，但內容與審議方式不同，屬對國家機關的授權規範；停止執行是否違憲違法，要分情形而定。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"若非重要政策變更且符合預算法要件，主管機關可依合義務裁量裁減經費或變動執行；但維持機關正常運作的經費若停止執行而影響機關存續，則不被允許。","cites":["2","4","5"]},{"text":"行政機關不能任意不執行預算；憲法增修條文設有預算案覆議程序，行政院若認預算窒礙難行，應在預算公布前循覆議處理。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"核四預算涉及儲備能源、環境生態、產業關連及善後複雜性，屬國家重要政策變更，立法院也應有參與或決議的機會。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"重要政策變更須依憲法增修條文第三條及立法院職權行使法第十七條，向立法院報告並備質詢；本件未依此程序處理，有瑕疵，立法院杯葛也非正常處置。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"報告後若獲多數立法委員支持即可貫徹；若立法院反對，則由各有關機關協商或循憲法現有機制選擇適當途徑，究採何途徑非大法官所能代為決定。","cites":["2","8"]}],"who":["行政院及相關部會首長","立法院及立法委員","執行法定預算的行政機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Point 4 of the Shimen Irrigation Association's rules on using its irrigation reservoirs was unconstitutional. That point decides who is charged fees for using surplus water. The court held that it is not unconstitutional.","held":"Point 4 of the Shimen Irrigation Association's reservoir-use rules does not violate the constitutional protection of property rights, the principle that restrictions on rights need a legal basis, or the proportionality principle.","points":[{"text":"Irrigation associations are public-law bodies with local self-government powers within what the law authorizes. They may make their own rules to carry out their tasks, but rules limiting people's rights need a legal basis or authorization, and must follow majority rule, proportionality and due process.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Managing surplus water is one of the associations' self-governing matters. The law gives them power to collect fees, including surplus-water fees, so they may make reasonable and necessary rules for this, whether or not the user is a member.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The law left the standards and procedures for fees to the provincial authorities. Those authorities set only a minimum rate and procedures for collection, and did not say who is charged or how much. An association may fill those gaps with its own rules reported to the authority for record, which fits the law's intent.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Point 4 sets out who is charged in different situations of surplus-water use. This serves effective water use and the user-pays idea, and the means are reasonable and necessary.","cites":["2","6"]},{"text":"The rules were passed by the association's council and recorded by the provincial water authority, so due process was met. They stay within the higher rules and do not conflict with the law or its authorization.","cites":["6"]}],"who":["Irrigation associations","Users of surplus water or reservoirs","Reservoir landowners and co-owners","Tenants and occupiers of reservoirs"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case challenged two provisions of the Detention Act (羈押法): one allowing jail staff to monitor and record meetings between detained defendants and their lawyers, and one allowing what was obtained to be used as evidence. The court held that blanket monitoring and recording of those meetings, and use of the results as evidence of the crime, violate the constitutional right to litigation. It also found one provision of the detention-house organization rules not to be a monitoring authorization, and rejected the applicant's request for a provisional measure.","held":"Article 23(3) of the Detention Act, to the extent it allows monitoring and recording of lawyer meetings regardless of need, and Article 28, to the extent it allows the results to be used as evidence of the charged crime, are unconstitutional and lose effect from 1 May 1998 (ROC year 98). The detention-house organization rule is an internal administrative supervision provision, not a monitoring authorization, so it raises no constitutional question, and the request for a provisional measure is dismissed.","points":[{"text":"The constitutional right to litigation gives criminal defendants a full right of defense, including free, uninterfered communication with their defense lawyer. This may be limited by law only if the limit meets the proportionality principle and is specific and clear.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"Detained defendants keep the same constitutional rights as others apart from those limited by detention, and since they are cut off from the outside, meetings with their lawyer are the only way to exercise their defense. Monitoring there includes listening and recording, and allowing it regardless of need for the detention purpose or house order goes beyond what is necessary. Merely watching without listening is still acceptable.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"Article 28 lets information from monitored lawyer meetings be used as evidence of the charged crime, which harms the defense right to that extent. The invalidity starts on 1 May 1998 to balance the right to litigation with time for authorities to adjust. Any restriction on lawyer-client communication should be decided by a court, with judicial remedies and clear rules.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The detention-house organization rule only describes courts' and prosecutors' supervisory and directing role over detention. It is internal administrative supervision, not authority to monitor or record.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The applicant had been released on bail and the request for a provisional measure did not meet earlier interpretations' standards, so it lacked the required protection of rights and was dismissed.","cites":["9"]}],"who":["Detained criminal defendants","Defense lawyers","Detention house staff","Prosecutors and courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an owner who has already given someone a dian right (a right to pay a price and occupy and use a property) over a property may also create a mortgage on it for another person. The court decided that the owner may, as long as the mortgage does not harm the dian right. It also said its earlier Interpretation No. 192 does not need to be changed.","held":"After setting up a dian right on a property, the owner may still create a mortgage on it for another person, provided this does not interfere with the dian right. Yuan Interpretation No. 192 stays unchanged.","points":[{"text":"A dian right means paying a price and occupying another's property to use it and take its benefits, while a mortgage does not transfer possession and only secures a debt, so the two are not incompatible in nature.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"After creating a dian right the owner has not lost ownership, so within the limit of not harming the dian right the owner can still create a mortgage with someone else.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The property part of the Civil Code has no rule forbidding this, so it cannot be seen as impermissible.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Owners of real property with a dian right","Holders of a dian right","Mortgage holders on such property"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case concerned a rule in Taiwan's civil servant discipline law that gave disciplined officials 30 days, counted from the day a related criminal judgment became final, to ask for a rehearing. The court held that, for some officials who cannot know when that judgment became final, counting from that day breaches the constitutional guarantees of equality and the right to sue. For them the time limit must run from the day they learn the judgment is final.","held":"The rule setting the start of the rehearing deadline is unconstitutional insofar as it counts from the judgment's final date for officials who could not know that date, and it no longer applies to them; their deadline runs from when they learn of it. Interpretation No. 446 is supplemented accordingly.","points":[{"text":"The right to sue under Article 16 must be carried out through laws that follow fair legal procedure and the equality guarantee of Article 7, and disciplinary rehearings affect the right to hold public office greatly.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The rehearing system lets disciplined officials seek a new hearing when a related final criminal judgment found facts different from the original decision, and the deadline exists to keep the law stable.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Where the official is a defendant who can appeal and the other side withdraws an appeal, the official is notified and can calculate the date, so counting from finality is not a problem.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"In other situations (the other side simply does not appeal, the official cannot appeal an acquittal, or the official is not a defendant), no rule requires anyone to notify the official, so they may not know when the judgment became final, and missing the fixed deadline loses the right.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Using the same start date for everyone, regardless of litigation position or knowledge, treats different situations alike without good reason and violates the equality principle.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Civil and administrative procedure laws already let retrial deadlines run from when the party learns of the ground, which shows that differing start dates are a reasonable treatment.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Disciplined civil servants seeking rehearing","Officials not defendants in the related criminal case","Civil Service Discipline Commission","Petitioners whose rehearing requests were rejected"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論的是，國家遭遇重大變故、夫妻被迫分隔且相聚無期時所發生的重婚，後婚姻能否被撤銷。大法官認為，民法關於禁止重婚及可請求撤銷的規定本身合憲；但若後婚姻已有長期實際共同生活，仍適用撤銷規定，就與憲法第二十二條保障人民自由及權利的規定相牴觸。","held":"修正前民法第九百八十五條與第九百九十二條為維持一夫一妻制度所必要，與憲法無牴觸；但對於國家遭重大變故、夫妻隔離下且有長期實際共同生活的後婚姻仍予撤銷，與憲法第二十二條有所牴觸。","points":[{"text":"禁止重婚及許可撤銷的規定，目的在建立一夫一妻的善良婚姻制度。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"撤銷權不設除斥期間，使撤銷權人隨時可行使，這是維持一夫一妻社會秩序所必要，與憲法無牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"修正前民法未規定重婚無效，因此重婚未經撤銷時，後婚姻仍屬有效。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"國家遭重大變故、夫妻隔離相聚無期，甚至音訊全無下的重婚，有不得已的因素，與一般重婚不同。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"對有長期實際共同生活的後婚姻仍予撤銷，會使人民不能享有正常婚姻生活，嚴重影響後婚姻當事人及親屬的家庭生活與人倫關係，反而妨害社會秩序，因此牴觸憲法第二十二條。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["重大變故下夫妻隔離後再婚的人","有長期實際共同生活的後婚姻當事人及其親屬","請求撤銷重婚的利害關係人","聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論公務人員退休後，依法令請領福利互助金若發生爭執，可以走什麼救濟程序。大法官認為這是公法上財產請求權的行使，權利受損時可以提起訴願或行政訴訟。","held":"公務人員公法上財產請求權受損害時，得依訴願或行政訴訟程序請求救濟；退休請領福利互助金發生爭執，也應依此辦理。釋字第一八七號、第二０一號及第二六六號解釋應予補充。","points":[{"text":"人民財產權受憲法第十五條保障，不因成為公務人員而受影響；無論來自公法或私法關係，國家都應保障，受損時應有法律救濟途徑，才符合憲法第八十三條保障公務人員的意旨。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"中央公教人員福利互助辦法等相關規定，是各機關為安定公務人員生活而實施，並有公款補助，具有公法性質。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"現行制度區分民事訴訟與行政爭訟，公務人員退休請領福利互助金屬公法上財產請求權，被機關拒絕會影響財產權，故應許其提起訴願或行政訴訟。","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"行政法院五十三年判字第二二九號判例前段不問處分內容一律不許訴願，與上述意旨不符，不再援用。","cites":["4"]}],"who":["退休公務人員","公務人員","辦理福利互助的機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether it is unconstitutional to punish reserve soldiers who move without reporting it, and to punish more heavily when the move means a call-up order cannot be delivered. The court found these rules do not violate the Constitution. It said the reporting duty does not restrict freedom of residence and that the punishments are within the legislature's lawmaking discretion.","held":"The criminal penalty for reserve soldiers who move without a valid reason and fail to report it does not violate Article 10 of the Constitution. The heavier punishment when a call-up order cannot be delivered, which treats the act as intent to avoid call-up, does not violate Article 23 either. Rules on fault (責任要件) still apply.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution sets a duty to serve in the military but does not say how conscription and call-ups work, so the legislature decides by law, weighing national security and social development, including the penalties for breaching the duty.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Whether to punish a breach of administrative duties with an administrative fine or a criminal penalty is for the legislature to decide, and it is not unconstitutional unless it exceeds proportionality. A different law using a fine for a different purpose does not bar criminal penalties elsewhere.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Reserve soldiers living somewhere other than their registered address affects public interests under the military service laws, so the legislature could use a criminal penalty to control reservist movements and keep the call-up system working. Courts can still set a suitable sentence within the legal range, so the law is not excessively harsh and fits proportionality.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Failing to report a move that leads to undeliverable call-up orders has already harmed call-ups and seriously affected national security, so treating it as intent to avoid call-up is within the legislature's discretion.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"The reporting rule only requires reservists to notify authorities of a move so orders can be delivered, and it does not limit freedom to choose or change residence.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Treating undeliverable orders as intent to avoid call-up does not remove the requirement of fault, which still applies.","cites":["2","4"]}],"who":["Reserve soldiers (後備軍人)","Legislature","Courts sentencing these cases"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Civil Service letter was unconstitutional for refusing retirement compensation for service before the Council for Economic Planning and Development was restructured in 1985. The Court decided the letter was not unconstitutional. Only service from the restructuring until June 30, 1995 qualifies for compensation under the 1995 measures.","held":"The Court held that the Ministry's letter, which pays compensation only for service from the January 9, 1985 restructuring through June 30, 1995 and not for earlier service, fits the purpose of the compensation measures and does not conflict with the constitutional protection of property rights.","points":[{"text":"The 1995 compensation measures were a policy-based remedy for ordinary public school and government employees, whose early retirement pay calculations left out 'other cash benefits'.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The Constitution's equality guarantee is substantive, not mechanical, so reasonable differences in treatment are allowed when the nature of the matter differs.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Staff of the Council before restructuring had a different hiring process and pay system from ordinary civil servants, and under a single salary scheme had no 'other cash benefits' component.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Their pre-restructuring service had already been settled through a difference payment, and the retirement pay per base unit was higher than for ordinary civil servants. For overall balance among public employees, the measures therefore do not cover that service.","cites":["4","5"]},{"text":"The Ministry's letter was a necessary supplementary rule issued within its authority to carry out unclear measures, consistent with their original intent and not in conflict with property rights.","cites":["5"]}],"who":["Former staff of the Council for Economic Planning and Development","Ordinary public school and government employees","Ministry of Civil Service"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑勞動基準法第49條第1項原則上禁止雇主使女性勞工在晚上10點到清晨6點工作，只有經工會或勞資會議同意並提供相關設施才例外，是否違反性別平等。憲法法庭認為這項規定對女性形成不利的差別待遇，手段與目的之間欠缺實質關聯，違反憲法第7條保障性別平等的意旨。因此該規定自解釋公布之日起失效。","held":"勞動基準法第49條第1項限制女工夜間工作的規定，違反憲法第7條保障性別平等之意旨，自本解釋公布之日起失其效力。","points":[{"text":"以性別分類造成差別待遇的法規，要採中度標準從嚴審查：目的須為重要公共利益，手段與目的須有實質關聯。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"系爭規定只限制女性夜間工作，且例外還須工會或勞資會議同意，男性則無此限制，是以性別分類對女性形成不利的差別待遇。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"規定的目的是保護女性人身安全、維護身體健康及穩定人口結構等，這些都屬重要公共利益。","cites":["10"]},{"text":"就人身安全而言，國家應採取保護措施，而非禁止女性夜間工作，所以手段與目的顯然欠缺實質關聯。","cites":["11"]},{"text":"就身體健康而言，避免違反生理時鐘是所有勞工的需求，不限女性；以家務負擔為由則是加深性別刻板印象，且雙重負擔不限於女性。","cites":["12"]},{"text":"以工會或勞資會議同意作為解除禁止的條件，未必能取代個別女性勞工的意願，與目的之達成也難謂有實質關聯。","cites":["13","14"]}],"who":["女性勞工","雇主","工會及勞資會議","男性勞工"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是關於非中華民國境內居住的華僑或外國人，依法核准在國內投資並擔任董事、監察人或經理人，其所領股利應否按固定稅率就源扣繳。行政法院的一則判例另加「無配偶居住國內」的條件，大法官認為這是增加法律沒有的限制，違反憲法的租稅法律主義，因此不予適用。","held":"該判例增列「無配偶居住國內」的限制，添加法律所無之規定，違反憲法租稅法律主義，應不予適用。符合條件者其股利依所定稅率就源扣繳，不適用所得稅法結算申報規定。","points":[{"text":"獎勵投資條例及促進產業升級條例的目的是獎勵生產事業、加速經濟發展，就源扣繳是為減輕投資人稅負、提升華僑及外國人投資意願，這些條例是所得稅法的特別法，受獎勵者應適用其減稅規定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"憲法第十九條的租稅法律主義，是指納稅主體、稅目、稅率、納稅方法及減免等都要依法律；判例也不能超出法律增加規定、加重人民稅負。","cites":["4"]},{"text":"獎勵投資條例第十七條只稱「非中華民國境內居住之個人」，並未附加配偶居住條件，符合規定者即適用就源扣繳，這也符合立法本意及特別法優於普通法的原理。","cites":["5","2"]},{"text":"該判例增列無配偶居住國內的情形，添加法律所無之限制，違反租稅法律主義，與本解釋意旨不符，應不予適用。","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"納稅義務人或其配偶是否因在境內有住所或其他情事而不符「非境內居住個人」要件，屬認定事實與適用法律問題，不在本解釋範圍。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"聲請人指民法第一千零零二條違反男女平等的部分，未具體指出如何牴觸憲法，不在受理範圍。","cites":["6"]}],"who":["非境內居住的華僑投資人","外國投資人","投資事業的董事、監察人或經理人","其配偶居住國內的納稅義務人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"37 people sentenced to death asked Taiwan's Constitutional Court to review whether the death penalty provisions for intentional killing offences, and the procedures used in death penalty cases, are constitutional. The court held that the death penalty for these offences is not unconstitutional, but only in the most serious cases and with the strictest procedural safeguards. It struck down a 1999 law making death the only penalty, and it required extra protections such as a lawyer present at questioning, a lawyer and oral hearing at the third trial level, and unanimous judges.","held":"The death penalty as the maximum sentence for these killing offences is allowed only where the crime is among the most serious and the process meets the strictest due process; the 1999 mandatory-death version of Article 348(1) is unconstitutional. The court also ordered new procedural safeguards, barred death sentences or executions for certain defendants with mental impairments, and allowed the applicants to seek case-specific relief; the requests for interim measures were rejected.","points":[{"text":"Life is the most important constitutional right but not absolute, so the death penalty is reviewed under a strict standard, as are its procedures.","cites":["79","80","81","83"]},{"text":"The purpose of just retribution and deterrence is legitimate. Because death is irreversible, it may be used only for the most serious killings, meaning direct, general or alternative intent and a completed killing, with especially grave circumstances.","cites":["86","87","88","89","94","95"]},{"text":"The 1999 version of Article 348(1) made death the only penalty regardless of how serious the case was, which is too harsh and violates the principle of culpability.","cites":["105","106"]},{"text":"To avoid wrongful convictions, suspects need a lawyer present during questioning, and the third trial level needs mandatory defence counsel and an oral hearing before a death sentence.","cites":["111","113","120","123"]},{"text":"A death sentence must be decided unanimously by the panel of judges, to ensure no reasonable doubt about the aggravating factors.","cites":["129","131"]},{"text":"Defendants whose ability to tell right from wrong was markedly reduced at the time of the offence, or whose ability to defend themselves at trial is clearly insufficient, may not be sentenced to death. Those who lack capacity to understand the sentence may not be executed.","cites":["138","141","142","147","148"]}],"who":["People facing death penalty charges for intentional killing","The 37 applicants on death row","People with mental impairments or intellectual disabilities","Prosecutors, police and courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及海關緝私條例第四十九條：聲明異議案件若無扣押物或扣押物不足，海關可要求在十四日內繳納二分之一保證金或提供同額擔保，逾期則不受理異議。大法官認為，這項規定使無力繳納或提供擔保的人失去行政救濟機會，對人民訴願及訴訟權利造成不必要的限制，與憲法第十六條意旨牴觸，因此不再適用，並變更釋字第二一一號解釋的相關部分。","held":"海關緝私條例第四十九條關於逾期未繳保證金或未提供擔保即不受理異議的規定，牴觸憲法第十六條，應不再適用；釋字第二一一號解釋相關部分予以變更。","points":[{"text":"憲法第十六條保障人民訴願及訴訟的權利，訴願可讓機關自行矯正違法或不當處分並保障人民權益；依憲法第二十三條，限制此權利須是必要的才可以用法律為之。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"以繳納全部或一定比例的稅款、罰鍰或提供擔保作為提起行政救濟的條件，使無法繳納或提供者喪失救濟，是不必要的限制，這是本院自釋字第二二四號解釋以來的一貫見解。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"第四十九條的目的是讓海關審酌個案，防止有人藉聲明異議拖延或逃避執行。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"但同條例第四十九條之一允許海關在處分書送達後免提擔保就聲請假扣押或假處分，原處分的執行已可確保。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"此外，法律沒有讓受處分人聲請暫免繳納或暫免提供擔保的救助規定，會使無力繳納或提供擔保者喪失行政救濟機會，所以該限制顯為不必要。","cites":["3","2"]}],"who":["聲明異議人","無力繳納保證金或提供擔保者","受海關處分之人","海關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及公開發行公司的全體董事或監察人未在期限內補足法定持股成數時，主管機關以施行規則規定要處罰全體董事或監察人，並規定法人當選者要處罰其負責人或代表人。大法官認為，處罰對象與多數人違規時的歸責方式涉及人民權利限制，必須有法律或法律明確授權，但本案規則並無此依據，因此與憲法第二十三條的法律保留原則不符。相關規定須在解釋公布後六個月內失效。","held":"實施規則第八條第一項及第二項後段，因無法律依據或法律具體明確授權，與憲法第二十三條法律保留原則尚有未符，應於解釋公布之日起六個月內失其效力。","points":[{"text":"處罰人民違反行政法上義務，其構成要件與效果應以法律定之；以命令規定的，須有法律明確授權，才符合法律保留原則。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"處罰對象的規定也涉及人民權利限制，除有法律或法律具體明確授權的法規命令外，不得逕以行政命令訂定；多數人違反同一義務時，若要採取不同於按情節輕重分別處罰的歸責方式，也要另以法律或明確授權的命令規定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"證券交易法第二十六條第二項只授權主管機關訂定股權成數及查核實施規則，並未授權就處罰對象或多數人共同違反義務時的歸責方式作特別規定，故實施規則第八條第一項及第二項後段已逾越授權範圍。","cites":["4","6"]},{"text":"證券交易法第一百七十八條第一項第四款只規定違反行為的態樣及法律效果，未就歸責方式或處罰對象特別規定，也沒有授權主管機關補充規定。","cites":["4","6"]},{"text":"實施規則第八條規定「處罰全體」及處罰法人代表人，屬歸責方式與處罰對象的規定，卻無法律依據，因此與法律保留原則不符。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"補足股份成數是不具裁罰性的行政法上義務，受罰後仍須履行，並不違反一事不二罰原則；至於個別負責、平均分擔或處罰法人或代表人，應以法律或法律明確授權的命令在合理且必要範圍內詳訂。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["公開發行公司的董事","公開發行公司的監察人","以法人身分或法人代表人當選的董事、監察人","證券交易法主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑肅清煙毒條例與毒品危害防制條例中，對製造、運輸、販賣第一級毒品者處死刑或無期徒刑的規定，是否違憲。大法官認為這些規定是為肅清毒害、維護國家安全與社會秩序所必要，不違反憲法第二十三條，也不牴觸憲法第十五條。另外，關於意圖販賣而持有毒品罪的條文及「販賣」一詞的實務見解，則不予受理。","held":"製造、運輸、販賣毒品的死刑、無期徒刑法定刑規定，無違憲法第二十三條，與憲法第十五條亦無牴觸；意圖販賣而持有毒品罪條文及「販賣」實務見解部分不予受理。","points":[{"text":"國家以特別刑法規定特別罪刑，只要目的正當、手段必要、限制妥當，就符合比例原則，不能僅因涉及生命、身體自由，就拿普通刑法相比而認定違憲。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"立法目的在肅清煙毒、防制毒品危害，維護國民身心健康、社會秩序與國家安全，並著重截堵毒品來源。","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"毒品為害已久，不只傷害個人與家庭，更是社會國家的大害，因此須嚴加規範並從源頭治理。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"製造、運輸、販賣是毒害的源頭，波及多數人與社會國家法益，不能只和侵害個人法益的殺人罪相比。","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"這些行為利潤極高，若只靠長期自由刑，成效難期，也有悖於公平與正義。","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"持有毒品罪條文未在起訴事實中，聲請人也未說明其為應適用的法律；「販賣」的解釋屬見解問題，不符釋字第三七一號意旨，故不受理。","cites":["7"]}],"who":["製造、運輸、販賣毒品者","一般國民與社會","聲請釋憲人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案涉及兩個問題：行政機關以通知書通知人民應繳罰款，是否屬於可以聲明不服的行政處分；以及交通工具排放空氣污染物罰鍰標準以到案時間提高罰鍰、逾期倍增，是否合憲。大法官認為，通知書若直接影響人民權利義務且已對外發生效力，就是行政處分，不能因仍有後續處分或載明不得訴願而否定；罰鍰標準中以到案時間倍增罰鍰的規定，與母法授權目的不符，也違反法律保留原則。","held":"以通知書名義作成、直接影響人民權利義務並已對外生效者，屬行政處分，不因有後續處分或載明不得訴願而改變；行政法院四十八年判字第九六號判例與憲法尚無牴觸。罰鍰標準第五條與本解釋意旨不符的部分，自公布之日起至遲六個月失其效力。","points":[{"text":"行政處分的認定不看用語、形式，也不看是否有後續行為或載明不得聲明不服，而是看行政機關是否就特定具體公法事件對外發生法律效果。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"通知書若載明應繳罰款數額、繳納方式、逾期倍增，直接影響人民權利義務且已生效，卻以仍有後續處分或載明不得訴願而視為非行政處分，不符憲法保障人民訴願及訴訟權利的意旨。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"行政法院四十八年判字第九六號判例只是對訴願法及行政訴訟法相關規定的詮釋，與憲法尚無牴觸。","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"法律既規定罰鍰額度又授權訂定裁罰標準，目的在尊重行政機關專業判斷，依違規情節訂定合目的性的標準，避免個案裁決恣意。","cites":["5"]},{"text":"罰鍰標準第五條只以到案時間及到案與否作為罰鍰下限的唯一依據，並非依違規事實情節，與母法授權目的未盡相符，且損及主管機關裁量權的行使，即使上限未超過法律額度亦同。","cites":["3","5"]},{"text":"罰鍰倍增即使有促使自動繳納、避免強制執行困擾的考量，但母法既無規定也未授權，標準創設十日內到案及逾期倍增的規定，違反法律保留原則。","cites":["3","5"]}],"who":["接獲行政機關通知書的人民","受交通工具排放空氣污染物罰鍰處罰的相對人","行政機關及中央主管機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked which court, administrative or ordinary, should handle a government request to take back public housing and enforce that order under the National Housing Act. The court decided it is a civil matter for the ordinary courts, so a civil division cannot reject the request just because administrative courts now exist.","held":"Contracts of sale, lease or loan made by the housing authority are private-law relations, so taking back housing under Article 21(1) is a civil matter for the ordinary courts. An administrative court that lacks jurisdiction must dismiss the case and transfer it to the ordinary court, which must resume hearing it.","points":[{"text":"The state may pursue its tasks through public-law or private-law acts. Disputes go to administrative courts if public-law and to ordinary courts if private-law, though the legislature may set a different arrangement, which then binds all organs and courts.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Apart from privately built housing, the authority approves an applicant and then signs a sale, lease or loan contract. These are private-economy measures for social welfare with no power-subordination relationship, so they are not an exercise of public power.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"The provision letting the authority take back housing and seek court enforcement gives enforceability to specific breaches of contract. It concerns private rights, so the court named is the ordinary court.","cites":["3","7"]},{"text":"Earlier cases that were really public-law matters went through civil litigation only because administrative litigation lacked suitable procedures, but this housing matter is private-law and so differs.","cites":["7"]},{"text":"The court's finding on jurisdiction in this case is treated as settled and binds all courts. An earlier ordinary-court dismissal for lack of jurisdiction was a flawed decision and has no binding force.","cites":["8"]},{"text":"The administrative court must dismiss and transfer the case, and the receiving court must restore it and hear it, in order to protect the constitutional right to sue. The relevant authorities are told to review and design a way to resolve such jurisdiction conflicts.","cites":["4","8"]}],"who":["Buyers, tenants and borrowers of public housing","Housing authorities","Ordinary courts","Administrative courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案起因於未辦理繼承登記的土地，經列冊管理期滿後由國有財產署公開標售，合法使用人主張有優先購買權而向法院起訴確認。基隆地院認為屬公法爭議而移送行政法院，行政法院則認為是私權爭議，兩院見解不同，因此聲請統一解釋。憲法法庭認定這類訴訟屬私法關係所生的爭議，應由普通法院審判。","held":"未辦理繼承登記土地或建築改良物的合法使用人，就其使用範圍，對國有財產署或所屬分支機構的公開標售行使優先購買權，而訴請確認優先購買權存在的事件，屬私法爭議，應由普通法院審判。","points":[{"text":"我國採二元訴訟制度，法律沒有規定時，依爭議性質並考量既有訴訟制度功能決定：私法爭議原則上由普通法院審判，公法爭議原則上由行政法院審判。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"土地法第73條之1第3項前段只規定合法使用人有優先購買權，並未規定爭議由哪種法院審判，因此應依爭議性質決定審判權。","cites":["7","8"]},{"text":"判斷是否為合法使用人，要審究其有無使用的正當權源，例如物權法上的占有權源或租賃、借貸關係，涉及的是私法法律關係是否存在。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"優先購買權成立的效果，只是確認主張者能否取代得標人成為買賣契約的買受人，與公權力的行使無涉，所以確認優先購買權存在之訴屬私法爭議。","cites":["9","10"]}],"who":["未辦理繼承登記土地或建築改良物的合法使用人","財政部國有財產署及所屬分支機構","標售的得標人","未辦理繼承登記土地的繼承人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"Three people were convicted of selling drugs after earlier naming their drug supplier. The supplier was caught only after their convictions became final. They asked for a retrial under Code of Criminal Procedure Article 420(1)(6), which allows a retrial when new evidence shows the person should have received an exemption from punishment. Courts rejected them because the law they relied on says punishment is to be reduced or waived, not simply waived. The Constitutional Court ruled that the retrial rule must cover laws that say punishment is 'reduced or waived' as well as laws that say it is 'waived'.","held":"The phrase 'should receive... exemption from punishment' in Article 420(1)(6) must cover laws providing for 'reduced or waived' punishment as well as laws providing for 'waived' punishment, or it violates the equal protection guaranteed by Article 7 of the Constitution. The petitioners may apply for a retrial in their own cases within 30 days of the judgment being delivered to them.","points":[{"text":"Under the wording, 'should receive exemption from punishment' means exemption the law requires. Laws saying 'reduced or waived' mean a court could objectively be required to waive punishment, as can laws saying 'waived'.","cites":["22","26"]},{"text":"The purpose of retrial is to find the truth and achieve justice, not to favor legal finality. Acquittal, dismissal and exemption from punishment are grouped together because each permanently bars the state from punishing, so justice outweighs finality. This also holds where a court could waive punishment under a 'reduced or waived' law.","cites":["28"]},{"text":"The 2015 amendment removed the word 'certain' from 'certain new evidence' to lower the threshold for a retrial and avoid wrongful imprisonment. People under 'reduced or waived' laws have the same need for effective relief.","cites":["30"]},{"text":"The retrial-opening stage only asks whether new evidence raises reasonable doubt and could lead to exemption from punishment. It does not decide whether exemption will actually be given, so people under 'reduced or waived' laws should also be able to reach a retrial.","cites":["32"]},{"text":"Because laws of both kinds let courts objectively order exemption, they are alike and must be treated alike under the equal protection guarantee of Article 7, absent a justification.","cites":["20","33"]}],"who":["People convicted whose law provides 'reduced or waived' punishment","The three petitioners in drug cases","Courts hearing retrial requests"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance directive was unconstitutional. The directive treats only half of the compensation paid to a tenant farmer, when the government expropriates rented farmland, as that year's income, and leaves the other half untaxed. The court held that the directive does not violate the Constitution.","held":"The directive counting half of a tenant farmer's expropriation compensation as income for the year, with the other half tax-free, is consistent with the income tax law and does not conflict with Constitution Articles 15, 19 and 23. It also does not violate the equal-treatment principle in Article 7 by being treated differently from the 1977 directive on crop compensation in land sales.","points":[{"text":"Compensation a tenant farmer receives when the lease ends under the law counts as income from Taiwan sources and is not tax-exempt. It is therefore taxable as 'other income' under the income tax law.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The compensation builds up over many years, and income tax rates rise with income. Taxing it all in one year would increase the tenant's tax burden. Counting only half is allowed for the comparable compensation paid when a landlord takes back land.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"Compensation from expropriation is similar in nature to that landlord-recovery compensation. So the directive's half-income treatment is fair, lightens the tenant's burden and fits the income tax provisions.","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"For these reasons the directive does not conflict with the protection of property (Art. 15), taxation according to law (Art. 19) or the legal-reservation principle (Art. 23).","cites":["4","2"]},{"text":"The other directive, on crop compensation in land sales, deals with a loss compensation, while the expropriation directive deals with other income. Their natures differ, so they cannot be compared and equal treatment is not violated.","cites":["5","2"]}],"who":["Tenant farmers on expropriated rented farmland","Landowners whose rented farmland is expropriated","Taxpayers receiving farm-related compensation"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether the Act on Restoring Rights Damaged During the Martial Law Period was unconstitutional in who it covers and on what conditions. The court found that limiting the Act to insurrection and treason cases was constitutional. It found, however, that Article 6 left out people who suffered equal harm, and that this conflicted with the constitution's equality clause (Article 7).","held":"Limiting the Act to insurrection and treason cases is within the legislature's discretion and does not violate the constitution. Article 6's omission of people detained or not lawfully released outside the stage before an acquittal becomes final violates Article 7, and those people may claim state compensation under Article 6 within two years of the ruling's announcement.","points":[{"text":"Military trials during martial law used different procedures from ordinary criminal cases and gave weaker remedies, so the legislature passed the Act to restore rights or give compensation.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Covering only insurrection and treason was constitutional because these crimes involve political factors, and military courts may have erred in finding facts and applying the law under martial law. Leaving out other criminal cases is within legislative discretion.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Article 6 covered only people detained or punished before a final acquittal. It left out people held or not lawfully released at other stages, such as around a decision not to prosecute, release for insufficient suspicion, after an acquittal, or after a sentence was completed. They suffered equal harm, and nothing in the nature of things justified treating them differently, so this was a serious legislative defect.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"Applying Article 6 as written would compensate only those detained before a final acquittal. This would create legal inequality and conflict with Article 7 of the constitution.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"So those omitted people may claim state compensation under Article 6, in the same way as the covered group, where their detention or punishment is well founded.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"The two-year claim period normally runs from the Act's promulgation date, which raises no constitutional problem. For claims made under this ruling, the two years run from the ruling's announcement.","cites":["7"]}],"who":["People tried by military courts during martial law for insurrection or treason","People detained or not lawfully released outside the period before a final acquittal","People convicted of other crimes, who are not covered by the Act"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案是質疑《公職人員利益衝突迴避法》禁止公職人員及其關係人與其服務或監督的機關交易，違者處交易金額一至三倍罰鍰，是否違憲。憲法法庭認為禁止交易的規定尚未違憲，但罰鍰規定在可能造成顯然過苛處罰時，沒有設適當的調整機制，因而違憲。該罰鍰規定至遲於解釋公布一年後失效。","held":"第九條禁止交易的規定尚未違反比例原則，也不違背工作權、財產權及契約自由；第十五條罰鍰規定因欠缺調整機制而違憲，至遲於公布後屆滿一年失效。另就關係人部分，相關機關應儘速通盤檢討。","points":[{"text":"憲法保障工作權、財產權、營業自由與契約自由，國家限制這些自由須符合比例原則；罰鍰也應責罰相當，並為避免個案過苛而設調整機制。","cites":["4","5"]},{"text":"禁止交易與處罰鍰的目的在防止利益衝突與不當利益輸送，目的正當，手段也有助於達成目的。","cites":["6"]},{"text":"一律禁止交易並以罰鍰確保落實，沒有其他侵害較小而效果相同的手段，因此是必要手段。","cites":["7"]},{"text":"禁止僅及於特定機關，當事人仍可與其他對象交易，限制尚未過當，與公共利益並非顯失均衡。","cites":["8"]},{"text":"對關係人禁止參與交易，若造成少數交易者壟斷而不利公共利益，且機關已有公開公平程序及防弊規制，是否仍有禁止必要，相關機關應儘速檢討。","cites":["9"]},{"text":"罰鍰為交易金額一至三倍，而交易金額常遠高於所得利益，重大工程尤其可能使人無力負擔，立法者卻未設調整機制，處罰逾越必要程度。","cites":["10"]}],"who":["公職人員","公職人員之關係人","公職人員服務或監督的機關","被處罰鍰的違規交易者"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a 1995 Ministry of Civil Service letter was unconstitutional. It ended a rule that let reserve officers who served four years be ranked and paid at an equivalent grade when moving into public jobs. The court held the letter was not unconstitutional, even though having no transition period was open to criticism.","held":"The 1995 letter that stopped applying the ranking preference for reserve officers moving into public service is consistent with the governing statute and does not conflict with the Constitution.","points":[{"text":"Protection of reasonable reliance is a constitutional principle. It covers the repeal or change of administrative rules, not only the withdrawal of benefits granted by individual administrative decisions.","cites":["2","4"]},{"text":"An agency may repeal or change a rule for the public interest. If people who relied on the old rule would lose substantive benefits and no existing remedy applies, the agency should offer reasonable relief or a transition period.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Reliance gets no protection if the rule seriously and obviously violates a higher norm, if it was issued because of improper means or false information, or if it is only a hope or expectation with no concrete sign of reliance.","cites":["2","5"]},{"text":"Protecting the open competitive examination system and the regular civil-service recruitment channel outweighs a special preference for the few officers who served longer. So stopping the rule served the public interest, though the lack of a transition period was open to criticism.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The 1987 letter could serve as a basis for reliance. But it was a stopgap for recruiting soldiers and did not match the statute, so no one could expect it to last forever.","cites":["3","6"]},{"text":"Reliance needs concrete conduct, such as taking the exam or qualifying to apply for ranking. The petitioner had not passed the exam or obtained qualification when the rule stopped, having passed only in 1997, so he could not claim reliance protection.","cites":["3","6"]}],"who":["Reserve officers who served four years of active duty","Applicants for public-service exams and ranking","The Ministry of Civil Service and rule-making agencies"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an administrative agency may directly seize and enforce against the property of someone who refuses to pay a fine it imposed. The court decided that it may not. Fines must be sent to a court for enforcement as the law provides.","held":"After the Compulsory Enforcement Act took effect, only courts may carry out compulsory enforcement. Administrative fines may not be enforced directly against a refusing person's property unless the matter is transferred to a court as the law provides, and the earlier Yuan Interpretation No. 3308 still applies.","points":[{"text":"Since the Compulsory Enforcement Act took effect, compulsory enforcement can be carried out only by a court.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"So an administrative agency cannot directly enforce against the property of someone who refuses to pay a fine; the fine must be transferred to a court as the law provides.","cites":["2"]},{"text":"The earlier Yuan Interpretation No. 3308 remains applicable.","cites":["2"]}],"who":["Administrative agencies that impose fines","People who refuse to pay fines","Courts handling enforcement"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The Legislative Yuan passed a resolution asking the Executive Yuan to pay civil servants and teachers an extra half month of year-end bonus this year, with the budget to be added later. The court decided this was a proposal to increase spending on a budget the Executive Yuan had submitted, which Article 70 of the Constitution forbids. The resolution therefore has no effect.","held":"The Legislative Yuan's resolution asking for an extra half month of year-end bonus, with the budget added later, conflicts with Article 70 of the Constitution and has no effect.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution has the Executive Yuan propose the budget and the Legislative Yuan vote on it, which separates the power to propose from the power to decide.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"This split lets the Executive Yuan take the nation's finances, economy and yearly policy needs into account when drafting the budget, while the Legislative Yuan, representing the people, checks it to keep spending reasonable and avoid waste.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"To carry out this purpose, Article 70 bars the Legislative Yuan from proposing increases in spending on the Executive Yuan's budget, in order to stop the government budget from growing and adding to people's burden.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The resolution asking for an extra half month of bonus, with the budget added later, was a proposal to increase spending on the budget.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"It made no difference that the resolution was made as a proposal by members; in substance it still conflicts with the Constitution and so has no effect.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Legislative Yuan","Executive Yuan","Civil servants and teachers","Taxpayers"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked how school staff who were hired without passing a civil service exam should be treated under the Teachers and Educators Appointment Act. The court held that the rule requiring exam passage matches the Constitution, and that staff already hired before the act took effect do not gain the same appointment status as exam passers. They can only keep working at their current school, though the Examination Yuan may still test them to set their qualification.","held":"Article 21 of the act, requiring school staff to pass the relevant exams, is consistent with Constitution Article 85. The clause letting earlier-hired staff follow their old rules does not give non-passers equal qualification; they may only stay at their original school, and the Examination Yuan may still examine them to set their qualification.","points":[{"text":"Constitution Article 85 sets the principle that civil servants are chosen by open, competitive exams and may not be appointed without passing one.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Article 21 of the amended act requires school staff to pass the school administrative staff exam or an equivalent senior or ordinary civil service exam, which fits that principle.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The 1985 version required existing staff to take an exam set by the Examination Yuan, and let those who did not pass stay in their posts until leaving, balancing the exam principle with those staff's existing interests.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The 1990 amendment lets staff hired before the act follow their old rules as an exception, but this does not give non-passers the same qualification as exam passers, so they can only stay at their original school.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Since these staff lack a legally required exam qualification, the Examination Yuan may still hold exams for those willing to take them, to set their qualification.","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["School staff hired before the act without passing an exam","School staff who passed the required exams","The Examination Yuan"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether an administrative court precedent was unconstitutional because it limits retrials based on forged or altered evidence. The Constitutional Court said the precedent is consistent with the constitutional protection of the right to sue. A retrial on this ground requires that the evidence was actually forged or altered, not merely claimed to be.","held":"The Administrative Court's 1987 precedent (76 Pan-Tzu No. 1451) does not conflict with Article 16 of the Constitution. Under it, forgery or alteration must be established by a final guilty judgment, or by a criminal case that cannot start or continue for reasons other than insufficient evidence.","points":[{"text":"Article 16 protects the right to sue, but the legislature decides the procedures and requirements for lawsuits by law, in a proper and reasonable way, according to the nature of the case.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"A retrial for forged or altered evidence requires that the evidence was truly forged or altered, not just that the party who wants a retrial says so.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Forgery or alteration counts as proven only if a guilty judgment is final, or the criminal case cannot start or continue for reasons other than insufficient evidence.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"A retrial is an extraordinary remedy against a final judgment and affects the stability of the legal order, so limits on bringing it are appropriate. The limits keep retrials from being unrestricted and protect the finality of judgments.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"These requirements reflect the legislature's balance between legal stability and the correctness of judgments, so they are not unconstitutional.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The administrative litigation law's retrial grounds were drawn from the civil procedure provision, and the amendment did not intend to remove the requirement of a final guilty judgment. The precedent is therefore consistent with that law and does not conflict with Article 16.","cites":["4"]}],"who":["People seeking a retrial in administrative cases","Parties to final administrative court judgments","Administrative courts"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案爭點是懲治盜匪條例對意圖勒贖而擄人者一律以死刑為法定刑，是否違憲。大法官認為這項規定雖然立法甚嚴，但裁判時仍有減輕其刑的規定可以適用，足以避免過嚴的刑罰，因此與憲法尚無牴觸。","held":"懲治盜匪條例第二條第一項第九款對意圖勒贖而擄人者，不分情況概以死刑為法定刑，因另有減輕其刑的規定可適用，與憲法尚無牴觸。","points":[{"text":"該條例為特別刑法，其規定旨在提高擄人勒贖罪的刑度，以遏阻犯罪、維護治安，使人民免於恐懼。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"該規定不分犯罪情況及結果，一律以死刑為法定刑，立法甚嚴，有導致情法失平之虞，宜在立法上兼顧人民權利及刑事政策妥為檢討。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"依同條例第八條，擄人勒贖案件仍適用刑法總則及刑法第三百四十七條第五項等規定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"裁判時若有情輕法重之情形，可依刑法第五十九條酌量減輕其刑。","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"未經取贖而釋放被害人者，也可減輕其刑，因此足以避免過嚴之刑罰，該規定尚難謂與憲法牴觸。","cites":["2","3"]}],"who":["意圖勒贖而擄人的被告","擄人勒贖案件的被害人","審理此類案件的法院","立法機關"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether Interior Ministry directives letting road authorities abolish non-planned roads (roads not in an urban plan) are unconstitutional. The court decided they are not, because within areas with a legally adopted urban plan, roads follow that plan. Once planned roads are built and open to the public, authorities may abolish a non-planned road that is no longer needed for public passage.","held":"Where an urban plan and its detailed plan have been legally adopted, roads must follow the plan. Once planned roads are open, the authority may abolish a non-planned road no longer needed by the public, and the two Interior Ministry directives on this do not conflict with the constitution's protection of people's rights.","points":[{"text":"Road planning in urban plan areas must follow the procedures in the Urban Planning Law, including a main plan and a detailed plan showing the road system.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"Those plans are reviewed by a planning committee, put on public display where any citizen or group can comment, and then approved and published, so people have a chance to know about and comment on road arrangements.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Once the plan is fixed, it must be carried out, and drawing up the road system through this process already implies abolishing non-planned roads.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"After planned roads are built and open, an authority may abolish a non-planned road with no continuing need for public passage, on its own initiative or on application, which fits the purpose of the Urban Planning Law.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The Interior Ministry's directives and Taipei's application rules match this view, so they do not conflict with the constitution's protection of people's rights.","cites":["2","3"]},{"text":"The court added that abolishing existing alleys subject to public-use easement affects public interest, so clear rules in the urban planning regulations would be preferable.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Road and urban planning authorities","Users of non-planned roads and alleys","Citizens and groups who comment on urban plans","Applicants seeking abolition or rerouting of non-planned alleys"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked how the speech of local council members at meetings should be protected. The court said the Constitution has no rule on this, and that an earlier interpretation (院解字第三七三五號) does not raise a constitutional problem. The ruling does not set out a detailed protection scheme.","held":"The Constitution does not say how local council members' speech at meetings must be protected. The earlier interpretation 院解字第三七三五號 does not raise a constitutional problem.","points":[{"text":"The Constitution has no provision on how local council members' speech at meetings should be protected.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"The earlier interpretation was issued about county councillors who abused their immunity for speech, so it does not raise a constitutional problem.","cites":["3"]},{"text":"Provincial, county and city council members who do not abuse this immunity keep their speech protection unaffected.","cites":["3"]}],"who":["Local council members","Provincial, county and city council members","County councillors who abuse speech immunity"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案聲請人在營利事業所得稅申報中，主張跨年度盈虧互抵時，財政部66年函要求先以虧損年度免計入所得額的投資收益抵減虧損，是違憲的。憲法法庭認為該函沒有違反租稅法律主義，也不生違反平等原則的問題。不過法庭提醒，核定各期虧損的基準，以法律或法律具體明確授權的命令明定為宜。","held":"財政部66年3月9日台財稅第31580號函與憲法第19條租稅法律主義尚無牴觸，也不生違反憲法第7條平等原則的問題；惟核定各期虧損的基準，仍以法律或法律具體明確授權之命令明定為宜。","points":[{"text":"主管機關在職權範圍內闡釋租稅法律，若依一般法律解釋方法且符合憲法原則與立法目的，就不違反租稅法律主義。","cites":["12"]},{"text":"所得稅法第39條第1項但書的「前10年內各期虧損」須先經稽徵機關核定，並非直接等同以前年度申報核認的虧損數，系爭函是為明確核定基準而作的釋示。","cites":["14","15"]},{"text":"系爭函只影響本年度純益額的扣除額如何核定，不會把以前年度投資收益計入本年度所得，且所得稅法第42條的目的並非避免對同一人就同一客體重複課稅；系爭函以實際營業虧損核定，符合正確衡量稅負能力的立法目的。","cites":["18","19","20","21"]},{"text":"在兩稅合一制下，虧損的營利事業須先彌補虧損才能分派股利，獲配的投資收益無法全額分給股東，第42條第1項的功能已減損，故系爭函尚未牴觸其立法意旨。","cites":["23","24"]},{"text":"財政部74年函、76年函所涉的證券交易所得與土地交易所得，各有不同的稅制設計與立法目的，與系爭函是基於不同事物的釋示，不生違反平等原則的問題。","cites":["26","27"]},{"text":"跨年度盈虧互抵制度的政策選擇影響國家財政、經濟與產業發展，並涉及人民租稅負擔，為避免疑義，核定各期虧損的基準以法律或法律具體明確授權之命令明定為宜。","cites":["29"]}],"who":["營利事業（公司組織）","稽徵機關","財政部","聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"本案討論的是公務員在受懲戒處分議決前，曾經被停止職務，之後若被處以休職，期滿後能不能復職。大法官認為，這種情形仍可適用休職期滿復職的規定，不會因為先前曾被停職就被排除。","held":"公務員懲戒法第四條第二項所定休職期滿之復職，不因公務員在懲戒處分議決前曾被停止職務，而排除其適用。","points":[{"text":"第十六條第三項的復職，是恢復懲戒處分議決前被停止的職務；第四條第二項的復職，是休職處分執行後回復被休的職務，兩者性質不同。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"休職期滿許其復職，已由公務員懲戒法第四條第二項明文規定。","cites":["3"]},{"text":"因此凡受休職處分者，不因議決前曾被停止職務，而排除休職期滿復職的適用。","cites":["3","2"]}],"who":["受休職處分的公務員","曾被停止職務的公務員"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"聲請人在審判中被受命法官裁定羈押，辯護人為其利益提出準抗告，卻被屏東地院認為辯護人不得提起而駁回。憲法法庭認為，除非與被告明示意思相反，辯護人可為被告利益聲請撤銷或變更羈押處分，並廢棄原裁定、發回重審。","held":"刑事訴訟法第416條第1項第1款須準用第346條，辯護人除與被告明示意思相反外，得為被告利益聲請撤銷或變更羈押處分，否則違憲；屏東地院112年度聲字第19號裁定違憲，廢棄並發回該院。","points":[{"text":"被告受羈押後與外界隔離，自我辯護能力幾近喪失，且抗告期間短暫，必須倚賴辯護人及時有效協助，這是憲法第8條及第16條所保障的權利。","cites":["18","19"]},{"text":"依先前判決，辯護人在不違反被告明示意思下，已可為被告利益對法院的羈押裁定抗告。","cites":["22"]},{"text":"羈押不論由法院或由審判長、受命法官、受託法官決定，對被告的影響與所需協助並無差別，沒有理由只准抗告而不准聲請撤銷或變更。","cites":["23"]},{"text":"準抗告在效力、處理期間及審查結果上準用抗告規定，救濟功能無實質差異，第419條的「抗告」應解釋為包含準抗告，故準用第346條。","cites":["23"]},{"text":"原裁定認為辯護人不得為被告利益提起準抗告，與上述意旨不符，侵害被告的人身自由與訴訟權，因此廢棄並發回重審。","cites":["24","25"]},{"text":"有3位大法官持續拒絕參與評議，本庭將他們從現有總額中扣除，以免拒絕評議者阻止判決作成。","cites":["12","13"]}],"who":["受羈押的刑事被告","被告的辯護人","審判中裁定羈押的審判長、受命法官、受託法官","本案聲請人"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"A defendant was detained by a trial judge, and the defense lawyer asked the court to cancel or change the detention on the defendant's behalf. The Pingtung court rejected this, saying only the detained person could do so. Taiwan's Constitutional Court ruled that this reading violates the Constitution, so a defense lawyer may make that request unless the defendant has clearly said otherwise.","held":"The rule on challenging detention orders (Code of Criminal Procedure Art. 416(1)(1)) is constitutional only if read to let a defense lawyer, unless the defendant has expressly objected, ask the court to cancel or change a detention order made for the defendant's benefit. The Pingtung court's ruling is unconstitutional, set aside, and sent back to that court for a new hearing.","points":[{"text":"Because three justices refused to take part in deliberation, the court deducted them from the total number of sitting justices, so it could still decide the case.","cites":["10","11","12","13"]},{"text":"The application met the requirements for review, so the court accepted it.","cites":["15"]},{"text":"Constitutional protections of personal liberty and the right to court access include the right of a defendant to timely and effective help from a defense lawyer.","cites":["18"]},{"text":"Detention is the most serious intrusion on personal liberty, and a detained person is cut off from the outside and can hardly defend themselves, so depends on a lawyer.","cites":["19"]},{"text":"A lawyer may already appeal a court's detention ruling for the defendant, and challenging a judge's detention order works in much the same way, so there is no reason to treat them differently.","cites":["22","23"]},{"text":"The Pingtung court's ruling relied on a reading that conflicts with this, so it violated the Constitution and was set aside and sent back.","cites":["25"]}],"who":["Detained criminal defendants","Defense lawyers","Trial judges and courts handling detention","The applicant in the Pingtung case"],"covered":true}

{"answer":"The case asked whether a prison law rule was unconstitutional that released prisoners who had finished their sentence only on the morning of the day after the sentence ended. The court held that this rule kept people detained after their sentence ended without proper legal procedure and went further than necessary, so it violated the Constitution. Until the rules are fixed, prisoners must be released on the morning of the day their sentence ends.","held":"The part of Article 83, paragraph 1 of the Prison Act requiring release on the morning after the sentence ends conflicts with Articles 8 and 23 of the Constitution, and that part loses effect from 1 June 2010. Until the rules are amended, prisoners must be released on the morning of the day their sentence ends; the request for a temporary order was rejected.","points":[{"text":"Under Article 8 of the Constitution, any measure restricting personal liberty needs a legal basis and proper legal procedure, and must also meet Article 23.","cites":["4"]},{"text":"The next-morning release rule began as a practical arrangement because of night-time work and transport difficulties, but the sentence period should be counted so that it ends at the end of its last day, and after that prisoners should be released unless another constitutional legal ground exists.","cites":["5"]},{"text":"The state's power to punish ends when the sentence is served, so holding people longer is like punishment, and the rule set no proper legal procedure for it, violating Article 8.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The aim of protecting prisoners' transport and safety is legitimate, but release in the morning of the final day is possible without those concerns, so the delay is not necessary and breaches proportionality under Article 23.","cites":["6"]},{"text":"The temporary order request was rejected because the ruling itself already decided the case, making such an order unnecessary.","cites":["3","7"]}],"who":["Prisoners finishing their sentences","Prison authorities","Agencies that must revise the release rules"],"covered":true}
